audits.scope: Evaluation metrics and statistical inference infrastructure across gen13 (gen13sep/metrics.py, inference.py, wildcluster.py, scripts/g13_analysis.py, scripts/g13_inference_audit.py, bootstrap/ and metrics/ outputs), gen14 dirbench.Blocked, gen15 (valuebench.py, fewshot.py, results/*contrasts*.csv), gen16_leads (bootstrap.py, claims.py, l3_decision.py, l5 scripts, DECISION_REPORT, PRE_REGISTRATION), gen16_protocol (clusterboot.py, g16_size/g16_bp1/g16_detectability/g16_dir_signflip/g16_oof_amplitude and results/), gen19ct/evaluation (metrics.py, transfer.py, discovery.py, confirmation.py, pairs.py, tests), docs/figures/METRIC_AUDIT.md, LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md sections 6, 8, 9, 10, and legacy src/lanthanide_separation R2 usage. Read-only; no experiment script was run; one read-only python snippet recomputed Kish n_eff from a committed CSV; pytest --collect-only verified 63 tests collect in the three stats/metrics test files.
audits.summary: The programme's deciding metric is extractant-macro MAE on pairwise log SF, implemented in generations/gen13_separation/gen13sep/metrics.py: per (split_seed, extractant) the MAE is pooled over all of that extractant's pairs (cells pooled, line 64-66), then averaged with equal weight per extractant within a seed and then over the 5 seeds (lines 92-98); chemotype-macro averages per-extractant MAE within chemotype, then over chemotypes, then over seeds (line 94); pooled MAE is the plain mean over every pair row of every seed (line 95); sign accuracy on strong pairs uses |y| >= 0.3 with np.sign equality (a zero prediction counts wrong, not 1/2, line 69), macro one vote per (seed, extractant). Inference is gen13sep/inference.py paired_contrasts: per-unit values are averaged over the five seeds before resampling (line 36), chemotypes (45) are drawn with replacement in one shared (10,000 x 45) index matrix with seed 8675309, every member extractant travels with its chemotype, the interval is the percentile 2.5/97.5 plus a BCa interval whose acceleration comes from a jackknife over chemotypes (src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/inference.py:34-66), the two-sided p is 2*min(P(draw<=0), P(draw>=0)) capped at 1, and the five seeds enter only as a separate per-seed sign count. The P1 rule as implemented (inference.py:92,102) is passes_intervals = percentile lower > 0 AND bca_low > 0 AND p < 0.05, then passes_P1 = passes_intervals AND point >= 0.02 AND seeds_positive >= 4 AND leave-one-chemotype-out sign-stable; the upper bound is never checked, so 'exclude 0' is one-sided. No code in gen13/14/15/16 computes any R2 on log SF; gen19ct/evaluation/metrics.py has a hand-written weighted r2_score (NaN when SS_tot = 0, no reason string, no force_finite) used only on the log D target, and legacy src/ modules call sklearn r2_score with its default force_finite=True; none of the plan's six R2 definitions (pooled, balanced with hierarchical weights, pair-macro, adjacent, PrNd, within-system) exists anywhere. The percentile bootstrap's size has been measured twice under simulated nulls on the real cluster membership: 0.071-0.077 at nominal 0.05 on the 45-chemotype profile (gen13 metrics/BP_all/inference_calibration.csv, 3000 sims) and 0.0705-0.0815 on the 40-chemotype/82-extractant profile (gen16_protocol/results/g16_size.log, 2000 sims), while the restricted wild cluster bootstrap-t holds 0.041-0.053 and the CR3/Bell-McCaffrey t 0.041-0.048; both gen13sep/wildcluster.py and gen16_protocol/gen16/clusterboot.py implement WCR, CR0-CR3 SEs, Bell-McCaffrey dof, test-inversion CIs and ROPE posteriors, but gen16_leads' sealed pre-registration and gen19's transfer.py kept the percentile+BCa cluster bootstrap, so WCR was never adopted as the deciding procedure. Benjamini-Hochberg exists in four independent implementations (gen19 transfer.benjamini_hochberg with NaN-counts-toward-m, gen19 confirmation.bh_adjust, gen16 l5_summary.bh, gen16 l4_retro.bh, gen18 evalproto) and is always printed beside the raw p and never decides; registered contrasts are judged on raw p by P1 or R19. Gen19's R19 (transfer.py:584-705) is the successor rule: six items, intervals and p under every registered cluster unit, 4/5 seeds in discovery and 5/5 at confirmation, LOCO must stay strictly > 0, every registered sensitivity positive, with the confirmation statistic being the mean over withheld seeds and a nested bootstrap applying the same resampled clusters to every seed. Effective sample size is Kish (sum n)^2/sum n^2 = 11.67 for 90 extractants in 45 chemotypes (34 singletons, one of size 23; recomputed here), 10.07 for the 82/40 rich-cell cohort, Bell-McCaffrey dof 11.13 (45) and 9.57 (40), CSS G* 1.9-2.6, and a reliability-weighted 34.26 effective chemotypes at ICC 0.72 which gen16_protocol argues is the right count for between-chemotype covariate questions. Measured-mode interval coverage is pooled over scored pairs with Gaussian z and the BLUP posterior sd: nominal 90% covers 0.988 at k=3 under BP (gen16_leads/results/L5/calibration_intervals.csv), and the deployed residual covariance is indefinite on all 430 leave-chemotype-out estimates. For a k-shot study, gen15 fewshot.evaluate already enforces a fixed scoring set (support pairs of the largest budget, union over strategies, excluded at every k) and byte-identical pairs across arms, but no code implements the plan's SHA-256-defined query sets or the arithmetic-closure constraint, no code does publication-grouped resampling on the gen13 pair table, and no code gives a chemotype-blocked CI on an R2 difference; the closest reusable primitive is gen19 transfer.cluster_bootstrap_statistic (any statistic, cluster resampling, jackknife, percentile+BCa+p), which is a per-replicate python loop and will be slow on 70k-row pair tables.

findings.topic: (1a) Extractant-macro MAE: exact definition and code
findings.detail: Atom is the pair table: one row per (split_seed, held-out cell, metal A, metal B) with y = log D(A) - log D(B), A lighter (gen13 orientation), one prediction column per arm. per_extractant() groups by (split_seed, extractant) and computes mae_all = mean |y - pred| over ALL of the extractant's pair rows (its cells pooled, no cell weighting). summarise() then takes, per arm, macro = per_ext.groupby('split_seed')['mae_all'].mean() (equal weight per extractant within a seed) and reports macro.mean() over seeds as macro_mae_extractant and macro.std(ddof=1) as macro_mae_extractant_seed_sd. Adjacent = dZ == 1 or the (Nd, Sm) pair; far = dZ >= 5; macro_mae_adjacent/far use pandas mean which silently drops extractants with no such pairs (n_units_adjacent 83, n_units_far 88 of 90 under BP_all). The pair table carries 14,150 pairs per seed (BP_all context.json).
evidence: generations/gen13_separation/gen13sep/metrics.py:93-99 (macro over extractants within seed, then mean/sd over seeds)

findings.topic: (1b) Chemotype-macro and pooled MAE
findings.detail: macro_mae_chemotype = sub.groupby(['split_seed','chemotype'])['mae_all'].mean() (mean of per-extractant mae_all within each chemotype) .groupby(level=0).mean() (equal weight per chemotype within seed) .mean() (over seeds). pooled_mae = (pairs['y'] - pairs[arm]).abs().mean() over every pair row of every seed, so each held-out cell contributes once per seed it is held out in and large extractants dominate; the module docstring labels pooled numbers 'descriptive only: one chemotype holds 375 of 521 cells'. pooled_sign_acc_strong is the same pooled convention. The contrasts also carry block_macro = mean over chemotypes of the mean per-extractant delta within chemotype (a chemotype-macro of the paired delta).

findings.topic: (1c) Sign accuracy on strong pairs and the heavier-always yardstick
findings.detail: strong = |y| >= STRONG_SIGN_THRESHOLD (0.3). Per (seed, extractant): sign_acc_strong = mean(np.sign(y) == np.sign(pred)) over strong pairs, NaN if none. Because np.sign(0) == 0, a prediction of exactly 0 (FLAT, or a tie) is scored WRONG, not 1/2 — this differs from gen19 pairs.py (|pred| <= 1e-12 counts 1/2) and from the recovery plan section 6.4 ('zero prediction counts 0.5'). Macro: by_seed['sign_acc_strong'].mean().mean(). heavier_always_sign_accuracy() uses hit = (y < 0) because with A lighter, 'heavier preferred' means y < 0; macro = one vote per (seed, extractant) = 0.6298; pooled = 0.8554 (BP_all context.json). B4_HEAVIER_ALWAYS is also run as an arm so the same per-extractant code scores it. HIGHER_IS_BETTER = {sign_acc_strong, pair_spearman, curve_spearman} is negated before any delta so 'positive favours candidate' holds.

findings.topic: (1d) Chemotype-blocked paired bootstrap: resampling unit, replicates, intervals, p, seeds
findings.detail: paired_contrasts(per_ext, comparisons, value='mae_all', replicates=10_000, seed=8675309, margin=0.02). Scoring unit = extractant; _per_unit() averages the value over split seeds per (arm, extractant) BEFORE resampling (line 36), so the bootstrap sees 90 units, not 450. Resampling unit = chemotype: names = sorted chemotypes, members[j] = unit indices of chemotype j, picks = rng.integers(0, G, size=(replicates, G)) — one index matrix shared by every comparison in the call; each replicate concatenates the member arrays of the drawn chemotypes and takes the mean of the finite deltas (delta = reference - candidate per unit; NaN units excluded via counts). Needs >= 2 chemotypes and >= 3 finite units. Percentile interval = np.nanquantile(draws, 0.025/0.975). BCa = gen8 _bca_interval(draws, point, delta, members): z0 = norm.ppf(mean(draws < point)) with the proportion clamped to [1e-6, 1-1e-6] (no mid-rank for ties), acceleration from the jackknife over chemotype blocks (leave one block out, mean of finite deltas), denominator guarded by max(1e-9, .), returns NaN only if < 50 finite draws or < 3 jackknife values. p_two_sided = min(1, 2*min(mean(draws<=0), mean(draws>=0))). bootstrap_se = std(draws, ddof=1); mde_80 = 2.80 * bootstrap_se. Seeds: seeds_positive = number of split seeds whose per-seed per-unit delta mean > 0 (computed from per-seed tables, lines 74-82); n_seeds reported. The same primitive is reimplemented in gen14 dirbench.Blocked (BOOT_REPS 10,000, seed 8675309, percentile only + LOCO) and reused unchanged by gen15 valuebench.contrasts and gen16 claims; gen16 L3 wrote its own 2,000-replicate percentile-only version with task units (disclosed deviation).
evidence: generations/gen16_leads/DECISION_REPORT.md:586-596 (deviation item 10: BCa half of P1 never computed for the confirmed claim)

findings.topic: (1e) Contrast CSV formats
findings.detail: gen13 bootstrap/<label>/paired_contrasts.csv columns: comparison,status,value,reference,candidate,point,ci95_low,ci95_high,bca_low,bca_high,p_two_sided,bootstrap_se,mde_80,block_macro,n_units,units_improved,seeds_positive,n_seeds,loco_min,loco_max,loco_sign_stable,margin,passes_intervals,passes_P1 (status = registered/exploratory inserted by g13_analysis.py). gen15 results/*contrasts*.csv: same columns with a leading 'design' column and no 'status'. gen16 contrasts add 'family' and 'p_bh_lead'. gen13 fewshot_stage2_contrasts.csv adds arm_scored and support_design. gen19 BootstrapResult.record(): contrast,cluster_unit,clustered,decides,point,percentile_low,percentile_high,bca_low,bca_high,p_two_sided,bootstrap_sd,mde_80,bias_z0,acceleration,loco_min,loco_max,n_units,n_clusters,n_resamples,bootstrap_seed,n_nan_draws,higher_is_better, with regime columns in front; gen19 tables/confirmation_claims.csv adds r19_verdict, confirmed, n_seeds_positive, tost_verdict, seed_deltas_by_index.

findings.topic: (2) P1 decision rule as implemented
findings.detail: inference.py:92: passes_intervals = (np.nanquantile(draws, 0.025) > 0) and (bca_low > 0) and (p < 0.05). inference.py:102: passes_P1 = passes_intervals and point >= margin (0.02) and seeds_positive >= MIN_SEEDS_POSITIVE (4) and loco_stable. Only lower bounds are tested, so 'exclude 0' is effectively one-sided in the candidate's favour; a bca_low of NaN makes passes_intervals False. g13_analysis.py:124-126 blanks passes_P1 (None) for every value other than mae_all, so the rule is registered for mae_all only; secondary metrics are reported with intervals. Registered contrast set: P1 M_SELECTED vs C_DIRECT_ROW, S1 vs B1_MEAN_CURVE, S2 vs B3_NN_TANIMOTO, S3 vs B2_PAIRMEAN, S4 vs B4_HEAVIER_ALWAYS (REGISTERED dict). Band contrasts (per similarity band) use max(2000, replicates//5) replicates and are descriptive. Gen16 added the shared rule that a registered contrast must pass P1 in all five designs and keep its sign in all five (l5_summary.py:47-55, PRE_REGISTRATION section 2.1). Outcome: P1 fails under B_primary (-0.0061, p 0.748, 2/5 seeds) and BP_all (-0.0016, p 0.956); S1-S4 pass.

findings.topic: (2b) Gen19 successor rule R19
findings.detail: transfer.r19(): item 1 point >= margin; item 2 percentile lower > 0 AND BCa lower > 0 under EVERY registered cluster unit of the design (V5/V5-P/V5-PAIR: system + publication_group; V6 percentile only, 13 clusters); item 3 two-sided p < 0.05 under every cluster unit; item 4 Delta > 0 in >= 4/5 discovery seeds or 5/5 at confirmation (VACUOUS for deterministic arms); item 5 no leave-one-cluster-out delta <= 0 (strictly positive, stricter than gen13's same-sign); item 6 Delta > 0 in every registered sensitivity (UNTESTABLE -> UNDECIDED). Verdict FAIL if any item fails, UNDECIDED if any untestable, else PASS. The bootstrap must be the registered one (clustered, 10,000 resamples, seed 19) and its point must equal Delta or items 2-3 fail. Discovery ran learned arms on seed 104729 only (item 4 NOT_EVALUATED); at confirmation the statistic is the mean over the 5 withheld seeds of the per-seed delta, with seed_mean_nested_cluster_bootstrap applying the same drawn clusters to every seed, LOCO removing one cluster from all seeds, and item4() requiring exactly 5 scored seeds. TOST: 90% interval (union of percentile and BCa by default) inside (-0.05, 0.05) = NO_DIFFERENCE; lower > -0.05 = non-inferior; else UNDECIDED. Margin delta5 = max(0.05, 0.20*(L5 - N0)), N0 = 0.299*sqrt(2/pi).
evidence: generations/gen19_chem_transfer/gen19ct/evaluation/discovery.py:1982-2037 (discovery contrast; seed 104729 primary), 1868-1878 (bootstraps per cluster unit)

findings.topic: (3) R2: what exists and with what conventions
findings.detail: Nothing in gen13sep/metrics.py, inference.py, gen14 dirbench, gen15 valuebench/fewshot or gen16_leads computes an R2 on pairwise log SF; the gen13 leaderboard has MAE, sign accuracy and Spearman only. gen19ct/evaluation/metrics.py:242-252 r2_score(y, pred, weights=None) is hand-written: weighted mean ybar, 1 - SS_res/SS_tot, returns NaN when y is empty or SS_tot == 0 (never 0/1), no 'reason', no force_finite argument; it is applied in logd_summary() to the log D target under three aggregations (unit_macro with each unit's rows summing to weight 1, row_pooled, system_macro) and is never applied to logSF pairs (pairs.py reports logsf_mae and direction accuracy only). Tests: test_metrics.py:69-76 pins R2 = 0.5 on a hand example, the weighted variant, and NaN for constant y. Legacy src/: evaluation.py:324 and gen3_metrics.py:26,130 call sklearn r2_score(truth, prediction) with the sklearn default force_finite=True (degenerate cases silently become 0.0/1.0); evaluation.py:630 guards with len>=2 and var>0 else NaN; evaluation.py:547-552 and deep_evaluation.py:617-622 compute R2 deltas candidate-reference with a group-balanced sample_weight (a 'balanced' R2 by ligand group, not the plan's hierarchical weights). gen16_protocol: g16_oof_amplitude.py:95-130 computes r2_vs_mean_curve, r2_vs_flat_curve (denominator sum y^2, i.e. FLAT as reference) and r2_affine_recalibrated on the per-cell amplitude of 289 rich cells (BP: 0.117 / 0.386 / 0.161 for G14); variance.py:239-262 Nakagawa-Schielzeth marginal/conditional R2 and a Shapley split; g16_identifiability.py:60 in-sample R2 with saturated indicators; wildcluster.detectable_r2 is a power calculation, not a metric. gen15/exp/condfe/diagnose4.py:37 within_r2 is an exploratory ridge within-group R2 on features, not a prediction R2. force_finite appears nowhere in the repository.

findings.topic: (4a) Bootstrap calibration: measured size of every procedure
findings.detail: gen13 scripts/g13_inference_audit.py calibration(): simulated null d_i = a_g + e_i with ICC 0.72 (and 0.3), normal and scaled-t(3) tails, on the real 45-chemotype size profile, seed 20260909; the committed metrics/BP_all/inference_calibration.csv (3000 sims, mc_se 0.004) gives rejection at nominal 5%: pairs_percentile_OLD 0.071 (ICC 0.72 normal), 0.068 (ICC 0.3), 0.077 (t3), 0.076 (t3, ICC 0.3); iid_t 0.44; cr1_normal 0.106; cr1_tG1 0.099; cr2_tG1 0.078; cr2_bm 0.059; cr3_bm 0.046; wcr_cr2 0.044; wcr_cr3 0.044. gen16_protocol clusterboot.size_study on the 82-extractant/40-chemotype rich-cell membership (2000 sims, 999 reps, seed 20260909+100*icc): percentile 0.0725/0.072/0.0815/0.0705 at ICC 0/0.2/0.4/0.6; WCR (CV1) 0.053/0.049/0.053/0.041; CV1-t 0.064-0.113. The ICC 0.72 row was never written (g16_size.log stops at 0.6; g16_size_study.csv does not exist). Consequences recorded: G14 - FLAT under BP +0.0884 has percentile p 0.0468 but WCR p 0.0593 and WCR CI [-0.0030, +0.1688]; gen14 claim 2 goes from p 0.006 to 0.0233 (WCR) and 0.0989 (CR2-t on BM dof 9.57); claim 1 p_wcr 0.0721.

findings.topic: (4b) Recommended inference and what was actually adopted
findings.detail: gen13sep/wildcluster.py provides cluster_robust (CR0/CR1/CR2/CR3 SEs, Bell-McCaffrey/Satterthwaite dof in closed form for the intercept-only model), wild_cluster_t (WCR, null imposed, Rademacher/Webb/Mammen weights, reps 9999, seed 8675309, se_kind CR2 default, p = (1 + #{|t*| >= |t_obs|})/(reps+1), p_wcu unrestricted variant, CI by grid inversion on 161 points at p >= 0.05, plus analytic p_t_dof and p_normal), bayes_bootstrap (Rubin, estimand unit_macro or cluster_macro, ROPE 0.02, 20,000 Dirichlet draws), random_effects (2-D grid posterior, Corani-Benavoli analogue), detectable (MDE = (t_{.975,dof} + t_{.80,dof})*se replacing 2.80*se) and detectable_r2. gen16_protocol/gen16/clusterboot.py duplicates WCR with CV1/CV3 variances, test-inversion CI by bisection, css_effective_clusters and percentile_block_p for side-by-side printing. The docstrings and README recommend WCR as default and CV3 as the non-bootstrap fallback (MacKinnon-Nielsen-Webb 2023), the cluster_macro estimand for the ROPE, and CR2-t MDEs (0.05-0.11 for paired contrasts). However, gen16_leads/PRE_REGISTRATION.md section 0 sealed gen13sep.inference.paired_contrasts as the inference, gen16_protocol/README.md:96-97 records 'Inference not adopted', and gen19 transfer.py re-implemented the percentile+BCa cluster bootstrap (seed 19) with no WCR. The gen13 re-inference table per_extractant_wildcluster.csv exists for BP_all (e.g. M_SELECTED vs B1: p_old 0.0038, p_wcr 0.0105, p_cr2_t_bm 0.019, dof_bm 11.13, mde80_OLD 0.056 vs mde80_cr2_t 0.060).

findings.topic: (4c) Measured-mode interval coverage and covariance defect (gen16 L5)
findings.detail: Coverage is computed POOLED over scored pairs (not per extractant): cover_lv = mean(|y - pred| <= z_lv * sd) with z_lv = norm.ppf(0.5 + lv/2) and sd = BLUP posterior pair sd (fewshot.pair_sd with NOISE_VAR 0.09); g15_uncertainty.coverage_table and l5_covrun.coverage_rows are the same logic. calibration_intervals.csv: BP POOLED cover90 = 0.9265 at k=0, 0.9825 at k=1, 0.9846 at k=2, 0.9884 at k=3 (n_pairs 52,662); the gen16 verdict rule requires cover90 within [0.85, 0.95] in every design and a smaller |cover90 - 0.90| gap than POOLED. DECISION_REPORT section 7: the deployed leave-chemotype-out residual covariance is indefinite on 100% of its 430 estimates (pairwise-complete second moment with 35-80% missingness), making Ledoit-Wolf catastrophic (k=3 MAE 34.41); intervals are conservative by about 2.5x in width; direction probability ECE 0.301 (Platt) / 0.139 (raw) against a 0.10 bar.

findings.topic: (5) LOCO (leave-one-chemotype-out sign stability)
findings.detail: gen13 inference.py:83-90: for each chemotype b, keep = all units except members of b, loco[b] = mean of finite deltas among kept units; loco_stable = all(sign(loco[finite]) == sign(point)) if point != 0 else False; reported as loco_min, loco_max, loco_sign_stable. leave_one_chemotype_out() writes the full sweep (dropped_chemotype incl. '(none)', delta, n_units) to bootstrap/<label>/leave_one_chemotype_out.csv. Same-sign means a NEGATIVE point with all-negative LOCO is 'stable'. gen14 paired_gain uses the identical rule. gen16 L3 uses loco_weights (zero weight for the dropped chemotype, task-level recomputation). gen19 transfer: the jackknife series jk[g] = (tot_s - s_g)/(tot_n - n_g) per cluster feeds both the BCa acceleration and R19 item 5, which FAILS if any LOCO delta <= 0 or is non-finite, under every registered cluster unit; at confirmation one cluster is removed from all five seeds at once.

findings.topic: (6) Benjamini-Hochberg usage
findings.detail: Five independent implementations, all 'printed beside the raw p, never deciding': gen19 transfer.benjamini_hochberg (stable argsort, step-up, monotone via reversed np.minimum.accumulate, capped at 1; a NaN p stays NaN and by default still counts toward m; rejects p outside [0,1]; tested against scipy false_discovery_control), applied by discovery.apply_bh per family (primary, H1b, S1(b), S1(c), H4, ladder, secondary designs, exploratory) on primary-cluster-unit rows of seed 104729, with p_bh_pooled_registered and p_bh_full_family (unevaluated registered contrasts entered as p = 1, m = 60) printed beside; gen19 confirmation.bh_adjust (dict version, NaN excluded from m); gen16 l5_summary.bh (mergesort, no NaN handling), gen16 l4_retro.bh (NaN dropped, rank method 'first'), gen16 refute_L4BP_A_checks recomputes BH over L4's family of 20; gen18 evalproto ComparisonCounter.benjamini_hochberg over the exploratory family only. Families: gen16 registered family of 126/128 and exploratory 902 (1030 rows); confirmed claim L3a q = 0.020-0.043 registered, 0.027 over the combined 1030. Holm-Bonferroni is used in gen13 stage-2 D7 (14 elements) and src/kshot_calibration.py (one-sided over gated (arm, policy, k)). The recovery plan section 10 instead prescribes Bonferroni 98.75% intervals for a maximum of four pre-named claims.

findings.topic: (7a) Needed additions: R2 with undefined-case handling, hierarchical weights, per-adjacent-pair R2
findings.detail: Write new: (i) an r2 function returning (value, reason) with NA for n < 2 or zero variance (plan section 6.2 rules), ideally calling sklearn.metrics.r2_score(..., force_finite=False) in sklearn 1.9.0 as the check — gen19 metrics.r2_score is the closest (weighted, NaN on SS_tot = 0) but has no reason string; (ii) a four-level weight builder w_i = 1/(L * P_l * C_lp * N_lpc) for MAE_bal/RMSE_bal/Bias_bal/R2_balanced — gen19 metrics.row_weights supports only a two-level nesting (1/(n_strata_u * n_us)) and the gen13 pair table has no publication/series columns (the cohort frame carries publication_id and the condition key, so a join on cell_id is needed; gen15 fewshot.evaluate reads bench.frame.publication_id); (iii) R2_pair_macro over the 91 unordered metal pairs with valid/total counts and exclusion list — reuse the pair table's A, B, dZ columns and metrics.is_adjacent for R2_adjacent; R2_PrNd filters A == 'Pr' & B == 'Nd' (gen13 lighter-first) — note the plan's within-system R2 requires groups (publication, system, metal pair) with >= 3 condition sets, which needs the condition key from the cohort frame. The old gen13 extractant-macro MAE must be printed beside under its own name, not equated to MAE_bal (plan section 6.1).

findings.topic: (7b) Needed additions: common-query vs remaining-query, paired comparisons on identical rows, CI on R2 improvement
findings.detail: Common vs remaining query: gen15 fewshot.evaluate already fixes the scoring set per cell (support pairs of kmax, union over strategies when hows is given, excluded at EVERY k, so k=0..3 are on byte-identical pairs) and l3/l5 reuse it; but the query set depends on the selection strategy and cell, not on a hash, and the zero-shot run scores all pairs (n_units 90) while few-shot scores 84 units. No code implements the plan's SHA-256('gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B') rule, the Q_PrNd set, or the arithmetic-closure constraint (support-pair graph components); gen19 support_graph.py's connected components are for the chemistry support graph, not pair closure. Write new. Paired comparisons on identical rows: reuse gen19 transfer._aligned (raises when units differ or values non-finite) and discovery.paired_units (raises if the two arms score different row index sets); gen13 paired_contrasts silently uses the finite intersection; gen16 g16_bp1.delta() uses dropna. 95% CI on an R2 improvement with chemotype-blocked resampling: reuse gen19 transfer.cluster_bootstrap_statistic(frame, cluster_col, statistic) with statistic = R2(cand) - R2(base) recomputed on each resampled frame (this recomputes denominators per resample as plan section 10 requires, gives percentile + BCa via the cluster jackknife + p + mde_80); it is a python loop over 10,000 replicates calling frame.iloc on concatenated member indices, so on a 70,000-row pair table it will be slow — a vectorised sums-based version like gen13 inference.py:63-67 / gen19 transfer.py:352-356 is needed for weighted R2 (per-cluster sums of w*e^2, w*y, w*y^2, w suffice). For a per-unit mean (e.g. per-extractant MAE delta) use gen13 paired_contrasts or gen13 wildcluster.wild_cluster_t for a size-correct p; WCR does not apply directly to an R2 difference. Publication-grouped resampling on the gen13 pair table does not exist (gen19 has publication_group clusters for V5 only); plan section 10 wants both groupings at 2000 resamples and 98.75% Bonferroni intervals.
evidence: generations/gen15_curve/gen15/fewshot.py:61-73 (fixed scoring set), 168-173 (union of support pairs excluded)

findings.topic: (8) Effective sample size: Kish 11.7 and its relatives
findings.detail: metrics.effective_sample_size(counts) = 1/sum(p^2) with p = n/sum(n), written to context.json as kish_n_eff_chemotypes = 11.6715 for BP_all; wildcluster.kish and clusterboot.kish_neff are the same (sum n)^2/sum n^2. Recomputed here from metrics/BP_all/per_extractant.csv: G = 45, N = 90, size profile {1: 34, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 1, 6: 2, 23: 1}, Kish 11.6715; the 289-rich-cell cohort (n_metals >= 5) has 82 extractants in 40 chemotypes, Kish 10.07, largest sc009 = 23. Related quantities: Bell-McCaffrey dof for the 45-chemotype profile 11.13 (per_extractant_wildcluster.csv) and 9.57 for the 40-chemotype one (g16_dir_signflip_BP.csv); CSS G* = G/(1+Gamma) with gamma_g = n_g + n_g(n_g-1)rho, 10.07 at rho 0, 2.5 at 0.2, 1.9 at 0.4, 1.7 at 0.6 (order-of-magnitude only); reliability-weighted effective chemotypes sum_g n_g/(n_g + (1-rho)/rho) = 34.26 at ICC 0.72, 29.48 at 0.6, 25.39 at 0.5 (g16_detectability.py argues this, not Kish, is the right count for between-chemotype covariate questions; Kish is right for a unit-weighted mean). Detectable between-chemotype R2 at 80% power: 0.196 (1 predictor) / 0.266 (3) at n_eff 34.26; 0.154 / 0.210 at nominal 45; 0.455 / 0.611 at Kish 11.67. ICC 0.72 is a hard-coded assumption (amplitude ICC from gen13 stage 2); gen16_protocol's REML profile puts the chemotype share at 0.313 [0.139, 0.711].

findings.topic: Orientation and convention mismatches a new experiment must reconcile
findings.detail: gen13 pair rows have A lighter (pair_rows_for_cell a < b, y = y[a] - y[b]; test_pair_rows_only_lighter_first), so 'heavier preferred' is y < 0; gen19 pairs.py puts state_a heavier so logSF_Nd/Pr > 0 means heavier preferred. MAE and direction accuracy are orientation-invariant but sign conventions, Bias_bal and any 'heavier always' yardstick are not. Zero-prediction sign convention differs (gen13 wrong, gen19 and plan 1/2). gen13 macro resamples 90 extractants in 45 chemotypes; gen15 few-shot scores 84 units; gen16 L3 uses (seed, metal-pair) tasks; gen19 V5 units are hidden cells clustered by system and publication group. BCa differs: gen8 clamps z0's proportion to [1e-6, 1-1e-6] with no mid-rank and returns NaN only for < 50 draws or < 3 jackknife values; gen19 uses the mid-rank proportion, returns NaN when the proportion is 0 or 1, when n_clusters < 3, or when the BCa denominator <= 0, and R19 treats NaN as failure. Seeds: gen13 averages per-unit values over seeds before resampling; gen16 L3 and gen19 confirmation resample clusters once and apply them to every seed; gen19 discovery used seed 104729 only.

findings.topic: Audit script, tests and documentation state
findings.detail: docs/figures/METRIC_AUDIT.md (67/67 checks) covers gen6-gen10 figure quantities, cohorts C-FULL (131 ECFP clusters), C-COMMON (99 extractants) and C-CURVE, and states every figure interval resamples chemotypes with gen8.inference.paired_chemotype_bootstrap (5000 replicates, seed 8675309); it does not audit the gen13-gen19 separation metrics. Tests: gen13 test_gen13_invariants.py has test_per_extractant_metrics_identity and test_pair_rows_only_lighter_first but no test of inference.paired_contrasts or wildcluster; gen19 test_transfer_stats.py covers seed-19 reproducibility, higher-is-better sign flip, LOCO hand values, p/MDE/record, unpaired rejection, BCa vs percentile on a skewed statistic, BCa against the scipy formula, generic-statistic draws, R19 items 1-6, TOST, BH, delta5, injection; gen19 test_metrics.py covers r2_score. gen16_protocol has no tests and is unreviewed/exploratory. pytest --collect-only on the three files collects 63 tests. The recovery plan (section 6, 8, 9, 10) was never executed: no MAE_bal, no six-R2 table, no 2000-resample two-grouping bootstrap, no hash-defined Q, no arithmetic-closure check exists in code.

reusable_components.what: per_extractant(pairs, arms, curve_spearman=None) -> per-(seed, extractant, arm) table (mae_all, mae_adjacent, mae_far, sign_acc_strong, pair_spearman); summarise(per_ext, pairs, arms) -> leaderboard with extractant-macro, chemotype-macro, pooled; is_adjacent(); heavier_always_sign_accuracy(); effective_sample_size() (Kish).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Feed any long pair table with columns split_seed, extractant, chemotype, cell_id, n_metals, A, B, dZ, y and one column per arm (gen15 valuebench.run_arms / gen13 runner.load_pair_table produce it). Call per_extractant then summarise; pass the result to inference.paired_contrasts. Use effective_sample_size(counts) for Kish n_eff.
reusable_components.caveats: Lighter-first orientation (y = logD(A) - logD(B), A lighter). A zero prediction counts as a wrong sign (np.sign(0) = 0). mae_all pools pairs within extractant (cells not equally weighted). Pooled numbers count each cell once per seed. NaN-dropping in macro adjacent/far means those macros are over fewer extractants (83/88 of 90).

reusable_components.what: paired_contrasts(per_ext, comparisons, value, replicates=10000, seed=8675309, margin=0.02): chemotype-blocked paired bootstrap on per-unit means (percentile + BCa + two-sided p + bootstrap_se + mde_80 + per-seed sign count + LOCO + passes_P1); leave_one_chemotype_out() sweep table.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Pass a per_extractant table with columns arm, extractant, chemotype, split_seed and the value column; comparisons = {label: (reference, candidate)}. Vectorised via per-replicate sums; one shared draw matrix per call so contrasts are comparable. Imports _bca_interval from src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/inference.py (paths.py puts src on sys.path).
reusable_components.caveats: Averages the value over seeds per unit before resampling (seed variance hidden). Only a per-unit mean statistic; cannot do an R2 difference. Percentile bootstrap over-rejects at 7-8% (nominal 5%). 'Exclude 0' tested on lower bounds only. Requires >= 3 finite units and >= 2 chemotypes. HIGHER_IS_BETTER set is hard-coded.

reusable_components.what: cluster_robust (CR0-CR3 SE + Bell-McCaffrey dof), wild_cluster_t (restricted wild cluster bootstrap-t, CI by inversion), bayes_bootstrap and random_effects (ROPE posteriors), detectable (MDE on t dof), detectable_r2, kish.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: d = per-unit paired delta (reference - candidate), cluster = chemotype labels; wild_cluster_t(d, cluster, reps=9999, se_kind='CR2') returns p_wcr, p_wcu, CI, dof_bm; g13_inference_audit.reinfer() shows the full pattern and writes *_wildcluster.csv. numpy/scipy only, < 1 s for N = 90.
reusable_components.caveats: Intercept-only model: applies to a mean of per-unit deltas, not to an R2 difference or any pooled statistic. Rademacher with G active clusters has a p floor 2/2^G_active (gen16_protocol g16_dir_signflip documents G_active 13 for one claim). Never adopted as the registered procedure in gen16/gen19.

reusable_components.what: wcr_test (WCR with CV1/CV3, bisection CI), percentile_block_p (gen13 estimator reimplemented), compare_inference (side-by-side row incl. verdict_changes_at_05), css_effective_clusters, kish_neff, size_study (null simulation on the real cluster membership).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: size_study(cluster_labels, icc, sims, reps) to measure any new test's size on a given cluster membership before registering it; compare_inference(delta, cluster) to print old vs WCR p for an existing contrast.
reusable_components.caveats: Unreviewed, exploratory, no tests; duplicates gen13 wildcluster with CV1 default instead of CR2; size_study uses Gaussian nulls (the gen13 audit adds t3 tails).

reusable_components.what: paired_cluster_bootstrap (vectorised, seed 19, 10,000, percentile + BCa with mid-rank z0 and cluster jackknife + p + mde_80 + LOCO), unclustered_bootstrap, cluster_bootstrap_statistic (any statistic of a frame under cluster resampling), seed_mean_cluster_bootstrap / seed_mean_nested_cluster_bootstrap (same resampled clusters applied to every seed), r19, tost, benjamini_hochberg, delta5.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: For a paired per-unit contrast: paired_cluster_bootstrap(comp_series, cand_series, cluster_series). For an R2 difference or any pooled statistic with recomputed denominators: cluster_bootstrap_statistic(frame, 'chemotype', lambda f: r2(f.y, f.cand, w) - r2(f.y, f.base, w)). For combining seeds: seed_mean_nested_cluster_bootstrap with one column per seed. BH: benjamini_hochberg(p, nan_counts_toward_m=True). Tested in tests/test_transfer_stats.py.
reusable_components.caveats: cluster_bootstrap_statistic is a python loop with frame.iloc per replicate (10,000 x concatenation) — slow on a 70k-row pair table; write a sums-based version for weighted R2. BCa returns NaN (never clipped) in degenerate cases and R19 treats NaN as failure. Imports gen19ct.evaluation.metrics (and lazily gen19ct.folds for guards) so it carries gen19 package assumptions; the bootstrap functions themselves are pure pandas/numpy.

reusable_components.what: r2_score(y, pred, weights) hand-written weighted R2 (NaN on SS_tot = 0); per_unit_table, row_weights(equal_weight_within), unit_index, spearman_rho, rank_accuracy_table, tidy summary_record/logd_summary with unit_macro / row_pooled / system_macro side versions.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: r2_score is the only existing R2 primitive with a NaN convention; wrap it to return (value, reason) and to accept the plan's hierarchical weights. row_weights shows the two-level 'each stratum weight 1/n_strata' pattern to extend to four levels. The tidy (stratum, metric, aggregation, role, value, note) summary format is a good target for the six-R2 table.
reusable_components.caveats: Built for the gen19 log D row target with V5/V1 unit columns and the V6 scoring guard (guard_scoring_index raises without a v6_mask unless design == 'V6'); use the pure helpers, not logd_summary, on a gen13 pair table. No force_finite, no reason strings.

reusable_components.what: evaluate(bench, arms, design, ks, how/hows, cov_kind, mask_publication, ...) -> fixed-scoring-set few-shot pair table; blup, blup_posterior, pair_sd, naive_line, line_plus_curvature, pick_support (widest / dopt), residual_covariance, centred_residual.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: The 'exclude the support pairs of the largest budget (union over strategies) at every k' construction is the existing common-query mechanism; its output table goes straight into gen13 per_extractant/summarise/paired_contrasts (modes named arm@howkK, NAIVE_LINE@kK, sd@kK).
reusable_components.caveats: Query set is strategy- and cell-dependent, not hash-defined; cells with <= kmax pairs or < min_metals+1 observed metals are dropped (84 vs 90 units); uses abs(hash((ci, seed))) for the per-cell RNG (int tuple, unsalted); residual_covariance is indefinite (gen16 L5); NOISE_VAR 0.09 over-covers.

reusable_components.what: calibration(sizes, icc, sims, reps, tails) null-simulation of nine procedures on the real chemotype-size profile; reinfer() recomputes every saved contrast under WCR, CR2-t(BM dof), Bayesian-bootstrap ROPE and random-effects ROPE; writes inference_calibration.csv and <per_extractant>_wildcluster.csv.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Run on any per_extractant.csv to get size-corrected p-values and CR2-t MDEs next to the percentile ones; the calibration() routine can be pointed at a new cluster-size profile (e.g. publication groups).
reusable_components.caveats: Overwrites committed CSVs next to the input (do not run in the repo tree without copying). Default sims = 1000 (committed file used 3000). ICC 0.72 hard-coded default.

reusable_components.what: reliability_neff(n_g, icc) = sum n_g/(n_g + (1-icc)/icc) and the detectable between-chemotype R2 table at nominal, Kish and reliability-weighted effective counts.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Quote the bracket [45 nominal, 34.26 reliability-weighted, 11.67 Kish] with the matching question (covariate vs unit-weighted mean) when stating power for a new experiment.
reusable_components.caveats: ICC 0.72 assumed; REML profile gives 0.313 [0.139, 0.711]; unreviewed directory.

reusable_components.what: bh() BH adjustment and add_bh() writing p_bh_lead per family into contrasts files; verdict logic: P1 in all five designs, sign consistency across designs, coverage band [0.85, 0.95] check.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Pattern for a mechanical verdict JSON over a contrasts table (registered family BH, all-five-designs rule).
reusable_components.caveats: bh() has no NaN handling (NaN propagates through argsort); prefer gen19 transfer.benjamini_hochberg.

risks.risk: The deciding p-value (chemotype percentile bootstrap, inference.paired_contrasts) over-rejects: 0.071-0.077 at nominal 0.05 on the 45-chemotype profile, 0.0705-0.0815 on the 40-chemotype profile; the 2.80*bootstrap_se MDE understates detectable effects. A new experiment that registers this p inherits a ~1.5x inflated type-I rate.
risks.mitigation: Register WCR (gen13sep.wildcluster.wild_cluster_t, se_kind CR2 or CR3) or CR3-t on Bell-McCaffrey dof as the deciding p for per-unit mean contrasts (both hold 0.041-0.048); print the percentile p beside for continuity; use wildcluster.detectable for MDE. Re-measure size with g13_inference_audit.calibration on the actual cluster profile (and on publication groups) before sealing.

risks.risk: R2 does not exist on log SF anywhere; adding it on the gen13 pair table will be dominated by sc009 (375/521 cells, 23/90 extractants), by far pairs (dZ >= 5 are 6,698 of 14,150 pairs per seed) and by 5x duplication of each cell across seeds if pooled over the seed-stacked table.
risks.mitigation: Compute R2 per seed (plan section 6.2: never average fold R2s with different variances; report per-seed values and the range), use hierarchical weights (MAE_bal/R2_balanced) and a per-pair macro with valid/total counts; NA with reason for zero-variance groups; keep the old extractant-macro MAE beside under its own name.

risks.risk: Two BCa implementations disagree in degenerate cases (gen8 clamps z0 and never returns NaN for a healthy draw count; gen19 returns NaN and R19 fails on NaN); with one chemotype holding a quarter of the units the acceleration from a 45-point jackknife is unstable, and gen19 itself calls BCa unreliable at 13 clusters.
risks.mitigation: Pick one BCa (gen19's mid-rank version with explicit NaN) and state the fallback when BCa is undefined; report bias_z0 and acceleration beside the interval as gen19 does; consider the cluster_macro Bayesian bootstrap (wildcluster.bayes_bootstrap) as the robustness check.

risks.risk: 'Exclude 0' is implemented as lower bound > 0 only (gen13 passes_intervals, gen19 item 2), and gen13 LOCO 'stable' is same-sign, so a rule can pass without the upper bound ever being inspected and a negative effect can be 'LOCO-stable'.
risks.mitigation: State the one-sided reading explicitly in the new pre-registration (as gen19 does) or test both bounds; adopt gen19's strict LOCO (> 0) and print loco_min.

risks.risk: Seeds are averaged per unit before resampling in gen13 (seed variance 0.014-0.042 macro MAE hidden), while gen16 L3 and gen19 confirmation resample clusters once and apply to every seed; mixing these conventions in one table makes intervals incomparable.
risks.mitigation: Use gen19 seed_mean_nested_cluster_bootstrap (same resampled clusters applied to every seed, per-seed values printed) for any multi-seed statistic, and the plan's rule that seeds are not bootstrap units.

risks.risk: Convention mismatches: gen13 lighter-first (heavier preferred = y < 0) vs gen19 heavier-first (logSF > 0); zero prediction counted wrong (gen13) vs 1/2 (gen19, plan); strong threshold 0.3 everywhere but plan adds 0.1 for Pr/Nd. A k-shot study mixing gen13 pair tables with gen19 conventions will mis-score direction and bias.
risks.mitigation: Fix one orientation and the 1/2 tie rule in code and tests before any number is produced; recompute B4_HEAVIER_ALWAYS and FLAT under that rule and check FLAT direction accuracy is exactly 0.5.

risks.risk: Measured-mode intervals and covariance are not usable as calibrated: 90% nominal covers 98.8% at k=3, the residual covariance is indefinite on 100% of 430 estimates, and coverage is pooled over pairs (not per extractant).
risks.mitigation: For a k-shot study use a PSD covariance (plan section 8.2), a per-cell or per-extractant coverage macro, and report coverage curves at 80/95% with widths (plan section 6.4); do not reuse NOISE_VAR = 0.09 without recalibrating on training residuals.

risks.risk: Common-query evaluation exists only as gen15's strategy-dependent exclusion (84 units) and gen10's C-COMMON cohort (99 extractants); no hash-defined Q, no arithmetic-closure guard, no publication-grouped resampling on the gen13 table. Implementing these ad hoc risks silently changing the question between k = 0 and k = 3.
risks.mitigation: Write a single query-set builder (SHA-256 rule, Q_PrNd, support-graph component check) used by every arm and policy, with a test that the Q per cell is identical across k, arms and policies; write a sums-based cluster bootstrap that accepts either chemotype or publication labels.

risks.risk: cluster_bootstrap_statistic (the only ready primitive for a bootstrapped R2 difference) loops over 10,000 replicates with frame.iloc; on 70k pair rows x 5 seeds this is minutes-to-hours per contrast and invites reducing replicates.
risks.mitigation: Vectorise: per-cluster sums of w, w*y, w*y^2, w*e_cand^2, w*e_base^2 give R2 of any resample as a matmul (the pattern of gen13 inference.py:63-67 and gen19 transfer.py:352-356).

risks.risk: gen16_protocol results are unreviewed and partly incomplete (size study stops at ICC 0.6; variance run never finished), and the ICC 0.72 used by every power statement is contradicted by the REML profile (0.313 [0.139, 0.711]).
risks.mitigation: Treat 34.26 / 11.67 / 45 as a bracket; if a power claim is needed, rerun size_study/calibration at the ICC actually estimated on the new target.
