open_questions: Which p-value will the new experiment register as deciding: the percentile cluster bootstrap (size 0.07-0.08) that gen16/gen19 kept for continuity, or WCR/CR3-t (size 0.04-0.05) that gen13 wildcluster and gen16_protocol recommend but nobody adopted? The recovery plan section 10 names only a 2000-resample paired bootstrap under two groupings and says the intervals promise no exact 95% coverage.

On which table should the six R2s be computed: the gen13 seed-stacked pair table (each held-out cell appears once per seed; pooled R2 would count it 5 times) or per seed with the range reported, and with the lighter-first or heavier-first orientation (Bias_bal flips sign)?

The plan's hierarchical weights need publication P_l and series C_lp per extractant; the gen13 pair table carries only cell_id/extractant/chemotype — the join to publication_id and condition-series keys must come from the cohort manifest (cohort_<key_mode>.parquet). Is key_mode 'exact' or 'series' the intended series definition (gen16 defect 7: 'series' uses the relaxed columns and gives 597 vs 557 cells)?

Publication-grouped resampling on the gen13 pair table does not exist; how are publication groups defined for the 521-cell cohort (gen16_protocol says 75 of 82 extractants are single-publication, so publication clusters nearly coincide with extractants)?

BCa reliability with 45 clusters of which one holds 23 units: gen19 declares BCa unreliable at 13 clusters and R19 fails on NaN; gen8's clamp hides the same degeneracy. Which behaviour is registered for the new experiment, and is the Bayesian-bootstrap cluster_macro ROPE the intended robustness check?
Should 'exclude 0' remain one-sided (lower bound > 0 only), and should LOCO use gen13's same-sign rule or gen19's strictly-positive rule?

The zero-prediction sign convention differs (gen13 wrong vs gen19/plan 1/2): which one applies to FLAT, B4_HEAVIER_ALWAYS and any tie, and does the 0.1 Pr/Nd threshold of the plan replace or sit beside the 0.3 strong threshold?

For the k-shot section: the plan's SHA-256 query rule ('gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B'), Q_PrNd, and the arithmetic-closure graph constraint have no code; gen15 fewshot.evaluate's fixed set (84 units) is strategy-dependent. Is the intended common cohort the intersection of cells where both policies can supply three admissible supports (plan 8.2), and how is the 90-vs-84 unit gap to zero-shot handled?

ICC 0.72 (amplitude) drives every power and size statement, but the REML profile puts the chemotype share at 0.313 [0.139, 0.711] and the ICC 0.72 size-study row was never run; which ICC should the new experiment's power statement assume, and should size be re-measured on the new target (log SF R2 difference rather than a per-extractant MAE mean)?

cluster_bootstrap_statistic is the only ready primitive for a bootstrapped R2 difference and is a per-replicate python loop; is a new vectorised sums-based implementation in scope, and should it live beside gen19 transfer.py or in a new gen20 package?

Which measured-mode numbers does the new design anchor to: gen15's widest-pair board (G14@k3 0.2051, NAIVE_LINE@k3 0.2359, 84 units), gen16 L5's D-optimal common scoring set (POOLED 0.1674, MIX6meanPC 0.1604) or the gen15 mixture board (POOLED@k3 0.1922)? These are different scoring sets and the prompt's 0.163-0.170 / 0.2347 match the gen16 table and neither gen15 board exactly.

audits.scope: READ-ONLY audit of train/test splitting, the five gen13 hold-out designs (A/B/BR/BQ/BP), publication masking, duplicate / near-duplicate handling, preprocessing and hyperparameter leakage, k-shot support/query isolation, and process-salted hashing, across generations/gen13_separation (gen13sep/splits.py, runner.py, cohort.py, features.py, models.py, basis.py, amplitude_bench.py, fewshot.py, fewshot_stage2.py, arms_stage2.py, tests/, PRE_REGISTRATION.md, DECISION_REPORT.md), generations/gen14_direction/gen14 (dirbench.py, models.py, GEN14_REPORT.md), generations/gen15_curve/gen15 (valuebench.py, fewshot.py, arms.py, shape.py, mixture.py, scripts/g15_*.py, GEN15_REPORT.md), generations/gen16_leads (tests/, gen16/anchors.py, foldhash.py, l5_fewshot.py, scripts/g16_env_check.py, START_HERE.md §1, CONFIRMATION.md), docs/audits/LEAKAGE_AUDIT.md, generations/gen19_chem_transfer/gen19ct/folds/*.py, gen19ct/data/leakage.py, folds/INDEX.json, DATA_AUDIT.md, src/lanthanide_separation/gen6/cohorts.py, and LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md §8. Three short read-only Python computations were run on the frozen cohort (manifests/cohort_exact.parquet, 521 cells) and gen19's leakage_publication_components.csv; pytest was run in --collect-only mode only. No tracked file was modified.
audits.summary: The gen13 fold plan is a single deterministic splitter (src/lanthanide_separation/gen6/cohorts.py:100-123: np.unique-sorted group labels, numpy default_rng(seed).permutation, round-robin dealing) applied to the frozen 521-cell cohort with five split seeds (104729, 130363, 155921, 196613, 262147; gen13sep/splits.py:24), 5 outer folds per seed, and one 4-way inner split per outer fold; designs B/BP/BR/BQ group on the frozen gen6 chemotype and A on the exact canonical SMILES (splits.py:30), so B, BP, BR and BQ share byte-identical test sets per seed and differ only in training rows. The BP publication mask is applied per fold, not per test cell: every training cell whose gen6 publication_id appears among any held-out cell of that fold is dropped (splits.py:75-77), BR drops the same count at random and BQ drops whole unrelated publications matched on cells and condition series (splits.py:78-103), and the inner split is re-dealt on the masked training set (splits.py:105-107). model_seed is 42 + fold*1009 + 9,999,991 (splits.py:59-60), i.e. five values (10000033…10004069) that depend only on the fold index and are reused across all split seeds and designs as the ExtraTrees random_state. Chemotype isolation is guaranteed structurally by whole-group dealing and asserted at run time by assert_fold_integrity (splits.py:124-149; called by runner.py:70), but the gen13 test suite exercises it for design B only (tests/test_gen13_invariants.py:69-77); the five-design fold plan is pinned by a SHA-256 computed in a subprocess (gen16/tests/test_anchors.py:40-49, gen16/foldhash.py) and the gen14/gen15/gen16 benches call all_folds without the integrity assertion. Exact-SMILES duplicates, homologues (7 ECFP-bit-identical groups covering 20 of the 90 extractants) and stereoisomers (90 SMILES collapse to 88 when stereo is removed; the one collapsing triple shares chemotype sc027) are all held out together under the chemotype designs, while design A deliberately leaks homologues. Cross-publication copies are not handled by gen13's BP: BP masks the raw gen6 publication_id, and gen19's copy-group map (which reproduces gen6 publication ids 1:1; DATA_AUDIT.md:443) places 45 gen13 cells from 5 publications in 3 multi-publication copy groups, including one group (pub_0af6736cb1) whose two gen13 publications span 5 chemotypes and 18 cells, so the sibling publication stays in training when BP masks the held-out cell's own. gen19 additionally detects state- and structure-wildcard copies that its registered near-duplicate key cannot see (265 pairs; V5-primary exact folds have 134 scored rows with a training-side copy, 26 strict) and reports rather than guards them (INDEX.json leakage_sensitivity_wildcard_copies; DATA_AUDIT.md:357-378). No imputer, scaler, PCA or feature selector is fitted on test rows anywhere in gen13–gen15: every learned transform sits inside an sklearn Pipeline fitted on the training fold, data bases are fitted on ctx.centred_train, and the per-cell ridge coefficients used as targets are cell-local. Hyperparameters were never tuned by nested CV in the deployed path: gen13 fixed them a priori and selected M_SELECTED on an inner chemotype split, but gen14's deployed LOGIT_TOPO39 (C=1, l2, std) was chosen from a 30-candidate sweep scored on the outer folds of all five designs including BP (GEN14_REPORT.md:160-168), the honest inner-CV penalty variant was evaluated and rejected, and gen15's D-optimal support policy and covariance settings were likewise compared on outer designs; the gen16 fresh-seed confirmation covered only the L3a measurements-saved claim, so the deployed 0.500 (BP) and 0.163–0.170 (D-optimal k=3) numbers have never been re-estimated on withheld seeds. For a k-shot extension, gen15/fewshot.py already handles a fixed scoring set at every budget, union exclusion of supports across strategies, a leave-chemotype-out and publication-masked residual covariance, and y-blind support selection, but it does not prevent algebraic closure: on the frozen cohort the gen15 widest-3 rule leaves 963 of 12,863 scored pairs (7.5%) determined exactly by the supports, in every one of the 321 scored cells, and its covariance is built from other test cells' out-of-fold residuals rather than from inner cross-fits inside the training set as the recovery plan §8.2 requires. Python's salted hash() is absent from every splitter; the only salted-bytes call on the gen13 path is arms_stage2.py:330 (stage-3 hierarchical arms, off the gen14/gen15 bench path), and the two int-tuple hash() seeds in gen15/fewshot.py:336 and gen16/l5_fewshot.py:169 are unsalted in CPython but platform-width dependent.

findings.topic: (1) Outer fold construction: splitter, seeds, shuffle, fold count
findings.detail: All five designs use seeded_group_kfold from src/lanthanide_separation/gen6/cohorts.py:100-123: group labels are cast to str, np.unique sorts them, np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(names) shuffles the GROUP labels (rows are never shuffled), fold_of = i % n_splits deals round-robin, and a fold with an empty test set is skipped. N_SPLITS=5 (splits.py:25), SPLIT_SEEDS=(104729, 130363, 155921, 196613, 262147) (splits.py:24), so all_folds returns 25 Fold objects per design (splits.py:116-121); test_gen13_invariants.py:73 asserts len(folds)==25 and :75-77 that every cell is held out exactly once per seed. Grouping key per design (splits.py:30): B, BP, BR, BQ -> frame['chemotype'] (the frozen gen6 chem__supercluster, cohort.py:199-205); A -> frame['extractant'] (canonical_smiles). Consequence: for a given seed, B/BP/BR/BQ have byte-identical test_index arrays and differ only in train_index; A has different test sets. Fold indices are positional into the cohort frame, which is sorted deterministically by (extractant, publication_id, condition_key) (cohort.py:208). Largest-group imbalance is accepted (cohorts.py:108-110); the 375-cell diglycolamide chemotype lands whole in one fold per seed (models.py:322-323 note).

findings.topic: (1) Publication mask (BP) is applied per FOLD, and the BR/BQ controls
findings.detail: splits.py:72-77: for BP/BR/BQ, held = set(publications[test_index]) is the set of publication_ids over ALL held-out cells of the outer fold; keep[i] = publications[train_index[i]] not in held. So a training cell is removed if its publication appears in any test cell of the fold, not only the cell currently being scored; masking is per fold, with one masked training set per (seed, fold). n_drop = number of removed training cells. BR (splits.py:78-81): drop exactly n_drop training rows at random with np.random.default_rng(seed*7 + k*101 + 3). BQ (splits.py:82-103): candidates = np.unique(train_pubs) not in held, rng.shuffle with default_rng(seed*11 + k*131 + 5), then greedy closest-fit removal of whole training publications until n_gone >= n_drop AND s_gone >= number of distinct (publication, condition_key) series BP removed. The inner validation split (splits.py:105-107) is re-dealt on the masked train_index with inner_seed = seed*31 + k*7919 + 17, N_INNER_SPLITS=4, taking only the FIRST inner fold (next(iter(...))) -> one inner train/validation split per outer fold; inner groups are the design's group column (chemotype for B/BP/BR/BQ, extractant for A). publication_id comes from runs/gen6_provenance/provenance_table.parquet joined on safe_exp_id (cohort.py:142-146; paths.py:25) and is part of the cell key (cohort.py:153-154), so a cell never spans two publications (test_gen13_invariants.py:42). Sizes: BP masked training sets hold 76-492 cells versus 103-507 unmasked; BP removes 952 training cells and 609 condition series over the 25 folds, BQ removes 971/922 (DECISION_REPORT.md:184, 210-214). Design BP/BR/BQ were added AFTER the primary endpoints were scored (PRE_REGISTRATION.md addendum 2, :164-179) and the rule 'the deployed configuration is chosen under BP, never under design B' is registered there (:176).

findings.topic: (1) model_seed
findings.detail: Fold.model_seed = MODEL_SEED_BASE + fold*FOLD_SEED_STRIDE + FOLD_SEED_OFFSET = 42 + k*1009 + 9_999_991 (splits.py:27-29, 59-60). It depends only on the fold index k in 0..4, NOT on the split seed or the design, so exactly five model seeds exist: 10000033, 10001042, 10002051, 10003060, 10004069, each reused across all five split seeds and all five designs. It is passed as FitContext.seed (runner.py:88-91) and becomes ExtraTreesRegressor/Classifier random_state (models.py:36-43 tree_pipeline; gen14/models.py:102-105, 275-277), the AntisymmetricPairArm subsampling rng (models.py:293), HelperBlockArm shuffle rng (ctx.seed+17, models.py:570), gen14 dirbench's fit_predict seed (dirbench.py:151), gen14 dir_logistic_cv inner-CV rng (gen14/models.py:180), and gen15 Ctx.model_seed used by g13_full and the k-medians prototypes (valuebench.py:113; arms.py:111; shape.py:163). Memory note (gen7 harness contract) that 'model seed is fixed at 42, independent of the split seed' is consistent with this.

findings.topic: (2) Guarantees that no chemotype crosses folds, and what is asserted
findings.detail: Structural guarantee: seeded_group_kfold assigns whole groups (cohorts.py:116-117) and every cohort extractant must be present in the frozen chemistry map or build_cohort raises (cohort.py:199-204). Runtime assertion: assert_fold_integrity (splits.py:124-149) checks (a) train/test index overlap, (b) inner train/validation overlap and containment in the outer train set, (c) counts of extractant, ecfp_cluster and chemotype values present on both sides and raises if the fold set's designs are a subset of {B,BP,BR,BQ} and any overlap is non-zero (:139-141), (d) publication_id overlap, asserted ONLY when the fold set is exactly {'BP'} (:142-148) -- a mixed-design call never checks publications. The gen13 runner calls it on every run (runner.py:70-71) and writes the report into run_spec.json (:77-79). gen14 dirbench.run (:144), gen15 valuebench.run_arms (:103), fewshot.evaluate (:258) and mixture.evaluate (:170) call all_folds directly and never call assert_fold_integrity (grep: only gen12, gen13 runner/tests and analysis/stage3/verify_direction/v_lookup.py do). Tests: test_design_b_folds_do_not_leak (test_gen13_invariants.py:69-77) asserts overlaps == {extractant:0, ecfp_cluster:0, chemotype:0} for design B ONLY; no gen13 test covers BP/BR/BQ (A is expected to leak chemotypes). gen16 tests/test_anchors.py:40-49 recomputes a SHA-256 over sorted test indices (and a stricter one with train indices) of all 125 folds of all five designs in a fresh subprocess and compares with results/anchors/anchors.json; gen16/results/env/ENV.md:85-88 records identical totals under PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 2. tests/test_gen6_cohorts.py:83-103 re-derives the gen5 reference algorithm, asserts group wholeness and seed dependence. gen16 tests/test_l6_cohort_audit.py:88-94 asserts the frozen chemotype map equals single-linkage Tanimoto 0.7 over the gen6 ECFP map, and :40-47 that the cohort fingerprint reproduces 4c3c6628ea0be949. gen16 tests/test_protocol.py:57-60 pins SPLIT_SEEDS.

findings.topic: (3) Exact-SMILES duplicates, homologue series, stereo/tautomer
findings.detail: Cell identity is canonical_smiles@@publication_id@@condition_key (cohort.py:153-154, 209-211; cell_id = blake2b of it); replicates are averaged per (cell, metal) (cohort.py:159-168) with counts/sd kept; 7 of 521 exact cells spanned two publications and were split by adding publication_id to the key (DATA_AUDIT.md:51-52). Ligand feature rows are looked up by canonical_smiles after drop_duplicates (features.py:101-102). Chemotype = frozen gen6 chem__supercluster = single-linkage Tanimoto >= 0.7 over the bundle ECFP (gen6/chemistry.py:406-407; gen16 test_l6_cohort_audit.py:88-94). Read-only computation on cohort_exact.parquet: 7 ECFP bit-identical groups cover 20 of the 90 extractants and every such group lies inside one chemotype, so homologues (e.g. TODGA chain variants; gen19 DATA_AUDIT.md:464 notes Morgan r=2 Tanimoto 1.0 across TODGA/TDdDGA/DHD2DGA/TDDGA/THDGA) are held out together under B/BP/BR/BQ but NOT under A (LEAKAGE_AUDIT.md:103-140 documents 49.8% of the older cohort affected by exact-extractant grouping, which is why A is 'sensitivity only'). Stereo: 6 of 90 cohort SMILES carry stereo marks; RDKit RemoveStereochemistry collapses 90 -> 88 distinct structures (one group of 3 SMILES, all chemotype sc027); RDKit TautomerEnumerator canonicalisation adds no further collapse (88). No stereo/tautomer canonicalisation is performed in gen13 code; isolation of stereoisomers is an empirical consequence of their identical fingerprint. Whether the bundle's ecfp_ bits were generated with chirality on or off is not recorded in the bundle README/manifest (grep empty); the repo's own generators (gen11/auxfeatures.py:452-454, gen11/composition.py:123) use GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048) defaults (no chirality). gen19 has an explicit stereo-free, salt-free parent key (folds/registered.py:95-99, parent_connectivity_key from descriptors/extractant_components.csv) used by its parent_structure V5 variant and component-aware hiding (cell_holdout.py:9-12, 101-108).

findings.topic: (3) Cross-publication copies: gen19 copy groups vs gen13 BP
findings.detail: gen19 builds publication groups by a union-find ladder (leakage.py:647-736): corrected DOI -> primary-source DOI -> archive duplicate_group_id -> value-matched cross-publication copies (same 6-s.f. near-duplicate key, |delta log D| <= 0.005, different g19_publication_id; cross_publication_copies at leakage.py:386, COPY_TOLERANCE_LOG_D=0.005 at :63) -> near-duplicate key (any value) -> compilation DOI. The registered V1 unit is group_cross_publication_copy (folds/io.py:60; source_holdout.py:3-5, 38-39): 139 groups with MODEL rows, 103 with >= 20 rows, 104 exact folds (83 with scored rows), 50 grouped10 folds over 5 seeds (INDEX.json V1__copy__exact / V1__copy__grouped10; DATA_AUDIT.md:328). The near-duplicate key (leakage.py:154-181) = extractant_system_key, g19_metal, g19_ox, acid_primary, solvent_key + acid M, extractant M, temperature at 6 s.f.; NA matches NA. gen19 publication ids reproduce the gen6 ids one-to-one (DATA_AUDIT.md:443; load.py:10-12), and all 58 gen13 cohort publications are present in data_audit/leakage_publication_components.csv (169 ids, 151 copy groups, 11 groups with >1 publication). Read-only join: 45 gen13 cells (5 publications, 3 copy groups, 21 extractants, 5 chemotypes) sit in multi-publication copy groups; two groups contain >= 2 gen13 publications: pub_04794d6d09 (2 pubs, 26 cells, 1 chemotype -- masked anyway by the chemotype hold-out) and pub_0af6736cb1 (2 pubs, 18 cells, 5 chemotypes). gen13's BP masks only the raw publication_id (splits.py:68, 75), so for the pub_0af6736cb1 group the sibling publication's cells in other chemotypes remain in training while the held-out cell's own publication is removed: gen13 BP does NOT account for cross-publication copies. Under the looser group_near_duplicate_key basis, 2 groups with >= 2 gen13 publications span >= 2 chemotypes and hold 96 cells. Not quantified here: how many of those 45 cells are literal value copies of a gen13 training cell (the row-level copy pair list restricted to the 5,992 bundle rows would answer it). gen19's wildcard copies (leakage.py:749-805: same key with the oxidation state wildcarded and different state label, or with the structure key dropped and different system, |delta log D| <= 0.005) are REPORTED, not guarded: 265 pairs (63 state-wildcard, 202 structure-wildcard; 123 strict), crossings per registered design e.g. V5__primary__exact 134 scored rows in 67 folds (26 strict), V1__copy__exact 20 scored rows in 11 folds (1 strict), V2 none (INDEX.json leakage_sensitivity_wildcard_copies.crossings_by_design; DATA_AUDIT.md:357-378).

findings.topic: (3) gen19 fold guards and duplicate classes
findings.detail: fold_isolation_check (leakage.py:1279-1346) always asserts: no index overlap, every label in the frame, no archive duplicate_group_id (classes A/B/C/E/F) on both sides, and no near_duplicate_key value crossing (with near_dup_value_tol only value-matched keys count). Level V1 adds no g19_publication_id on both sides; V2 no metal state / unknown-state alias (element-level option); V5 no (state, system) cell with component-aware hiding (V5_hidden_state_in_component_sharing_system); V6 forces component-aware. Guards per design: V1 via io.guard with publication_col=GROUP_COL so the publication basis is the copy group (io.py:445-481; source_holdout.py:117-124; finding VR-02); V5 guard_v5 (cell_holdout.py:466-475) and guard_v5p adds a V1 check on scored rows (:540-550); V2 guard_v2 (metal_holdout.py:77-83); V0 has no guard, partition only (random_split.py:4-9, 37-40). The group_near_duplicate_key V1 variant is checked value-blind (source_holdout.py:111-114). Archive duplicate classes in MODEL rows: 0 A/B, 10 C groups, 305 E_VALUE_CONFLICT groups (4 spanning publications) (DATA_AUDIT.md:288-303); two E groups spanning copy groups broke 5 registered V1 folds until the archive-duplicate rung was added (DATA_AUDIT.md:327-328). Fold files are content-hashed (fold_hash = SHA-256 of sorted 'role,row_id' lines; design_hash; assignment_sha256; io.py:146-174) and read_design re-derives and refuses mismatches (io.py:389-410). Registered folds pass their guards in tests/test_registered_folds.py (5 tests) and tests/test_folds.py / test_leakage.py (29 + 37 tests collected).

findings.topic: (4) No preprocessing is fitted on test rows in gen13-gen15
findings.detail: gen13 models.py: tree_pipeline = make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(median, keep_empty_features=True), ExtraTreesRegressor) (:36-43) fitted on ctx.X_train only (:198, :225, :263, :310); data bases via fit_data_basis(ctx.centred_train) (:163, :194, :394, :489); KernelCoefficientArm condition median/mean/sd from X_train (:452-455); HelperBlockArm z_median/mean/sd from training X (:591-595); CalibratedGainArm gain chosen on the inner validation block (:743-752); SelectedArm on inner split (:357-373); FitContext carries training arrays only (:46-56, docstring 'training cells only'). features.py has no fitted transform: Ipc log10 (:107-108) is a fixed, target-free map; test_features_are_target_free (test_gen13_invariants.py:56-66) proves bit-identical features under randomised log D; forbidden-token assertions on every matrix (features.py:68-71; cohort.py:64-71). amplitude_bench.load_bench computes coef for ALL cells (:82-83) by a per-cell ridge on that cell's own observed metals (basis.py:107-117) -- cell-local, no cross-cell statistic, and it is the target/oracle, not a feature. gen14 models.py: SimpleImputer, StandardScaler, QuantileTransformer, PCA all inside make_pipeline fitted on Xtr (:101-106, :143-145, :156-158, :189-197, :212-213, :265-266, :275-278); dir_threshold median from Xtr (:234); extractant_units collapses training only (:55-70). gen15: Ctx exposes the whole bench including test Y (valuebench.py:50-62); arms named O_* read test labels and are declared oracles (arms.py:119-171, module docstring :1-17); query_span_magnitude / n_metals_magnitude read only which metals the test cell measured (arms.py:77-81, 186-198), declared not oracles; _fit_magnitude_1d fill value from training median (:47); shape.py pipelines on X[tr] (:45-47, :174-178); mixture.fit_components from training (:68-93). No StandardScaler/PCA/feature selector is fitted globally anywhere on the path. docs/audits/LEAKAGE_AUDIT.md (older src/ pipeline) reached the same verdicts for items 2-9 (:60-101).

findings.topic: (5) How hyperparameters were chosen; outer-test selection of deployed numbers
findings.detail: gen13: tree hyperparameters fixed a priori (400 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2, median imputation; PRE_REGISTRATION.md:67-71; models.py:36-43) -- no tuning, so no nesting needed; the registered primary M_SELECTED picks one of six candidates per (seed, fold) on the inner-validation chemotypes (models.py:319-373; PRE_REGISTRATION.md:73-78; selections recorded in predictions/<label>/selections.csv). gen13.1 exploratory V2_ bags/gain arms and 'best observed test arm' are labelled as such and the decision report forbids quoting them (DECISION_REPORT.md:534-535). BP was introduced after the primary endpoints were scored (PRE_REGISTRATION.md:164-179). gen14: the deployed arm LOGIT_TOPO39 = dir_logistic(C=1.0, penalty l2, StandardScaler) x amp_constant (gen14/models.py:381-405, 512-515; gen15/arms.py:102-105) was selected from a sweep of 30 direction candidates and 8 amplitude priors each scored on the OUTER folds of all five designs including BP on the same five discovery seeds (GEN14_REPORT.md:160-168; scripts/g14_sweep.py:34-43). The honest alternative dir_logistic_cv (penalty chosen by chemotype-grouped inner CV, gen14/models.py:163-199) was evaluated and rejected because it scored -0.086 under BP (GEN14_REPORT.md:165); 'C = 3 and C = 10 are +0.000 to +0.007 ... C = 1 stays' (:168). Therefore the deployed BP number 0.5000794414203691 (gen16/anchors.py:23; test_anchors.py:56) is an outer-test-selected figure, defended by design-invariance (range 0.491-0.500 over five designs, GEN14_REPORT.md:71-85) rather than by nesting or withheld seeds. gen15: BLUP constants shrink=0.25, ridge=1e-3, min_pairs=20, noise_var=0.09 inherited from gen13 stage 2 (gen15/fewshot.py:42, 57-72; gen13 fewshot_stage2.py:55-80); cov_kind (empirical/smooth/blend), noise 0.04/0.20 and per-cell noise were compared on outer designs (scripts/g15_fewshot_sweep.py:36-44, mask_publication=True at :53), and support policies widest/dopt/random were compared on outer designs with union exclusion (scripts/g15_support.py:40-63), so the 'D-optimal k=3 0.1633-0.1700' (GEN15_REPORT.md:253) is also outer-selected. gen16's confirmation on five withheld seeds (commitment sha256 5a30455b..., CONFIRMATION.md:6-24; test_protocol.py:35-54; test_gen16_results.py:46-62) admitted exactly one claim, L3a G14_saved_vs_0 (CONFIRMATION.md:27-43); the zero-shot G14 BP=0.500, FLAT=0.5885062528901843 and the k-shot 0.163-0.170 / 0.231 numbers were never re-estimated on withheld seeds.

findings.topic: (6) k-shot support/query isolation: what gen13/gen15 handle
findings.detail: Handled: (a) support pairs are never scored -- gen13 fewshot.py:85 queries exclude the support pair, fewshot_stage2.py:155-157 skip it, evaluate_support_budget scores only pairs outside the design (:281); gen15 fewshot.evaluate excludes the supports of the LARGEST budget at every k so k=0..3 are scored on byte-identical pairs (fewshot.py:230-235, 339-340) and with hows= the UNION of every strategy's supports is excluded (:237-242, 339); gen16 l5_fewshot extends the union over covariance estimators (:13-16, 179-180). (b) Support selection never reads the scored cell's y: gen13 _support_widest uses metal indices only (fewshot_stage2.py:102-103), _support_random uses blake2b stable_hash (:97-99; fewshot.py:35-41), greedy_support_design uses only the covariance and the measured-metal set (:216-246); gen15 pick_support widest sorts by Z span, dopt by posterior variance reduction under cov, random by rng (fewshot.py:173-210). (c) The residual covariance is leave-chemotype-out in gen13 (fewshot_stage2.py:134-135) and leave-chemotype-out AND publication-masked in gen15 when mask_publication=True (fewshot.py:244-248, 293-305); every GEN15_REPORT §4/§5 number used it (GEN15_REPORT.md:192-195; g15_support.py:63; g15_fewshot_sweep.py:53) but scripts/g15_fewshot.py defaults MASKPUB to False unless --maskpub is passed (:44). (d) Fallback to a parametric smooth covariance when fewer than 10 residual rows remain (fewshot.py:299-300, 245-258). (e) Direction-conditional curvature stats from the training fold only (fewshot.py:270-275). (f) mixture.py prototypes and pooled covariance from training (mixture.py:68-93, 191). The gen13 stage-2 figure 0.266 (GEN14_REPORT.md:221-222) predates the fixed pair set and the publication mask; gen15's 0.231 (k=1, widest, BP, G14 prior, mask_publication) is GEN15_REPORT.md:202.

findings.topic: (6) k-shot isolation: what is NOT handled (closure, covariance provenance, noise, dependence)
findings.detail: 1. Algebraic closure of pairs within a cell: neither gen13 nor gen15 constrains supports so that query endpoints stay in different connected components of the support graph (pick_support, fewshot.py:173-210; greedy_support_design, fewshot_stage2.py:216-246). Measured on the frozen cohort with gen15's own inclusion rule (>= 4 metals, > 3 pairs; widest-3 by (-dZ, lighter index), fewshot.py:185-186, 326-330): 321 cells, 12,863 scored pairs, 963 (7.5%) are exactly determined by the three supports, and every one of the 321 cells has at least one such pair (widest-k chains endpoints: La-Lu, La-Yb, Ce-Lu imply Yb-Lu, La-Ce, Ce-Yb). Not quantified for D-optimal (needs the covariance). LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md:238 registers the component rule; it is unimplemented. 2. Covariance provenance: gen15's residual rows are OUT-OF-FOLD residuals of OTHER test cells of the same split seed (fewshot.py:285-290, 296-298). For the cell being corrected those cells are training cells, but their residuals were produced by models trained on folds that include the corrected cell, so the covariance carries second-order information from the corrected cell's own labels; the plan (§8.2, :248, :256) requires C and R from inner out-of-training predictions inside the training set, which no existing code does. The gen13 stage-2 covariance has no publication mask at all (fewshot_stage2.py:134). 3. Indefiniteness: residual_covariance zeroes entries with < 20 jointly observed cells, fills the diagonal, shrinks 0.25 toward the diagonal and adds a 1e-3 ridge (fewshot.py:57-72); nothing projects to PSD, and blup solves D cov D' + noise I directly (:104-106) with a silent fallback to the prior on LinAlgError (:107-108). The task background's gen16 finding that the covariance is indefinite and 90% intervals cover 98.8% was not re-verified here. 4. Noise model: noise_var is a scalar 0.09 (two readings at sd 0.212) applied as noise_var*I, i.e. supports are treated as independent even when they share a log D reading (fewshot.py:104, 274); per_cell_noise=True reads the TEST cell's own replicate spread repsd__<Ln> (fewshot.py:308-317) -- test-cell metadata, declared option, not label leakage, but the plan asks for R from training. 5. No Pr/Nd-specific query set or protection (plan §8.1 :232, :236); the scored set is 'all pairs minus supports' and differs from the zero-shot cohort (321 vs 521 cells; fewshot.py:326-330). 6. Scripts default: g15_fewshot.py runs without the publication mask unless --maskpub (:44); a successor copying the script defaults would drop the mask. 7. gen19 contains no few-shot / BLUP / support-pair code (grep empty), so any k-shot extension on gen19 designs must be built from gen15/fewshot.py.

findings.topic: (7) Python hash() and process-salted ordering
findings.detail: Splitters: no Python hash() anywhere in the fold path. seeded_group_kfold uses np.unique (sorted) + np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation (cohorts.py:112-117); splits.py uses set() only for membership/len and builds BQ candidates from np.unique + seeded rng.shuffle (:75-103); gen16's g16_env_check.py REVIEWED list classifies every set()/np.unique site on the frozen import path (:77-100) and records bit-identical fold-plan hashes under PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 2 (results/env/ENV.md:85-88). gen19ct: zero hash() calls; SHA-256/sha1 content hashes (folds/io.py:146-174; cell_holdout.py:126), numpy SeedSequence streams per design/stream tag (io.py:67-69, 186-188), and every permutation is over a sorted list (io.py:304-305; cell_holdout.py:286-294). Remaining hash() sites: (i) generations/gen13_separation/gen13sep/arms_stage2.py:330 `hash(row.tobytes())` in extractant_key -- bytes ARE salted per process; used by the stage-3 ExtractantBalancedArm (order-free, safe) and HierarchicalCurveArm S3_HIER / S3_EXT_LEVEL (per-extractant matrix row order follows the salted order, so ExtraTrees fits are bit-identical across processes only up to float summation order); classified UNSAFE-IN-PRINCIPLE by g16_env_check.py:78-84 and audit_numbers.py:552-556; not on the gen14/gen15 bench path (gen15.arms.g13_full calls tree_pipeline directly). (ii) generations/gen15_curve/gen15/fewshot.py:336 and generations/gen16_leads/gen16/l5_fewshot.py:169 `abs(hash((int(ci), int(seed)))) % 2**32` -- tuple of ints, unsalted in CPython (verified empirically in ENV.md:87-88), but depends on the platform hash width; only drives how='random' support draws. (iii) generations/gen15_curve/exp/decision/dec_arms.py:111 (int tuple, exploratory) and generations/gen15_curve/exp/external/class_level.py:43, unit_level.py:42 hash(tuple(np.round(r, 9))) (numeric tuples, unsalted, exploratory). Protective tests that already exist: gen16 tests/test_anchors.py:40-49 (subprocess fold hash), tests/test_gen9_reproducibility.py:123-138 (scans for bare hash() calls), tests/test_gen8_harness.py:282-326 and scripts/gen11_self_audit.py:256-271 (splits identical across PYTHONHASHSEED), gen12 tests/test_gen12_invariants.py:183. gen13 fewshot.stable_hash is blake2b (fewshot.py:35-36); cohort fingerprint uses pd.util.hash_pandas_object (deterministic, cohort.py:90-93).

findings.topic: gen19 design families relevant to a k-shot extension (V0/V1/V2/V5 and seeding)
findings.detail: gen19 keeps the five discovery seeds (io.py:56-57; INDEX.json discovery_seeds) and derives independent streams via SeedSequence([seed, STREAM_TAGS[stream], *extra]) with tags V0=0, V1_grouped=1, V5_batch=5, V5P_batch=6, V5PAIR_batch=7, inner_V1=11, inner_V2=12, inner_V5_groups=15, inner_V5_subsample=16, inner_V5_batch=17 (io.py:67-69, 186-188). V0 rows random5: sorted canonical_measurement_id permuted and dealt round-robin, 25 folds, no guard (random_split.py:18-34). V1 copy exact: leave-one-copy-group-out for groups >= 20 MODEL rows plus one REMAINDER fold (source_holdout.py:33-34, 74-89); grouped10 by seeded greedy balance (io.py:301-312). V2: 23 metal states with >= 100 rows and >= 5 systems, element-level hiding registered (metal_holdout.py:3-10, 29-30). V5: cell = (metal state, extractant_system_key), eligibility k10 p1 m3 + non-bridge, component-aware hiding of the state in every system sharing a component, exact (one fold per cell) or batched by greedy conflict colouring per seed and per selection/confirmation half (cell_holdout.py:1-41, 86-108, 434-463); V5-P hides a cell plus one copy group (:481-537); V5-PAIR scores comparable test-test row pairs generated AFTER the fold is formed from scored rows only, passing pair_isolation_check (:571-667). Selection/confirmation halves are a deterministic salted assignment independent of targets (registered.py:73-92, HALF_SALT at :32). V6_TARGET_ROWS (580 rows) are never scored in discovery or inner folds (io.py:12-14, 254-271; registered.py:54-70). Population: 12,411 MODEL rows, 10,585 scorable, Sr(III) unscored (INDEX.json population). Orientation: gen19 pairs put the heavier state first (gen19ct/evaluation/pairs.py:12-14, 173) whereas gen13 scores lighter-first (metrics.py:39-41; test_pair_rows_only_lighter_first) -- sign conventions must be flipped when joining the two.

risks.risk: Deployed/headline numbers were selected on the outer BP test folds of the same five discovery seeds (gen14 LOGIT_TOPO39 C=1 from a 30-candidate sweep; gen15 D-optimal policy and covariance kind from outer sweeps) and were never re-estimated on withheld seeds; the gen16 confirmation covered only L3a.
risks.mitigation: For the new study, pre-register the k-shot adapter, policy and covariance estimator before looking, select on the registered selection half or inner cross-fits, and re-estimate once on gen16-style committed fresh seeds (test_protocol.py:35-54 pattern). Quote the existing 0.500 / 0.163-0.170 as discovery-seed, outer-selected numbers.

risks.risk: Algebraic closure: under gen15's widest-k support rule 963 of 12,863 scored pairs (7.5%) in all 321 scored cells are exactly determined by the supports, so part of the measured-mode gain is arithmetic, not transfer; D-optimal is unquantified but unconstrained too.
risks.mitigation: Implement the recovery plan §8.1 component rule (query endpoints must remain in different connected components of the support graph, enforced at every greedy step) and report the arithmetic-recovery number separately; recompute the closure fraction for the dopt policy before trusting any k>=2 number.

risks.risk: gen13 BP masks the raw gen6 publication_id, not the cross-publication copy group: 45 gen13 cells (5 pubs, 3 copy groups) sit in multi-publication copy groups, and one group spans 5 chemotypes/18 cells, so a copied series can remain in training when BP removes the held-out cell's publication.
risks.mitigation: Add a BP variant (e.g. 'BPG') whose mask is group_cross_publication_copy from leakage_publication_components.csv; report BP and BPG side by side; quantify literal value copies among those 45 cells with gen19's cross_publication_copies on bundle rows.

risks.risk: gen15's residual covariance is built from out-of-fold residuals of other test cells of the same seed (second-order contamination by models trained on the corrected cell) and is not guaranteed positive semi-definite; the plan requires C and R estimated from inner out-of-training predictions within the training set.
risks.mitigation: Estimate the covariance from inner cross-fitted residuals inside each outer training set (publication-masked), project to PSD (eigenvalue clipping) and record the minimum eigenvalue per fold; keep gen15's estimator as a comparison arm only.

risks.risk: The publication-masked covariance is opt-in: fewshot.evaluate(mask_publication=False) is the default and scripts/g15_fewshot.py only enables it with --maskpub; a successor reusing defaults silently drops the mask.
risks.mitigation: Make mask_publication=True the only path in any new module and assert it in a test; or assert in the covariance builder that no residual row shares the corrected cell's publication (and copy group).

risks.risk: gen19's wildcard copies (state- or structure-wildcarded value matches) cross registered folds: V5-primary exact has 134 scored rows with a training-side copy (26 strict); they are reported, not guarded. Any k-shot study on gen19 designs inherits them.
risks.mitigation: Score with the existing scoring filters wildcard_copies_excluded_scoring / wildcard_copies_strict_excluded_scoring (discovery.apply_scoring_filter) as a registered sensitivity, or merge strict cross-group pairs into the publication groups before building folds.

risks.risk: Isolation assertions are not exercised on the benches that produced the deployed numbers: gen14 dirbench.run, gen15 valuebench/fewshot/mixture call all_folds without assert_fold_integrity, gen13 tests cover design B only, and the publication check fires only for pure-BP fold sets.
risks.mitigation: Add a parametrised test over all five designs asserting zero chemotype overlap (B/BP/BR/BQ), zero extractant overlap (A) and zero publication overlap (BP), and call assert_fold_integrity inside any new bench loop.

risks.risk: Design A groups on canonical SMILES and therefore lets homologues/stereoisomers with bit-identical ECFP (20 of 90 extractants) and copy-group siblings cross folds; its numbers are leak-priced sensitivities, not estimates.
risks.mitigation: Never select or quote on A; keep it only as the leak price, as PRE_REGISTRATION.md §2 already states.

risks.risk: model_seed depends only on the fold index (five values reused across seeds and designs), so seed-to-seed variation reflects the split only; tree-seed variance is never sampled.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable for comparability with gen7-gen16; if tree-seed variance matters for intervals, add a declared model-seed sweep rather than changing the formula.

risks.risk: arms_stage2.py:330 hashes bytes with Python hash() (salted per process): stage-3 S3_HIER / S3_EXT_LEVEL arms are reproducible only up to floating-point summation order across processes.
risks.mitigation: Do not reuse extractant_key; derive the extractant grouping from the cohort frame or from a blake2b of the fingerprint row. Off the gen14/gen15 bench path.

risks.risk: per_cell_noise=True reads the test cell's own replicate spread; widest/dopt supports are treated as independent measurements even when they share a log D reading; no Pr/Nd query protection exists.
risks.mitigation: Fix R from training replicate statistics (plan §8.2), model support dependence through shared log D readings, and build Q_PrNd per the plan §8.1.

open_questions: Were the bundle's ecfp_ bits generated with chirality off? Not recorded in 'dataset with 3D structures' README/manifest; the repo's own Morgan generators use defaults (no chirality). The empirical fact that stereoisomers share chemotype sc027 suggests chirality off, but it cannot be proven from this repository.

How many of the 45 gen13 cells in multi-publication copy groups are literal value copies of another gen13 cell (row-level cross_publication_copies restricted to the 5,992 bundle rows)? Only group membership was checked.
What is the algebraic-closure fraction under gen15's D-optimal policy (needs the leave-chemotype-out covariance per seed/chemotype)? Only widest-3 was quantified (7.5%).

gen16's finding that the measured-mode residual covariance is indefinite and that 90% intervals cover 98.8% (task background) was not re-verified here; the code path (residual_covariance -> blup_posterior) has no PSD projection, which is consistent with it.
Does tests/test_gen9_reproducibility.py's bare-hash() scanner cover the generations/ tree or only src/? Its file scope was not read.

Should a copy-group-aware BP (masking group_cross_publication_copy instead of the raw publication_id) be registered as a sixth design or as a BP sensitivity? gen19's preregistration_draft §2 lists the equivalent decision for wildcard copies as open.

Were any of the gen15 §4 numbers in GEN15_REPORT.md:200-207 produced by scripts/g15_fewshot.py without --maskpub (the script defaults MASKPUB=False)? The report asserts every number uses the mask (:195) but the script default contradicts it; the committed results CSV tags (TAG at :46) would settle it.

For a k-shot extension on gen19 designs: no few-shot/BLUP code exists in gen19ct; which gen19 fold family (V1 copy groups, V5 cells, V5-PAIR) is the intended analogue of gen13's BP for the support/query split, and how would support measurements be defined when the unit is a (metal state, system) cell rather than a 14-lanthanide curve?
