audits.summary: The repository has two completely separate measured-mode lineages. The pairwise log-SF lineage (gen13 stage-2 -> gen15 -> gen16 L5) is the one that matters for a new separation study: it is a BLUP on the centred 14-metal curve with a leave-chemotype-out, publication-masked residual covariance, NOISE_VAR fixed at 0.09, and three support-selection rules (widest dZ, greedy D-optimal, random). All of it lives in one 378-line module, /Users/lilshadix/PycharmProjects/ml_separator/generations/gen15_curve/gen15/fewshot.py, whose `evaluate` already implements the like-for-like ladder (the union of every strategy's k=3 support pairs is removed from scoring at every k) and the `mask_publication` fix. The second lineage is the log-D row task (gen7/gen8/gen9/gen10/gen12), which uses offset/series ridge adapters, a dozen acquisition policies and k up to 10; it shares no code with the pairwise one. A third, gen4's src/lanthanide_separation/kshot_calibration.py, is a per-extractant calibrator study on an older 34-extractant OOF cohort and is the only k-shot code anywhere that computes R2. Numbers come in three non-interchangeable pair sets, and the repository's own README says so: §4 (widest only, BP only) gives G14 0.4387 -> 0.2314 -> 0.2235 -> 0.2058 at k=0..3; §5 (common scoring set, all five designs) gives G14@doptk3 0.1633-0.1700 and NAIVE_LINE@doptk3 0.2347 under BP; §7 (training-fold covariance) gives POOLED@k3 0.1922 and MIX6meanPC@k3 0.1852. Under P1 (margin 0.02, both intervals excluding zero, p<0.05, >=4/5 seeds, LOCO-sign-stable) the contrasts that pass are: one measurement vs zero (+0.207), k=3 vs k=1, D-optimal vs widest at k=3 (+0.033-0.035, all five designs), widest vs random at k=1 (+0.10), and G14 vs NAIVE_LINE at D-optimal k=3 (+0.062-0.065, all five designs). The contrasts that fail are every "chemistry adds something once a measurement exists" comparison at k=1 (G14-NAIVE_LINE +0.008, p=0.35; G14-FLAT +0.002, p=0.72). Known defects are documented and unrepaired: the deployed residual covariance is indefinite on 100% of its 430 leave-chemotype-out estimates in every design (safe only because no pair contrast d'Sigma d is non-positive, which Ledoit-Wolf breaks catastrophically, BP MAE 34.41 at k=3), and the intervals over-cover by roughly 2.5x in width (nominal 90% covers 98.8% at k=3) because NOISE_VAR alone exceeds the realised squared error. LOWRANK2/LOWRANK3 in gen16/l5_cov.py are positive-definite on every key and are the ready-made repair. The random-support RNG is seeded with abs(hash((int(cell_index), int(seed)))) % 2**32, which is reproducible across processes only because Python salts str/bytes hashes and not int tuples - I verified this empirically - but it is exactly the pattern the repository elsewhere forbids and replaces with blake2b. k was never evaluated above 3 on the pairwise task, structurally: a cell needs more pairs than kmax and at least min_metals+1 observed metals, and the scored cohort is 84 of the 90 extractants. Nothing in the pairwise measured mode computes R2 of any kind, so all six R2 definitions in the recovery plan's §6.2 are unimplemented for this mode. No code anywhere does D-optimal restricted to a target subset Q, or a Pr/Nd-specific acquisition objective; the existing criterion always minimises posterior variance over the whole 14-metal curve. Acquisition is sequential and greedy in both gen13 and gen15, and g15_predict.py already recommends the next pair from the live posterior. Uncertainty-based acquisition exists only for the log-D task (gen8 policies) and at the corpus level (gen16 L4 UNCERT), both negative results. For a new module, the whole frozen scaffold - bench loading, Ctx, all_folds, cell_weights, basis, blup, pick_support, per_extractant/summarise, paired_contrasts - is importable, provided gen15.valuebench is imported before gen15.fewshot, because fewshot.py's gen13sep imports execute before the sys.path side effect that makes them resolvable.

findings.topic: gen15 measured mode: exact algorithm and function signatures
findings.detail: All of it is in generations/gen15_curve/gen15/fewshot.py (378 lines). Constants: N_LN=14 (fewshot.py:38), Z_VEC (fewshot.py:39), NOISE_VAR=0.09 (fewshot.py:42), documented as 2*0.212^2, two independent log D readings at the cohort's median within-replicate sd. Signatures: centred_residual(y_row, c_pred) -> ndarray (fewshot.py:48) returns observed-minus-predicted on the measured metals, centred over them, NaN elsewhere; residual_covariance(residuals, *, shrink=0.25, ridge=1e-3, min_pairs=20) (fewshot.py:57) is a pairwise-complete second moment of row-centred residual curves, entries with <20 co-measured curves set to 0, non-positive variances replaced by the median positive variance, symmetrised, shrunk 0.25 toward its own diagonal, plus ridge*I*fallback; smooth_covariance(scale=1.0, length=1.0, nugget=0.05, basis_row=None) (fewshot.py:75) is a squared-exponential kernel in standardised ionic radius used as the fallback and the 'smooth' option; blup(c_pred, cov, supports, *, noise_var=NOISE_VAR) (fewshot.py:94) builds D with rows e_a-e_b, r = y_ab - (c_pred[a]-c_pred[b]), solves S = D cov D' + noise_var*I and returns c_pred + cov D' S^-1 r, returning c_pred unchanged on LinAlgError; blup_posterior(cov, supports, *, noise_var) (fewshot.py:112) returns cov - cov D' (S^-1 D cov); pair_sd(post, a, b, *, noise_var) (fewshot.py:133) returns sqrt(d' post d + noise_var); naive_line(basis, supports) (fewshot.py:140) is least squares of y on (r[a]-r[b]) using basis row 0 only, no corpus; line_plus_curvature(basis, supports, b_heavy, b_light) (fewshot.py:152) adds the training fold's direction-conditional curvature chosen by sign(a_hat); pick_support(pairs, k, how, cov, *, rng=None, noise_var=NOISE_VAR) (fewshot.py:173) with how in {random, widest, dopt} - widest sorts by -(Z[b]-Z[a]) then p[0], dopt is greedy maximising ||cov d||^2/(d' cov d + noise_var) with a rank-1 posterior downdate post -= vv'/(d'v+noise_var) after each pick; FewShotResult dataclass (pairs, modes, seconds) at fewshot.py:216; evaluate(bench, arms, design, *, ks=(0,1,2,3), how='widest', hows=None, cov_kind='empirical', noise_var=NOISE_VAR, mask_publication=False, per_cell_noise=False, min_metals=3, seeds=None, verbose=True) -> FewShotResult at fewshot.py:223. evaluate runs three passes: (1) per fold of all_folds(design) build Ctx and the predicted 14-metal curve coef@basis for every arm, plus per-fold direction-conditional curvature means bstats, which fall back to the overall train mean when a direction has fewer than 10 well-determined training cells (fewshot.py:272-275); (2) residual curves of the FIRST arm in the dict (ref = next(iter(arms)), fewshot.py:285) define the covariance, built per (seed, chemotype, publication) key by cov_for (fewshot.py:293-305) from held-out residuals of OTHER chemotypes of the same split seed, additionally excluding rows whose publication equals the test cell's when mask_publication is set, falling back to smooth_covariance(scale=0.25, length=1.0, nugget=0.05) when fewer than 10 rows remain (fewshot.py:291, 299-300); cov_kind 'blend' is 0.5*empirical + 0.5*trace-matched smooth, anything other than 'smooth'/'blend' returns the empirical matrix; (3) per held-out cell, require len(obs) >= min_metals+1 and len(pairs) > kmax (fewshot.py:325-330), choose each strategy's kmax support order, exclude the UNION of all strategies' support pairs from scoring for every strategy and every k (fewshot.py:338-340), then for each k emit blup predictions per arm, NAIVE_LINE at k>0, LINE_PLUS_CURV only when hows is None (fewshot.py:355-358), and a predictive sd column per (strategy, k) from blup_posterior/pair_sd (fewshot.py:350, 372). Mode names are arm@<how>k<k> when hows is given and arm@k<k> otherwise. per_cell_noise replaces NOISE_VAR with clip(2*median(repsd__<metal>)^2, 0.02, 0.5) (fewshot.py:309-317).

findings.topic: The three gen15 pair sets are different populations and must not be mixed
findings.detail: Section 4 (scripts/g15_fewshot.py, how='widest', single strategy, BP only in the committed output) excludes only the widest strategy's three support pairs. Section 5 (scripts/g15_support.py, hows=('widest','dopt','random')) excludes the union of all three strategies' support pairs, which is why its k=0 column is identical across strategies (BP G14@*k0 = 0.42424 for all three) and why its G14@widestk1 (0.22605) differs from §4's G14@k1 (0.23139). Section 7 (scripts/g15_mixture.py) uses a TRAINING-FOLD covariance via gen15.mixture.fit_components, not the leave-chemotype-out one, so its POOLED@k3 = 0.1922 is not comparable with §5's 0.1700. generations/gen15_curve/README.md:90-91 states this explicitly. gen16 L5 re-ran the §5 route and had to drop 4,976 further pairs (its own union of five estimators' D-optimal supports), leaving 52,662 scored pairs under BP, which moves POOLED@doptk3 from 0.1700 to 0.1674 - a scoring-set effect, not an estimator effect.

findings.topic: Which measured-mode contrasts pass P1, per design
findings.detail: P1 is defined in gen13sep/inference.py:41-106: passes_intervals = (percentile 2.5% > 0) AND (BCa low > 0) AND p < 0.05; passes_P1 = passes_intervals AND point >= margin (0.02) AND seeds_positive >= 4 AND loco_sign_stable. PASS, §4 set, BP (results/g15_fewshot_contrasts_widest_empirical_n0.09_maskpub.csv): G14k1_vs_G14k0 +0.20735 [+0.12855,+0.26367] p=0.0, 72/84 extractants, 5/5 seeds; G14k3_vs_G14k1 +0.02561 [+0.01764,+0.03242] p=0.0; OBOTHk1_vs_G14k1 +0.04926 p=0.0. FAIL, same file: G14k1_vs_NAIVEk1 +0.00808 [-0.01046,+0.02218] p=0.3538 (45/84 improved); G14k1_vs_FLATk1 +0.00215 p=0.7232 and loco_sign_stable=False; FLATk1_vs_NAIVEk1 +0.00593 p=0.1802; G14k0_vs_FLATk0 +0.08203 [-0.00064,+0.13855] p=0.053 (the zero-shot gain itself fails P1 under this scoring set). PASS in all five designs, §5 set (results/g15_support_contrasts_empirical.csv + _BP.csv): dopt_vs_widest@k3 (+0.0350 B, +0.0346 BR, +0.0351 BQ, +0.0342 A, +0.0326 BP), widest_vs_random@k1 (+0.0991/+0.0964/+0.0983/+0.1007/+0.1026), dopt_vs_random@k1, doptk1_vs_k0 (+0.193 BP), doptk3_vs_doptk1 (+0.0613 BP), G14_vs_NAIVE@doptk3 (+0.0641/+0.0636/+0.0640/+0.0620/+0.0646). FAIL: dopt_vs_widest@k1 is NEGATIVE in all five (-0.0033 to -0.0062) - widest wins at k=1; dopt_vs_widest@k2 is +0.0129..+0.0161, passes_intervals in B/BQ/A/BP but under the margin so P1=False everywhere; G14_vs_NAIVE@doptk1 +0.0108 BP p=0.1834 (BR +0.0181 p=0.038 passes_intervals=True, P1=False on margin); G14_vs_FLAT@doptk1 +0.0025 BP p=0.7054. OBOTH_vs_G14@doptk3 passes P1 in B, A and BP (+0.0203/+0.0211/+0.0229) but not BR (+0.01995) or BQ (+0.01922), both a hair under the margin - the remaining headroom above the deployed k=3 arm is 0.019-0.023.

findings.topic: The two protocol defects gen15 fixed, and what they were worth
findings.detail: Defect 1, the ladder was not like for like: excluding only the current budget's support pairs makes each rung an easier question. GEN15_REPORT.md §4 states the fix (exclude the largest budget's support pairs at every budget). §5 quantifies the related cross-strategy version: because removing the widest-dZ pair takes the hardest pair out of the test set, the k=0 score alone moved by 0.02 between strategies before the union fix. That artefact is still visible in the committed single-strategy sweep, where G14@k0 is 0.4387 (widest), 0.4395 (dopt) and 0.4597 (random) - three different numbers for a rung that uses no measurement at all. Defect 2, the covariance could see the test cell's laboratory: design BP removes the held-out cell's publication from TRAINING, but the covariance was built from other chemotypes' held-out residuals, which may come from that same publication. The fix is the mask_publication flag (fewshot.py:296-298, docstring 244-248). It is small but real: §4 G14@k1 goes 0.23087 (unmasked, results/g15_fewshot_board_widest.csv) to 0.23139 (masked, ..._maskpub.csv), i.e. the leak was worth about 0.0005 on this arm. Every committed §4/§5 number uses the mask; g15_fewshot_sweep.py:53 and g15_uncertainty.py:93-94 hard-code mask_publication=True.

findings.topic: Defect: the deployed residual covariance is indefinite on every estimate
findings.detail: gen16 L5 measured the conditioning of the deployed estimator on the real leave-chemotype-out, publication-masked residual rows: 430 covariance keys per design, median 512 residual rows each, frac_keys_indefinite = 1.0 for POOLED in all five designs, median minimum eigenvalue -0.3167 and worst -0.4075 under design B, median -0.317/worst -0.459 under BP. It has never invalidated a published number because the BLUP never inverts Sigma - it solves D Sigma D' + noise*I - and the measured fraction of pair contrasts with d'Sigma d <= 0 is exactly 0.000 for POOLED: the negative eigendirections lie outside the pair-contrast cone. Ledoit-Wolf breaks that accident (median min eig -0.4907, 0.79% of pair contrasts non-positive, 5e-5 below -noise_var), and because greedy D-optimal maximises ||Sigma d||^2/(d'Sigma d + noise) it actively seeks those contrasts: BP MAE goes 0.2214 at k=1 to 0.6539 at k=2 to 34.41 at k=3. The same explosion occurs with the FLAT prior, so it is the covariance and not the prior. LOWRANK2 and LOWRANK3 (probabilistic PCA, gen16/l5_cov.py:115-136) are positive definite on 0% of keys indefinite, i.e. PSD everywhere, and are the only estimators that both improve MAE at k=1-2 and improve interval calibration at every k. gen16's own recommendation is to project the covariance onto the PSD cone before any future shrinkage work. No fix has been applied to gen15/gen13 code.

findings.topic: Defect: the measured-mode intervals over-cover by about 2.5x in width
findings.detail: results/L5/calibration_intervals.csv, 25 (design, arm) blocks x k=0..3, coverage pooled over the scored pairs. Deployed POOLED under BP: k=0 cover90 0.9265 (nearly honest, median |z| 0.502), k=1 0.9825, k=2 0.9846, k=3 0.9884, against pooled MAE 0.4729/0.2434/0.2096/0.1760 and RMSE 0.6844/0.3336/0.2923/0.2477. The mechanism is one constant: after a measurement the errors collapse (RMSE 0.684 -> 0.248) but the predictive sd does not (mean sd 0.656 -> 0.468), because the sd is floored by NOISE_VAR = 0.09 (sd 0.30), which by itself exceeds the realised squared error at k=3 (0.248^2 = 0.061). The registered calibration verdict is empty: better_calibrated_than_pooled_all_designs = []; LOWRANK2/LOWRANK3 beat POOLED on |cover90-0.90| at every k in all five designs (0.0810/0.0809 vs 0.0861 mean over k=1,2,3) but no arm reaches 90% coverage inside [0.85,0.95] at any k>=1. g15_uncertainty.py is the script that computes coverage, resolution and decision value, and its committed outputs (g15_uncertainty_coverage_*.csv) are NOT in the repository - only the gen16 port's are.

findings.topic: Other defects and caveats recorded against the measured mode
findings.detail: (a) gen15 §7's MIX6meanPC was never compared with the deployed route; gen16 ran that comparison and the gain survives at +0.0070 at k=3 (p<1e-4, all five designs, 5/5 seeds, LOCO-stable, 57/84 extractants under BP), three times under the 0.02 margin, so not deployable. (b) The largest sub-margin estimator effect is LOWRANK2 at k=2, +0.0151 under BP (p=0.002), which vanishes at k=3 (+0.0003, sign flips across designs) and is p=0.34 under design A. (c) HIER (chemotype-balanced covariance) is significantly WORSE at k=3 in B/BR/BQ/A (-0.0074 to -0.0097). (d) The 'ceiling 0.182' quoted in g15_predict.py's docstring is an in-sample oracle; GEN15_REPORT.md §1a and README.md:87-89 state the leave-pair-out value is 0.2736, so the measured-mode headroom quoted against O_BOTH is roughly half again too large. (e) README.md:98 records that GEN15_REPORT §7's table value 0.1865 is MIX4meanPC, while MIX6meanPC@k3 is 0.1852 in the CSV - I confirmed both numbers in g15_mixture_board_dopt.csv. (f) Ranking at k=1 is a null and the no-model line wins: gen16 L3c gives NAIVE_LINE@k1 regret 0.339 and cross-extractant Spearman 0.799 against G14@k1 0.361 and 0.772, and the registered contrast is negative on Spearman in all five designs (p 0.013-0.026). (g) g15_support_board_all.csv is not an independent run: I verified it equals the row-concatenation of g15_support_board_empirical.csv (B/BR/BQ/A) and g15_support_board_empirical_BP.csv (BP) to 0.0 maximum absolute difference across all 225 rows, and README.md:47-48 flags these three filenames as matching no current script output.

findings.topic: Random-support RNG seeding and cross-process reproducibility
findings.detail: generations/gen15_curve/gen15/fewshot.py:336 seeds per cell with np.random.default_rng(abs(hash((int(ci), int(seed)))) % (2 ** 32)), where ci is the cell's integer index into the bench frame and seed is the split seed. generations/gen16_leads/gen16/l5_fewshot.py:169 copies that line verbatim. It IS reproducible across processes, but only by accident of CPython's implementation: PYTHONHASHSEED salts str/bytes hashing, not integers or tuples of integers. I verified empirically in three separate interpreter processes - hash((17,42)) and hash((3,7)) gave identical values every time (68605531, 1211335945) while hash('abc') changed between processes (1018550582 vs 3672776333). The repository elsewhere treats this exact pattern as a defect: src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/kshot.py:48-62 documents that seeding an RNG with hash(ligand) silently broke cross-run pairing in gen8 and replaces it with blake2b; gen12eu/fewshot.py:45-47 does the same and gen12's test suite re-derives a draw in a subprocess under a different PYTHONHASHSEED (generations/gen12_eu_pred/tests/test_gen12_invariants.py:183-190). gen13sep/fewshot.py:35-41 also uses blake2b over a string key. Two further properties: the rng is consumed only by the 'random' branch of pick_support (fewshot.py:181-184), so widest and dopt are fully deterministic and strategy ordering cannot shift the random draw; and because the seed keys on the cell's positional index ci, any change to cohort row order silently changes every random support draw.

findings.topic: What k values were ever evaluated, and why k never exceeded 3 on the pairwise task
findings.detail: Pairwise log SF: gen13 stage-1 is k=1 only, five deterministic support draws per cell (gen13sep/fewshot.py:71-103, scripts/g13_fewshot.py --repeats 5). gen13 stage-2 adds a budget sweep to k_max=3 (gen13sep/fewshot_stage2.py:249-298, evaluate_support_budget(k_max=3, min_metals=4)); the committed metrics/B_primary/fewshot_stage2_budget.csv has k_measured 0..3 on 321 cells. gen15 uses ks=(0,1,2,3) as the default in fewshot.py:225 and as KS=(0,1,2,3) in all four scripts (g15_fewshot.py:49, g15_fewshot_sweep.py:33, g15_support.py:41, g15_uncertainty.py:38); mixture.py:158 likewise. Nothing on the pairwise task was ever run above k=3. The structural reason is in fewshot.py:325-330: a cell is skipped unless len(obs) >= min_metals+1 (min_metals=3, so >=4 measured metals) AND len(pairs) > kmax; raising kmax both shrinks the cohort and shrinks the held-out set each cell contributes. The scored cohort is already only 84 of the cohort's 90 extractants (n_units_mae_all=84 in every committed board). Log-D row task, for contrast: gen7 kshot_early used k=[0,1,2,3,5,8] (runs/gen7_architecture/kshot_early/summary.json); gen12 uses K_VALUES=(0,1,2,3,5) (gen12eu/fewshot.py:39); gen10's frontier tables are k=0,1,2,3,5; gen4's KShotConfig defaults to ks=(1,2,3,5,10) with k_max=10 and 20 draws (kshot_calibration.py:284-293). So k=10 exists in the programme, but only for log D on a different cohort with a different estimator.

findings.topic: Acquisition: D-optimal is sequential and whole-curve; nothing targets a subset Q
findings.detail: Sequential greedy D-optimal exists in two places with the same criterion: gen15 pick_support's dopt branch (fewshot.py:189-210) and gen13sep.fewshot_stage2.greedy_support_design(cov, pairs, k, *, noise_var=0.09) (fewshot_stage2.py:216-246). Both maximise ||Sigma d||^2 / (d' Sigma d + noise_var), which is the trace reduction of the posterior summed over the WHOLE 14-metal curve, and both apply the rank-1 downdate after each pick, so the choice is sequential and uses only the covariance and which metals the cell has - never a measured value, so it is a design a laboratory can follow before any experiment. There is NO variant anywhere that restricts the objective to a target subset Q, and no Pr/Nd-specific or pair-specific objective: the recovery plan's §8.2 requirement ('maximum expected reduction in the variance of the TARGET pairs Q, and for Pr/Nd optimise Pr/Nd uncertainty') is unimplemented. Deployment-time sequential acquisition does exist: g15_predict.py:163-165 recomputes pick_support(remaining, 1, 'dopt', post) from the CURRENT posterior, so after a supplied La/Lu it asks for a mid-series pair (GEN15_REPORT §5 reports Nd/Er). Uncertainty-based acquisition for support selection on the pairwise task does not exist - the sd columns the harness emits are only consumed by g15_uncertainty.py for coverage/resolution/decision tables. It exists in two other scopes: gen16 L4 at the corpus level (which chemotypes to measure; gen16/l4_acq.py ORDERS = RANDOM, MAXMIN, AOPT, UNCERT, with order_uncert at l4_acq.py:259 using three AOPT warm-up picks), where the registered contrast fails the five-design rule (AOPT-RANDOM sign flips: -0.012/+0.023/-0.003/+0.037/+0.050) and a featureless size-ordered refuter reproduces it; and in the log-D lineage, src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/kshot.py:252-331 (policy_max_sd, policy_min_sd, policy_max_disagreement, policy_max_predictive_variance, policy_max_variance_reduction, policy_d_optimal, policy_central_then_spread, policy_medoid, make_oracle_policy), where gen8's documented finding is that a calibrated uncertainty approximates argmin|r_i| and scores 0.780 against random's 0.709, i.e. worse than choosing blindly, because the right target is |r_i - median(r)| (src/lanthanide_separation/gen9/acquisition.py:1-40).

findings.topic: No R2 is computed anywhere in the pairwise measured mode
findings.detail: I grepped for r2 / r_squared / r2_score across generations/gen15_curve/gen15/, generations/gen15_curve/scripts/, gen13sep/fewshot.py, gen13sep/fewshot_stage2.py, gen13sep/metrics.py, gen16/l5_fewshot.py, gen16/l5_mixture.py and gen12eu/fewshot.py: zero hits. The frozen scoring function gen13sep.metrics.summarise (metrics.py:85-120) emits macro_mae_extractant, macro_mae_chemotype, macro_mae_adjacent, macro_mae_far, macro_sign_acc_strong, macro_pair_spearman and the pooled equivalents, and no R2 at all. The ONLY k-shot R2 in the repository is gen4's: src/lanthanide_separation/kshot_calibration.py:592 _guarded_r2(sse, sst, n) with R2_MIN_ROWS=15 and R2_MIN_SD=0.05 (returns NaN below either threshold), consumed as per-extractant r2 in summarise_per_extractant (line 609), pooled_r2 and macro_r2_median in _per_draw (line 631) and surfaced by summarise_grid (line 660). That is on log SF pairs of the older 34-extractant gen3/gen4 OOF cohort with a leave-extractant-out split, not the frozen gen13 cohort, and the study is explicitly exploratory and post-hoc. Consequence for a new experiment: all six R2 definitions in LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md §6.2 (R2_pooled, R2_balanced, R2_pair_macro, R2_adjacent, R2_PrNd, R2_within_system) have no implementation for the measured mode, and §9.3's success bar R2_balanced(k=3) >= 0.50 cannot currently be evaluated against any committed artefact.

findings.topic: gen13's two few-shot layers and their results
findings.detail: Layer 1, the locked S6 study (gen13sep/fewshot.py, scripts/g13_fewshot.py): adapters no_model_linear (slope through the measured pair on standardised Shannon radius), rescale (gain adjuster shrink=0.5, gated at |contrast| >= 0.3, clipped to [0,3]) and basis_shift (move along the basis direction that changes the measured contrast, lam=0.7). Support is ONE pair drawn per (cell, repeat) by blake2b stable_hash (fewshot.py:35-41), 5 repeats, min_metals=3, query = all pairs except the support. Results (metrics/B_primary/fewshot_leaderboard.csv): M_PHYSICS|basis_shift 0.3963, C_DIRECT_ROW|rescale 0.4358, M_SELECTED|rescale 0.4396, M_SELECTED|basis_shift 0.4526, any arm|no_model_linear 0.4832, M_SELECTED|zero_shot 0.4844. The REGISTERED primary S6 contrast failed both ways (bootstrap/B_primary/fewshot_contrasts.csv): basis_shift vs zero_shot +0.0318 p=0.1634, vs no_model_linear +0.0306 p=0.4728. Layer 2, stage 2 (gen13sep/fewshot_stage2.py): adapt_conditional (the single-pair BLUP, line 79), adapt_conditional_multi (line 192), greedy_support_design (line 216), evaluate_one_pair_conditional (line 106, support_design in {random, widest}), evaluate_support_budget (line 249), macro_scores (line 172); covariance leave-chemotype-out per split seed only, with NO publication mask - that is the hole gen15 closed. Numbers: B_primary widest X_ENS 0.4548 -> 0.2510 (line 0.2718), random 0.4635 -> 0.3618 (line 0.4832); BP_lean widest C_DIRECT_ROW 0.5410 -> 0.2664, M_SELECTED 0.5309 -> 0.2742, mean curve 0.6088 -> 0.2777; B_v2 widest V2_BAG_MIX3 0.4345 -> 0.2485. Budget sweep 0.4091/0.2106/0.1933/0.1674 for k=0..3 on 321 cells with >=4 metals. The model-vs-line contrast at the widest pair is already null here: C_DIRECT_ROW|widest|vs_no_model_linear +0.0054 p=0.368, M_SELECTED|widest|vs_no_model_linear -0.0024 p=0.776; with a random pair it passes (+0.0719 p=0.001). A 5x5 sensitivity sweep over (shrink, noise_var) moves the widest-pair score only between 0.2480 and 0.3060, with the defaults (0.25, 0.09) at 0.2510 and the grid optimum at 0.2480.

findings.topic: The separate log-D few-shot lineage (gen4, gen7, gen8, gen9, gen10, gen12) shares no code with the pairwise mode
findings.detail: gen4 src/lanthanide_separation/kshot_calibration.py (885 lines) is a per-extractant CALIBRATOR study on frozen OOF pair predictions: four forms (scale y~a*p, offset y~p+b, affine, trend y~a*p+b*dZ) ridge-shrunk toward the identity, five support policies (random, adjacent, widest, foreign as control, cross_condition), nested support prefixes so every k is scored on identical query rows, a union-find 'free' stratum removing query pairs that are exact arithmetic consequences of the support (determined_by_support, line 230), and rejection of degenerate fits back to the identity. Its headline (docs/results/kshot_calibration_study_20260817.md) is that in the ligand-transfer regime the model adds nothing from k>=2: at k=3 A2+TP 0.2773 against ZERO (y~b*dZ) 0.2719 and PAIRMEAN 0.2750. gen7 runs/gen7_architecture/kshot_early scores zero_shot/offset_only/no_model/affine at k=0..8 (REAL_best_tree 1.0196 -> 0.5995 offset at k=3). gen8 src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/kshot.py is the engine (K1 level, K2 level+trend, K3 response coefficients, all ridge-shrunk, DEFAULT_RIDGE=4.0) with a dozen acquisition policies; runs/gen8_architecture/cross_series/calibration_geography.md is the where-to-measure study (zero-shot 0.995, one-shot averaged 0.709, oracle level 0.480) and the cross-series transfer matrix showing off-diagonal transfer is often negative. gen9 adds a hierarchical series-local adapter (series_adapter.py) and a learned acquisition model (acquisition.py). gen10 corrects the prior estimator (gen10/adaptation.py FIXED/INNER/ML) and freezes the frontier: runs/gen10_final/headline_tables/t11_frontier.csv gives 1.036 / 0.654 / 0.559 / 0.493 / 0.441 at k=0/1/2/3/5 on 99 common ligands. gen12 gen12eu/fewshot.py is the cleanest harness in the repository (blake2b support draws, support rows never scored, byte-identical draws across arms, level/shape decomposition) with K_VALUES=(0,1,2,3,5); its result is that all of the gain is level and none is shape (level 0.990 -> 0.437, shape 0.767 -> 0.728), and gen12.2 shows one measurement erases the entire representation difference (zero-shot gap 0.024 -> 0.0007 after k=1). None of this code touches the 14-metal curve, the gen13 cohort or the five designs, so it is reusable as design precedent and nulls, not as an implementation.

findings.topic: Import conventions, verified by execution
findings.detail: Convention: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] from a module two levels inside a generation directory (gen15/valuebench.py:31, scripts/g15_predict.py:45, gen16/l4_acq.py:40), then sys.path.insert of ROOT/'generations'/'gen13_separation' and ROOT/'generations'/'gen14_direction' (valuebench.py:32-34); g15_predict.py additionally inserts gen15_curve and gen12_2_eu_pred (for gen122.coordination). Scripts instead do sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])) and then `from gen15 import fewshot as FS` (g15_fewshot.py:23-26), relying on gen15.valuebench's module-level side effect to make gen13sep and gen14 importable - arms.py:23 documents this ('inserts gen13_separation/ and gen14_direction/ on sys.path'). I verified the ordering trap by execution: with only generations/gen15_curve on sys.path, `from gen15 import fewshot` raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gen13sep', because fewshot.py's gen13sep/gen14 imports (lines 31-34) execute BEFORE its `from .valuebench import Ctx, MIN_METALS` (line 36), and gen15/__init__.py is empty (0 bytes). Importing gen15.valuebench first, then fewshot/mixture/gen13sep.*, works and resolves SPLIT_SEEDS = (104729, 130363, 155921, 196613, 262147), NOISE_VAR = 0.09, DESIGNS = ('B','BR','BQ','A','BP'), MIN_METALS = 5, RESULTS = generations/gen15_curve/results. Note that gen15.valuebench re-exports gen14.dirbench.load (valuebench.py:41), which is what every script calls as V.load(); it reads the pickled bench from generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl, which is gitignored (.gitignore:91) but PRESENT on disk, so a bench load is fast. generations/gen15_curve/models/ does not exist, so the deployed predictor's joblib payload (.gitignore:98) would have to be refitted before g15_predict.py predict can run.

findings.topic: Orientation, cohort and metric conventions a new module must match
findings.detail: gen15/fewshot.py defines the target as y[a]-y[b] with a<b over indices into LANTHANIDES, i.e. lighter-first, and dZ = Z[b]-Z[a] >= 0 (fewshot.py:328, 367); g15_predict.py:122 documents 'La/Lu=-1.31' as log D(La) - log D(Lu). The task brief says gen19 uses heavier-first orientation, so any reuse of blup/naive_line/pick_support needs an explicit sign convention at the boundary - naive_line and line_plus_curvature fit on (r[a]-r[b]) and would silently absorb a flipped convention into a_hat's sign, which then selects the wrong direction-conditional curvature in line_plus_curvature (fewshot.py:167). Metric conventions: far pairs are dZ >= 5 (metrics.py:29), strong pairs |y| >= 0.3 (metrics.py:30), adjacent includes the Nd-Sm pair that straddles promethium (metrics.py:34-36), per-cell Spearman needs >= 4 metals (metrics.py:31). The unit of inference is the extractant and the resampling block is the chemotype (inference.py:34-39); the measured-mode cohort is 84 extractants x 5 seeds in every committed board, against the cohort's 90 extractants, because of the >=4-metals and >kmax-pairs filters. Fold seeds and model seed: SPLIT_SEEDS has five entries, and Fold.model_seed = 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 (splits.py:27-29, 66-70), i.e. the model seed is a function of the fold only, independent of the split seed.

findings.topic: Recovery plan §8 versus what exists
findings.detail: LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md §8.1 requires: Q and S fixed before values are revealed with Q intersect S empty; Q defined by sorting unordered pairs on SHA-256 of 'gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B' and taking the first max(1, ceil(0.2*n_pairs)), plus Pr/Nd if measured; k=0..3 scored on the SAME Q for every model and policy; a separate Q_PrNd; and an arithmetic-closure guard - build the support graph and require each target pair's endpoints to stay in DIFFERENT components, enforced as each next support is chosen. §8.2 requires a PSD covariance ('do not copy the old indefinite matrix'), a support-noise model R that accounts for pairs sharing a source log D, solving the linear system rather than inverting, and two fixed policies: widest admissible pair, and maximum expected variance reduction of the TARGET pairs Q (Pr/Nd-optimised for the Pr/Nd target). Gap analysis: the fixed-Q hash rule is unimplemented (gen15 excludes supports from a dynamically computed held set instead, fewshot.py:338-340 - like-for-like across k, but Q depends on which pairs the policy chose, which is exactly the comparison artefact §8.1 is written to prevent). The arithmetic-closure guard is unimplemented in the pairwise lineage; the only union-find implementation in the repository is gen4's determined_by_support (kshot_calibration.py:230-280), which STRATIFIES query rows into determined/free after the fact rather than constraining the choice of support. A PSD covariance exists but only in gen16 (l5_cov.py lowrank2_cov/lowrank3_cov) and was never wired into gen15. Correlated support noise is unimplemented: both blup and blup_posterior use noise_var*I (fewshot.py:104, 125), so two support pairs sharing a log D reading are treated as independent. Q-targeted acquisition is unimplemented, as is anything Pr/Nd-specific. The plan also forbids comparing scores across the two scoring sets it defines (the zero-shot test on all pairs versus the ladder on the Q subset), which is the same trap gen15 §5 and gen16 L5 both had to fix empirically.

findings.topic: gen16's L5 port is the best template for a new measured-mode module
findings.detail: generations/gen16_leads/gen16/l5_fewshot.py (292 lines) is a copy of gen15.fewshot.evaluate with exactly two additions and one bookkeeping change, all documented in its docstring: a cov_estimators hook (name -> estimator(rows, groups) -> 14x14) so several covariance estimators are handed the SAME leave-chemotype-out, publication-masked residual rows; per-estimator D-optimal supports with the union across (strategy, estimator) excluded for every mode, so all estimators score on byte-identical pairs; a mixtures hook; and accumulation as arrays per cell instead of dicts per row, because 140+ modes x tens of thousands of pairs would not fit 8 GB as dicts. It deliberately has NO seeds argument (discovery seeds are all_folds' frozen defaults). Its verification script checks G14@doptk3 = 0.1700393901 and G14@doptk1 = 0.2313450953 under BP against gen15 before any new arm is scored, and covrun_checks.json records the k=0 invariant that all estimator arms agree to <1e-9 at k=0 (no measurement, so the covariance cannot matter). gen16/l5_fewshot.residual_rows (line 254) exposes passes 1-2 alone, which is the clean way to inspect or repair the covariance without touching any scored number. This is the pattern to copy: a hooked re-implementation plus a numeric reproduction gate against the frozen anchors.

reusable_components.what: The whole pairwise measured mode: NOISE_VAR, centred_residual, residual_covariance, smooth_covariance, blup, blup_posterior, pair_sd, naive_line, line_plus_curvature, pick_support (widest/dopt/random), FewShotResult, evaluate.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Import the primitives and write a new evaluate rather than editing this file, exactly as gen16/l5_fewshot.py did: `from gen15.fewshot import blup, blup_posterior, pair_sd, pick_support, naive_line, residual_covariance, centred_residual, NOISE_VAR, N_LN, Z_VEC`. blup/blup_posterior/pick_support are pure functions of (cov, supports, noise_var) and carry no cohort assumptions, so they are directly reusable for a Q-targeted or heavier-first study.
reusable_components.caveats: Import gen15.valuebench BEFORE gen15.fewshot or the module-level gen13sep import fails (verified: ModuleNotFoundError). The covariance is built from the FIRST arm in the arms dict only. noise_var enters as noise_var*I, so correlated supports sharing a log D are mis-modelled. Orientation is lighter-first (y[a]-y[b], a<b). pick_support's dopt objective is whole-curve, not Q-restricted. The rng seeding at line 336 uses hash() on an int tuple.

reusable_components.what: The bench: Ctx dataclass (bench, design, seed, fold, train, test, w, model_seed, fs, X, rich plus amp/cur/feat/rich_train/rich_weights/train_mean_* helpers), run_arms, board, contrasts, score, wide, DESIGNS, MIN_METALS=5, RESULTS, and the re-exported load.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen15 import valuebench as V; bench = V.load(); ctx = V.Ctx(...)`. Import this first in any new module - it performs the sys.path inserts for gen13_separation and gen14_direction. Ctx is the arm contract: arm(ctx) -> (n_test, 2) basis coefficients.
reusable_components.caveats: load() reads the gitignored pickle generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl (present on disk); if it were missing the first load rebuilds it in about a minute. V.RESULTS points at the committed results directory, so any script that writes there overwrites locked CSVs.

reusable_components.what: all_folds(frame, design=, seeds=SPLIT_SEEDS), build_folds, Fold (with model_seed property and inner train/validation indices), SPLIT_SEEDS, the BP/BR/BQ masking logic, assert_fold_integrity, fold_plan, max_train_tanimoto.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen13sep.splits import all_folds, SPLIT_SEEDS` and iterate folds exactly as fewshot.evaluate does. Designs are 'B','BR','BQ','A','BP'; BP is the one that selects.
reusable_components.caveats: Fold.model_seed = 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 depends on the fold only, not the split seed. BP/BR/BQ need publication_id and BQ additionally condition_key columns. assert_fold_integrity exists but fewshot.evaluate does not call it.

reusable_components.what: BenchData (frame, Y, basis, coef, n_obs, frames, groups, matrix(), columns()), load_bench, cell_weights(groups, n_obs, mode='balanced'), _pair_frame, LEAN_BLOCKS / CHEM_BLOCKS / ALL_BLOCKS.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen13sep.amplitude_bench import LEAN_BLOCKS, cell_weights, BenchData`. cell_weights(bench.groups[train], bench.n_obs[train]) is the frozen chemotype-balanced weighting every arm uses. bench.basis is the k x 14 physics basis, bench.Y the raw log D matrix with NaN for unmeasured metals.
reusable_components.caveats: _pair_frame is private but is the canonical long pair table builder (it is what run_arms uses); the measured-mode harness does not use it and builds its own rows, so the two tables have different columns. cell_weights has a 'reliability' mode that is NOT the locked convention.

reusable_components.what: per_extractant(pairs, arms), summarise(per_ext, pairs, arms), pair_rows_for_cell, is_adjacent, heavier_always_sign_accuracy, effective_sample_size, FAR_MIN_DZ=5, STRONG_SIGN_THRESHOLD=0.3.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen13sep.metrics import per_extractant, summarise`; pass a long pair table with columns split_seed, extractant, chemotype, cell_id, n_metals, A, B, dZ, y plus one column per arm. This is the frozen scoring pipeline - a number produced this way is comparable with every locked board.
reusable_components.caveats: Emits no R2 of any kind. macro_mae_extractant averages per extractant within a seed then over seeds. The adjacency definition folds in the Nd-Sm pair. summarise sorts by macro_mae_extractant, so row order is not arm order.

reusable_components.what: paired_contrasts(per_ext, comparisons, value='mae_all', replicates=10000, seed=8675309, margin=0.02) - chemotype-blocked paired bootstrap with percentile and BCa intervals, per-seed sign agreement, leave-one-chemotype-out stability, mde_80 = 2.80*bootstrap sd, passes_intervals and passes_P1; plus leave_one_chemotype_out and the constants REPLICATES/SEED/MARGIN/MIN_SEEDS_POSITIVE.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen13sep.inference import paired_contrasts`; comparisons is {label: (reference_arm, candidate_arm)} and positive favours the candidate. Higher-is-better metrics (sign_acc_strong, pair_spearman, curve_spearman) are negated automatically via HIGHER_IS_BETTER.
reusable_components.caveats: Returns an empty frame when fewer than two chemotype blocks are present, and silently skips a comparison whose arms are missing from per_ext - check the returned labels against the requested ones. P1 requires BOTH intervals to exclude zero AND point >= 0.02; several real effects in this programme sit under that margin.

reusable_components.what: LANTHANIDES, ATOMIC_NUMBER, SHANNON_RADIUS_CN8, physics_basis(), jorgensen_e1/e3.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen13sep.metals import LANTHANIDES, ATOMIC_NUMBER, physics_basis`. physics_basis()['radius'] is the standardised Shannon radius row that naive_line and smooth_covariance use.
reusable_components.caveats: Promethium is absent from the 14-metal list, which is why adjacency special-cases Nd-Sm.

reusable_components.what: The reference and oracle arms with the Ctx signature: flat (predict zero), mean_curve, g14 (deployed logistic direction x train mean magnitude), g13_full, o_sign, o_amp, o_both, o_curvature, o_extractant_magnitude, o_publication_magnitude, o_level, query_span_magnitude, n_metals_magnitude.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen15 import arms as A` then pass {'G14': A.g14, 'FLAT': A.flat, 'OBOTH': A.o_both} as the arms dict. FLAT is the floor every gain should be quoted over; OBOTH is the in-sample two-coefficient oracle.
reusable_components.caveats: Every O_* arm is in-sample and optimistic - the honest leave-pair-out value for O_BOTH is 0.2736, not 0.181. mean_curve (0.622 BP) is WORSE than FLAT (0.589) and must not be used as a baseline.

reusable_components.what: Components dataclass, fit_components(ctx, k, shrink_to_pooled=0.5, min_members=12), posterior(comp, supports, shift, noise_var), separation_nats (the pre-check), and its own evaluate.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Use fit_components + posterior if a prototype-mixture prior is wanted; the shift=True convention makes k=0 identical to the reference arm so every later difference is attributable to the measurement.
reusable_components.caveats: Its evaluate uses a TRAINING-FOLD covariance, not the leave-chemotype-out one, so its numbers are not comparable with §5. The full mixture arms all lose; only the pooled-covariance variant (meanPC) gains, and only by +0.002..+0.007.

reusable_components.what: Covariance estimators with a uniform hook signature estimator(rows, groups) -> 14x14: POOLED (identical to residual_covariance), LW (NaN-aware Ledoit-Wolf), LOWRANK2/LOWRANK3 (probabilistic PCA, PSD by construction), HIER (chemotype-balanced), plus pairwise_moment and two self-checks (check_pooled_matches_residual_covariance, check_lw_matches_sklearn).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: `from gen16.l5_cov import ESTIMATORS, lowrank2_cov` - lowrank2_cov is the ready-made PSD replacement the recovery plan §8.2 asks for, and it is the only estimator family that is positive definite on all 430 keys in all five designs while also improving MAE at k=1-2.
reusable_components.caveats: LW must not be used with greedy D-optimal selection (BP MAE 34.41 at k=3). LOWRANK2's advantage is a k=2 effect that vanishes and changes sign at k=3, and it is p=0.34 under design A, so it is a conditioning repair, not a performance claim.

reusable_components.what: The hooked re-implementation of gen15's evaluate (cov_estimators, mixtures, array accumulation) plus residual_rows, which exposes passes 1-2 so the residual rows handed to any estimator can be inspected without touching a scored number.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Copy this file's structure for a new module: keep the frozen route reachable with the default estimator, add hooks, and gate the run on reproducing the anchors. residual_rows is the direct way to audit or repair the covariance.
reusable_components.caveats: Hard-codes the discovery seeds (no seeds argument) by design. Its own scoring set is smaller than gen15's (52,662 pairs under BP, 4,976 fewer), so its absolute numbers differ from gen15's by about 0.003 at k=3 - within-run contrasts only.

reusable_components.what: The original pairwise BLUP: adapt_conditional (single pair), adapt_conditional_multi (k pairs), greedy_support_design (the D-optimal rule), evaluate_one_pair_conditional, evaluate_support_budget, macro_scores, plus centred_residual and residual_covariance (byte-identical to gen15's).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Useful as the independent second implementation to cross-check a new one: adapt_conditional_multi and greedy_support_design are mathematically the same as gen15's blup and pick_support('dopt') and should agree to floating point. It operates on saved curve parquets (predictions/<label>/curves/<arm>.parquet) rather than on a live bench, which is a cheaper reuse path if OOF curves already exist.
reusable_components.caveats: No publication mask - its covariance can see the test cell's laboratory, which is the leak gen15 closed. Its numbers (0.251/0.266) are on a different cohort (383 cells, 89 extractants, >=3 metals) than gen15's (84 extractants).

reusable_components.what: gen4's calibrator harness: four ridge-shrunk forms including the transitivity-preserving trend y~a*p+b*dZ, five support policies, nested prefixes so every k shares query rows, determined_by_support (union-find arithmetic-closure stratification), _guarded_r2 and the only k-shot R2 summaries in the repository, paired_extractant_bootstrap_delta, holm_adjust, transitivity_violation_rate.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: determined_by_support (line 230) is the implementation to adapt for the recovery plan's arithmetic-closure guard, and _guarded_r2 (line 592) with R2_MIN_ROWS/R2_MIN_SD is the precedent for guarded R2 reporting the plan's §6.2 demands.
reusable_components.caveats: Built for a different cohort (34 extractants, leave-extractant-out, log SF rows with condition_id) and a different estimator family - it calibrates a prediction column, it does not model the 14-metal curve. It stratifies determined query rows after the fact instead of constraining support choice. Its study is explicitly exploratory and post-hoc.

reusable_components.what: The cleanest support-draw harness in the repository: blake2b stable_hash, support_draw as a pure function of (seed, repeat, extractant, n_rows), an assertion that no support row is scored, byte-identical draws across arms, a common cohort so the learning curve is not drawn on a shrinking population, and a level/shape decomposition of the query error.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Copy stable_hash and support_draw verbatim to replace gen15's hash()-seeded RNG, and copy the common_cohort/learning_curve discipline (a curve drawn on a cohort that shrinks with k is not a learning curve).
reusable_components.caveats: It is a log-D row task with offset adapters; nothing about its estimator transfers to the pairwise curve. Its shrinkage constant is estimated from all held-out extractants including the one being adapted (about 1/915 self-contribution), which gen12.2 documents.

reusable_components.what: The numeric guard that pins the BP anchors (G14 0.5000794414203691, FLAT 0.5885062528901843) and checks the fold-plan hash in a SUBPROCESS.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Run as the pre-flight gate before trusting any new measured-mode number: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest generations/gen16_leads/tests/test_anchors.py -q -m 'not slow'. Add the measured-mode anchors (G14@doptk3 = 0.1700393901, G14@doptk1 = 0.2313450953 under BP) alongside them.
reusable_components.caveats: These are zero-shot anchors; the measured-mode anchors are only checked inside gen16's results/L5/verify.json, not by a test. I did not run this test suite (read-only audit).

risks.risk: Quoting measured-mode numbers across the three incompatible pair sets (§4 widest-only, §5 common set, §7 training-fold covariance) and producing an apparent gain or loss that is purely a scoring-set artefact. The programme has already made this mistake twice: gen15 §5 records that the first strategy comparison was inadmissible because each strategy removed its own support pairs (0.02 at k=0 alone), and gen16 L5's own union shifted POOLED@doptk3 from 0.1700 to 0.1674.
risks.mitigation: Fix one scoring set before any value is revealed, ideally the recovery plan's hash-defined Q, and score every model, every policy and every k on it. Record the pair count and the extractant count beside every number (gen15's committed boards are 84 extractants, 5 seeds). Never compare a number from one results file with a number from another without checking the n_units and the support-exclusion rule that produced it.

risks.risk: Reusing the deployed residual_covariance as-is. It is indefinite on 100% of its 430 leave-chemotype-out estimates in every design. It is currently safe only because no measurable pair contrast has d'Sigma d <= 0, which is an accident of the pair-contrast cone, not a property of the estimator. Any change - a different shrinkage target, a different basis, a different cohort, correlated noise, or a Q-restricted D-optimal criterion - can move a contrast into a negative direction, and greedy D-optimal selection actively seeks those because its objective diverges where the denominator vanishes (Ledoit-Wolf: BP MAE 34.41 at k=3).
risks.mitigation: Use a PSD estimator from gen16/l5_cov.py (lowrank2_cov or lowrank3_cov, PSD on every key) or project onto the PSD cone, which is gen16's explicit recommendation. Add a hard assertion that min(eig(Sigma)) > 0 and that d'Sigma d + noise_var > 0 for every candidate contrast before each D-optimal pick, and log the minimum eigenvalue per covariance key as covariance_conditioning.csv does.

risks.risk: Treating the measured-mode intervals as calibrated. Nominal 90% intervals cover 98.8% at k=3 and 92.6% at k=0 under BP; the programme's intervals are conservative by roughly 2.5x in width, traced to the fixed NOISE_VAR = 0.09 whose sd (0.30) alone exceeds the realised RMSE at k=3 (0.248). No arm tested reaches 90% coverage inside [0.85,0.95] at any k>=1.
risks.mitigation: Do not quote the intervals as calibrated (gen16 guardrail 6). If intervals are a deliverable, fit the measurement variance rather than fixing it - per_cell_noise already exists as a hook (fewshot.py:309-317) and the sweep shows noise 0.04 beats 0.09 and 0.20 at k=3 - and report cover50/80/90/95 with |cover90-0.90| per design and per k, as calibration_intervals.csv does.

risks.risk: Claiming that the model, the chemistry or a better representation helps once a measurement exists. Every such contrast at k=1 is null: G14-NAIVE_LINE +0.008 (p=0.35), G14-FLAT +0.002 (p=0.72), POOLED-FLAT +0.003 at k=1 under BP; gen13 saw the same (+0.0054, p=0.368 at the widest pair); gen4 saw it at k>=2 on the older cohort; gen12.2 saw a 0.024 zero-shot representation gap collapse to 0.0007 after one measurement; gen16 L3c found the corpus makes RANKING worse at k=1 in all five designs.
risks.mitigation: Install NAIVE_LINE (or the plan's regularised line) as the null at EVERY budget, not just k=0, and require the win against it at the SAME supports, which is what the recovery plan §8.2 demands. The only place the corpus has ever earned its keep is at D-optimal k=3 (+0.062..+0.065, all five designs), and that gain comes from the learned covariance, not from ligand descriptors.

risks.risk: The orientation flip. gen19 uses heavier-first; gen15/gen13 are lighter-first (y[a]-y[b] with a<b, dZ >= 0). naive_line and line_plus_curvature fit a slope on (r[a]-r[b]) and line_plus_curvature then branches on sign(a_hat) to pick the heavy or light curvature constant, so a silent convention flip inverts that branch without any error.
risks.mitigation: Canonicalise pair orientation once at the data boundary, assert dZ > 0 (or < 0) on every row entering the harness, and unit-test that blup and naive_line are equivariant under swapping a and b with y negated.

risks.risk: Cross-process reproducibility of the random-support arm. gen15 and gen16 seed with abs(hash((int(ci), int(seed)))). It happens to be stable because CPython does not salt integer hashing, but it is undocumented, depends on the cell's positional index so any cohort row-order change silently re-draws every support, and it is precisely the pattern that broke gen8's cross-run pairing.
risks.mitigation: Replace with the repository's own blake2b stable_hash keyed on stable identifiers (cell_id, split seed, repeat), as gen12eu/fewshot.py and gen13sep/fewshot.py do, and add the subprocess PYTHONHASHSEED test that generations/gen12_eu_pred/tests/test_gen12_invariants.py:183-190 already implements.

risks.risk: Arithmetic closure. Within one cell the target is exactly additive, so a query pair whose two metals are joined by support pairs is a pure arithmetic consequence of the support and needs no model. gen4 measured that about 32% of macro-weighted query rows are determined this way at k=10 (91-97% for the smallest extractants). The gen15/gen13 pairwise harness has no closure guard at all; at k=3 on a 4-metal cell the three supports can easily span the whole graph.
risks.mitigation: Implement the recovery plan's §8.1 guard - build the support graph and require each target pair's endpoints to stay in different components, enforced as each next support is chosen - and additionally report the determined/free stratification using gen4's determined_by_support as the cross-check. Report how many series are dropped for lack of admissible supports, by availability and before any value is revealed.

risks.risk: Independent-noise assumption on the supports. blup and blup_posterior use noise_var*I, so two measured separation factors sharing a source log D reading (e.g. La/Lu and La/Eu) are treated as independent, which understates their correlation and overstates the information in k>1. The recovery plan §8.2 explicitly forbids declaring that dependence zero without a sensitivity check.
risks.mitigation: Build R from the pair design (R = B diag(sigma_logD^2) B' for pairs sharing a reading) instead of noise_var*I, and run the sensitivity both ways. The existing sweep (noise 0.04/0.09/0.20 and per-cell noise) is the precedent for reporting this as a sensitivity rather than a selection.

risks.risk: Reusing in-sample oracle values as ceilings. 'ceiling 0.182' appears in the deployed predictor's own docstring, and the §4 table carries O_BOTH 0.182. The honest leave-pair-out value is 0.2736, and gen16 L2 confirmed roughly 0.044 of gen15's +0.073 curvature headroom was the oracle absorbing the noise of the pair it was scored on.
risks.mitigation: Quote only leave-pair-out oracles, and compare any new arm against the leave-pair-out oracle rather than the in-sample one. README.md:87-89 and GEN15_REPORT §1a carry the correction; gen15_curve/exp/labelerr/s4b_oracle_honesty.py is the implementation.

risks.risk: Running any committed script to regenerate a number. Every gen15 script writes into generations/gen15_curve/results/ via V.RESULTS and overwrites locked CSVs; README.md:52 warns about exactly this, and the task is read-only.
risks.mitigation: Point RESULTS at a new directory (or pass a new output root) in any new module, and never invoke the gen15/gen13 scripts to reproduce a value - read the committed CSVs, or re-derive with a separate module as gen16 did.

risks.risk: Statistical power. The programme's bar is a 0.02 margin on 84-90 extractants, and gen16 showed one registered gate (L2 curvature) had a minimum detectable effect of 0.039 - nearly twice its own registered margin - so it could not have opened at its registered effect size whatever was true. Several real measured-mode effects (MIX6meanPC +0.0070, LOWRANK2 +0.0151, dopt-vs-widest at k=2 +0.013..+0.016) sit under the margin.
risks.mitigation: Compute and report mde_80 (paired_contrasts already emits it as 2.80*bootstrap_se) for every registered contrast BEFORE the run, and state plainly when a gate is underpowered to detect its own margin. Do not reinterpret a sub-margin but significant and design-invariant effect as a pass.

risks.risk: The deployed predictor cannot currently be run: generations/gen15_curve/models/ does not exist (the joblib is gitignored), so any reuse of g15_predict.py requires refitting on the frozen corpus first, and that fit uses an all-cells covariance rather than the honest leave-chemotype-out one (documented at g15_predict.py:84-86).
risks.mitigation: Refit with scripts/g15_predict.py fit if the deployed object is needed, and keep the distinction clear: the deployment covariance is fitted on everything, while every evaluation number comes from the leave-chemotype-out, publication-masked construction.

numbers.name: NOISE_VAR (assumed variance of one measured log SF)
residual_covariance defaults
numbers.value: shrink=0.25 toward its own diagonal, ridge=1e-3 x median positive variance, min_pairs=20

numbers.name: gen15 §4 G14 ladder, BP, widest support, publication-masked
gen15 §4 LINE_PLUS_CURV, BP (worse than the plain line at every k)

open_questions: Which scoring set should a new k-shot study adopt? The recovery plan §8.1 specifies a hash-defined fixed Q (first ceil(0.2*n_pairs) by SHA-256 of 'gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B', plus Pr/Nd), which is NOT what gen15 does (gen15 scores on all pairs minus the union of the policies' supports). Adopting the plan's Q makes every committed number incomparable; adopting gen15's construction keeps comparability but leaves Q policy-dependent. I cannot determine which the user intends.

Is the arithmetic-closure guard compatible with k=3 on this cohort? The guard requires each target pair's endpoints to stay in different components of the support graph. On cells with 4-6 measured metals, three supports plus a 20% target set may leave no admissible third support. Nobody has counted how many of the 84 extractants / 521 cells survive the guard at k=3 - the plan itself says an empty or too-small set is a limitation of the mode, not a licence to weaken the guard.

Should the PSD repair be lowrank2_cov, a PSD-cone projection of the existing estimator, or a re-parametrised smooth kernel? gen16 recommends projection, implements lowrank2/3 as PSD alternatives, and notes smooth_covariance already exists as a two-parameter PSD kernel in gen15 (sweep: widest_smooth 0.2051 vs widest_empirical 0.2058 at k=3, i.e. indistinguishable). Which is chosen changes both the point estimates and the D-optimal support order, so it must be fixed in training before any value is revealed.

How should the support-noise matrix R be built? Pairs sharing a source log D reading are correlated, and the per-metal replicate spreads repsd__<metal> are in the bench frame (fewshot.py:309), so R = B diag(sigma^2) B' is constructible. Nobody has measured how much k=2 and k=3 change under correlated versus independent R.

Does the D-optimal order change materially when the objective is restricted to a target subset Q (or to Pr/Nd alone) instead of the whole 14-metal curve? This is unimplemented everywhere, and it is the plan's second required policy. The existing evidence is only suggestive: widest wins at k=1 and D-optimal from k=2, which is consistent with the first measurement pinning the ramp and later ones probing curvature.

Is Pr/Nd measurable at all in this cohort, and with what spread? Every committed measured-mode metric is a macro over all pairs or over far pairs (dZ >= 5); Pr/Nd is adjacent (dZ = 1) and the plan requires separate MAE and R2 for it. I did not verify how many of the 521 cells measure both Pr and Nd, nor the variance of log SF(Pr/Nd), and the plan itself warns R2 may be unstable at low variance.

Which R2 definitions can actually be computed on the measured mode without changing the frozen metric panel? gen13sep.metrics.summarise emits no R2, and adding one changes nothing that is already locked, but R2_within_system requires groups with at least three comparable condition sets, and nobody has counted those groups in the gen13 cohort.

Should the random-support arm be kept at all? It exists only as a lower reference (widest beats random by +0.10 at k=1), and it is the only arm that consumes the hash()-seeded RNG. Replacing the seeding with blake2b changes its numbers, so a decision is needed on whether to re-derive that reference or drop it.

Can the gen13 stage-2 route be used as an independent cross-check of a new implementation? Its adapt_conditional_multi and greedy_support_design should agree with gen15's blup and pick_support('dopt') to floating point on the same inputs, but it reads saved curve parquets under predictions/<label>/curves/ and I did not verify which labels still have those files, nor run the comparison.

Was g15_uncertainty.py ever run on the committed configuration? Its three output files (g15_uncertainty_coverage_*.csv, _decision_*, _resolution_*) are absent from generations/gen15_curve/results/, and the only committed coverage numbers come from gen16's port. If calibration is a deliverable, the gen15 script's own outputs would need regenerating, which overwrites nothing but is a run the audit could not perform.

Several result filenames in generations/gen15_curve/results/ match no current script output (README.md:47-48 flags g15_support_board_empirical_BP.csv, g15_support_board_all.csv, g15_fewshot_board_widest.csv). I established that _all is the concatenation of the other two support boards, and that g15_fewshot_board_widest.csv is the unmasked variant of the maskpub file, but the exact command lines that produced them are not recorded anywhere I could find.

audits.summary: The bundle is 5,992 rows x 2,261 columns, one row per safe_exp_id (unique), sha256 fefbefc6... pinned at gen13sep/paths.py:22 and enforced by assert_bundle_unchanged (paths.py:54-58). log_D is exactly log10(D): max |log_D - log10(D)| = 0.0 over all rows, D > 0 everywhere. It holds the 14 lanthanides La..Lu with no Pm (metals.py:11, 17-21; the bundle's lanthanide_index skips 5: Nd=4, Sm=6). A gen13 cell is canonical_smiles @@ publication_id @@ condition_key, where the condition_key joins all 64 cond__ columns (59 int8 one-hot acid/additive/diluent + 5 float continuous) with floats at 9 significant digits and NaN as the literal "NA", so missing matches missing and a value never matches missing (cohort.py:96-110, 148-154). Replicates are averaged per (cell, metal): logD__{m} = mean, nrep__{m} = count, repsd__{m} = sample sd (NaN when nrep = 1) (cohort.py:159-168). After the TODGA-name quarantine (129 rows) and three log_D <= -6 sentinels (all Pr at -12.467), the exact cohort is 521 cells with >= 2 metals, 90 extractants, 45 chemotypes, 58 publications, 3,871 rows, 14,150 all pairs, 2,348 adjacent (dZ = 1 plus Nd-Sm), 6,698 far (dZ >= 5). Gen13 orients pairs lighter-first (y = logD[a] - logD[b], a < b in La..Lu order; metrics.py:39-41, runner.py:54, PRE_REGISTRATION.md:49-50), so heavier-preferred means y < 0; gen19 orients heavier-first (state_a = larger Z then higher oxidation state, logsf_obs = y_a - y_b; pairs.py:12-14, 130-146; previous_gen.py:958-961 asserts delta_z >= 1), so the two generations' log SF differ by sign. The publication id is publication_id from runs/gen6_provenance/provenance_table.parquet (format pub_ + 10 hex, 0 NaN, 105 publications over the bundle, 58 in the cohort, DOIs in publication_references, all rows status "reconstructed"), joined one_to_one on safe_exp_id (cohort.py:142-146). Chemotype = chem__supercluster of the frozen gen6 map: single-linkage agglomeration at Tanimoto >= 0.7 over de-duplicated 2048-bit ECFP columns ecfp_0..ecfp_2047 (levels.py:66, 200-231; chemistry.py:67, 406-407), giving 98 superclusters over 190 extractants and 45 inside the cohort; the diglycolamide chemotype sc009 holds 375/521 cells, 23/90 extractants, 1,259/2,348 adjacent pairs (53.6%) and 7,210/14,150 all pairs, and TODGA alone holds 171 cells and 606 adjacent pairs (25.8%). Per-cell metal coverage is bimodal: 138 cells have 2 metals and 78 have all 14; 321 cells have >= 4, 268 >= 6, 131 >= 9, 116 >= 11 (50 extractants, 25 chemotypes, 25 publications; 52 of the 116 in sc009, 30 are TODGA). Each adjacent pair type is measured in 147 (Tm/Yb) to 234 (Nd/Sm) cells, 54-78 extractants, 26-37 chemotypes and 28-39 publications; 300 cells carry >= 2 adjacent pairs, 275 >= 3, 211 >= 5, 113 >= 11, and 129 cells carry none. Adjacent log SF (heavier minus lighter, pooled over 13 pair types) has mean +0.112, sd 0.260, mean |.| 0.190, 69.1% heavier-preferred, with per-type sd from 0.119 (Yb/Lu) to 0.386 (Nd/Sm), while the per-(cell, metal) replicate sd has median 0.302 (216 replicated combinations) and the propagated sd of an adjacent pair where both metals are replicated has median 0.556 (163 pairs): the noise floor exceeds the signal sd. The only R2 figures that exist for adjacent SF are in-sample (DATA_AUDIT.md:88-97: pair-type mean 0.113, per-extractant mean 0.163, additive 0.275, extractant x pair-type 0.680); no out-of-sample R2 of adjacent log SF exists in any gen13-19 metric file, and the recovery plan's R2_adjacent (LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md:143-154) was never executed. Two contract mismatches matter for a k-shot study: PRE_REGISTRATION.md:57 defines mae_adjacent as dZ <= 2 while metrics.py:34-36 implements dZ == 1 plus Nd-Sm, and the 64-column condition key identifies a cell's publication with 94% 1-NN accuracy (splits.py:31-34), which is why design BP removes the held-out cells' publications from training (splits.py:72-76).

findings.detail: cohort.py builds cell_key = canonical_smiles + '@@' + publication_id + '@@' + condition_key (cohort.py:153-154). condition_key = '|'.join over all 64 cond__ columns, floats formatted '.9g', NaN -> 'NA' (CONDITION_KEY_SIGNIFICANT_DIGITS = 9, cohort.py:96-110). findings.topic: (2) log D storage and log SF formation; orientation gen13 vs gen19
findings.detail: log_D = log10(D) exactly (max |log_D - log10(D)| = 0.0; max |log_D - ln(D)| = 16.2; no D <= 0). log_D over the bundle: mean 0.304, sd 1.666, min -12.47, max 4.21. Gen13: for a held-out cell, every unordered pair of observed metals (a, b) with a < b in LANTHANIDES order (La..Lu) gives y = logD[a] - logD[b], i.e. log SF = log D(lighter) - log D(heavier) (metrics.py:39-41 pair_rows_for_cell; runner.py:49-55 with dZ = Z[b] - Z[a] > 0, columns A = lighter, B = heavier). 'Heavier preferred' is y < 0 (metrics.py:121-127). PRE_REGISTRATION.md:49-50 states Z_A < Z_B, y = log D(A) - log D(B). Gen19: comparable_pairs orients state_a = heavier (larger atomic number, then higher oxidation state), logsf_obs = y_a - y_b = log D(heavier) - log D(lighter) (pairs.py:12-14, 92-155; swap at 130-132); training_ln3_pairs asserts delta_z = Z_a - Z_b >= 1 'heavier-first' (previous_gen.py:958-961); heavier_direction yardstick = sign(Z_a - Z_b) for Ln(III)-Ln(III) only, NaN otherwise (pairs.py:173-182). Hence gen19 log SF = -(gen13 log SF) for the same pair; MAE and direction accuracy are orientation-invariant, signed means are not. Gen19 also pairs across oxidation states and actinides; gen13 is Ln(III) only (metal_ox all 3 in the bundle).
evidence: dataset.parquet columns D, log_D (checked with numpy on all 5,992 rows)

findings.topic: (3) Condition matching rule for a pair
findings.detail: Gen13: two rows can contribute to the same cell (and hence a pair) only if they share canonical_smiles, publication_id and a byte-identical condition_key over all 64 cond__ columns; NaN is encoded as the string 'NA' and therefore matches NaN but never a value ('missing equals missing'); floats are rounded to 9 significant digits before joining so 10.0 and 9.9999999999 cannot split a cell (cohort.py:11-18, 96-110, 148-154). The docstring records why: requiring every condition present collapsed 190 extractants to 34 in gen2-gen4; treating 'not reported' as a value recovers 90 extractants (cohort.py:11-16). Adding publication_id split 7 of 521 exact cells that had mixed two publications (DATA_AUDIT.md:51-55). Gen19: comparable_pairs groups by [fold, g19 publication group, extractant_system_key, condition_key] and requires different known metal states; rows with a missing key, fold or state (X(?)) never pair (pairs.py:5-9, 110-117). gen19 condition_key = JSON list over 17 fields (5 categorical verbatim: acid_signature, solvent_key, modifier_name, complexant_structure_key, holdback_structure_key; 12 numeric rounded to DEFAULT_SIG = 6 significant figures incl. metal_concentration_M, phase_ratio_org_aq, contact_time_min, shaking_time_min), missing -> 'NA' ('two rows that both lack a temperature match, and a row with a temperature never matches one without') (normalize.py:65, 133-145, 419-441). So the two generations agree on the missing-equals-missing rule but differ in key fields (64 one-hot columns at 9 s.f. vs 17 normalised fields at 6 s.f.), and gen19 draws rows from the larger SAFE archive (16,770 rows; 7,858 distinct condition keys) of which the bundle is a strict subset (gen19 DATA_AUDIT.md section 15).

findings.topic: (5) Chemotype assignment algorithm
findings.detail: cohort.py:199-205 maps extractant -> chem__supercluster (chemotype), chem__ecfp_cluster (ecfp_cluster), chem__family (chem_family) from the frozen map runs/gen7_architecture/cache/chemistry_map.parquet (190 rows x 40 columns; raises if any cohort extractant is unmapped). The map is built by src/lanthanide_separation/gen6/chemistry.py build_chemistry_map (lines 376-536) calling levels.tanimoto_cluster_labels (levels.py:200-231): fingerprint = the bundle's binary ecfp_0..ecfp_2047 columns (2,048 bits; 1,383 constant over the 190 extractants, 1,623 constant over the 90 cohort extractants, which is DATA_AUDIT.md:108's figure); bit-identical fingerprints are first merged (ecfp_cluster = sha1 of the bit vector, chemistry.py:654); dense Tanimoto = |a&b| / (|a|+|b|-|a&b|); dist = 1 - Tanimoto; scipy linkage(method='single') and fcluster(t = 1 - 0.7, criterion='distance'), i.e. single-linkage agglomeration at Tanimoto >= 0.7 (TANIMOTO_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD = 0.7 at levels.py:66; DEFAULT_SUPERCLUSTER_THRESHOLD at chemistry.py:67; chemistry.py:355-360 warns the cut must be expressed as 1 - 0.7 = 0.30000000000000004 or 98 groups become a different number). Labels are renumbered sc000.. by the alphabetically first member SMILES (chemistry.py:96-114). Result: 98 superclusters over 190 extractants (80 singletons; largest sc009 = 51 extractants, 48 diglycolamide + 3 amide_other), 164 ecfp clusters; the cohort carries 45 chemotypes and 77 ecfp clusters. chem__family comes from rule-ordered motif counts (FAMILY_ORDER, chemistry.py:78-88): bundle 81 diglycolamide, 41 n_heterocyclic_polydentate, 28 amide_other, 11 phosphoryl, 11 malonamide, 8 sulfur_donor, 4 podand_ether, 3 other, 3 hydroxyl_acid. ECFP generation parameters (radius, bit size) are NOT recorded in bundle_manifest.json or the bundle README; gen11's own recomputation says GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048) (gen11/auxfeatures.py:22) but that is not provenance for the bundle columns.

findings.topic: (8) Existing noise-floor, variance and R2 figures for adjacent log SF
findings.detail: Variance decomposition: log D variance 89% between (extractant x condition), 11% along the Ln axis (within-cell variance 0.313 of total 2.776) (DATA_AUDIT.md:63-64). Adjacent (dZ = 1, n = 2,115, lighter-first sign convention): mean +0.089 heavier-preferred, sd 0.231, mean |.| 0.167, 68% heavy-preferred; per-type sign consistency 50% (Er-Tm, Yb-Lu, Eu-Gd) to 88% (Gd-Tb) (DATA_AUDIT.md:65-67). Recomputed here on the 13 types incl. Nd/Sm (heavier minus lighter): n 2,348, mean +0.1115, sd 0.2602, mean |.| 0.1895, 69.1% > 0. Replicate noise floor: within-replicate sd of log D median 0.237 / mean 0.419 on the bundle (313 combinations), median 0.302 on the frozen cohort (216 combinations), so one adjacent log SF carries noise of order sqrt(2) x 0.237 = 0.34 (DATA_AUDIT.md:75-83); half-vs-half pairwise MAE 0.60 on the 9 extractants with replicated pairs (DATA_AUDIT.md:80-83; DECISION_REPORT.md:96-99). Recomputed: adjacent pairs with both metals replicated = 163, median sqrt(sd_a^2 + sd_b^2) = 0.556, mean 0.671. In-sample adjacent R2 (the only R2 figures that exist for adjacent SF): predict-0 MAE 0.167; per pair-type mean MAE 0.141, R2 0.113; per-extractant mean MAE 0.138, R2 0.163; additive extractant + pair-type R2 0.275; (extractant x pair-type) mean R2 0.680 with 764 groups => >= 32% of adjacent-SF variance is condition/replicate residual even knowing extractant and pair; 'heavier always' sign rule 0.681 accuracy (DATA_AUDIT.md:88-97). Out-of-sample adjacent MAE (design B, extractant-macro, 5 seeds): B0_ZERO 0.207, B1_MEAN_CURVE 0.210, B2_PAIRMEAN 0.203, M_SELECTED 0.190, best exploratory 0.182, B4_HEAVIER_ALWAYS 0.230 (DECISION_REPORT.md:103-115); 'Do not read adjacent-pair MAEs as skill: 0.18-0.19 sits at the replicate noise floor' (DECISION_REPORT.md:536-537). Gen15 WLS calibration R^2 over ALL pairs (not adjacent-specific), design BP: G14 0.261, G14_TIED 0.304, G13_FULL 0.124, MEAN_CURVE 0.003, HEAVIER_ALWAYS 0.058, in-sample oracle O_BOTH 0.905 (gen15_curve/exp/decision/REPORT.md:520-543). Gen15 measured mode: residual covariance indefinite in 100% of 430 estimates; nominal 90% intervals cover 98.8% at k = 3 (gen15_curve/README.md:96-97). Gen17: median replicate sd of log D 0.333, |delta a| noise floor 0.130 (gen17_pairdiff/results/g17_summary.txt:17-20). No out-of-sample R2 of adjacent log SF exists in any gen13-19 metric file: the only 'r2' hits under gen13 metrics/ are 'cr2' cluster-robust columns (per_extractant_wildcluster.csv) and quadratic-fit R2 of curves (analysis/stage2/d1_curve_atlas). LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md:143-168 defines six R2 kinds incl. R2_adjacent = R2_balanced on adjacent lanthanides and R2_PrNd, and sections 8.1-8.2 (lines 226-262) fix the k-shot protocol (SHA-256 of 'gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B' selects Q = first max(1, ceil(0.2 n_pairs)) pairs, Pr/Nd always added; support graph must keep each query's endpoints in different components; BLUP update f_post = f_prior + C B^T (B C B^T + R)^-1 (y - B f_prior)); none of it has been run.

findings.topic: Hold-out design BP and the publication fingerprint
findings.detail: GROUP_COLUMNS: B/BP/BR/BQ group by chemotype, A by extractant (splits.py:30). BP = chemotype hold-out plus a publication mask: every training cell whose publication_id appears among the held-out cells is dropped, because the 64 condition columns identify a cell's publication with 94% 1-NN accuracy (splits.py:31-35, 72-76); inner validation is re-dealt on the masked training set. BR drops the same number of random training cells; BQ drops whole random training publications matched on cells and condition series (splits.py:36-44, 82-95). assert_fold_integrity raises if BP leaks a publication (splits.py:143-148). Seeds (104729, 130363, 155921, 196613, 262147), 5 outer folds, 4 inner, model seed = 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 (splits.py:24-29, 58-60). Under BP the diglycolamide fold trains on 103 cells (DECISION_REPORT.md:94-95).

findings.topic: Code run (read-only pandas) that produced the counts
findings.detail: LN = ('La','Ce','Pr','Nd','Sm','Eu','Gd','Tb','Dy','Ho','Er','Tm','Yb','Lu'); c = pd.read_parquet('generations/gen13_separation/manifests/cohort_exact.parquet'); M = c[[f'logD__{m}' for m in LN]].to_numpy(float); present = ~np.isnan(M); n_metals distribution = c.n_metals.value_counts(); for k in thresholds: mask = c.n_metals >= k -> mask.sum(), c.loc[mask,'extractant'].nunique(), 'chemotype', 'publication_id'. Adjacent: adj = [(LN[i], LN[i+1]) for i in range(13)]; for (a,b): ia, ib = LN.index(a), LN.index(b); mask = present[:,ia] & present[:,ib]; d = M[mask,ib] - M[mask,ia] (heavier minus lighter); counts = mask.sum(), nunique of extractant/chemotype/publication_id on c[mask]; d.mean(), d.std(ddof=1), abs(d).mean(), (d>0).mean(). nadj per cell = sum over the 13 masks; cells with >= k adjacent = (nadj >= k).sum() plus nunique of extractant/chemotype/publication_id. All pairs = sum over cells of n(n-1)/2 with n = present.sum(1) = 14,150; far = sum over (i<j) with Z[j]-Z[i] >= 5 of (present[:,i] & present[:,j]).sum() = 6,698. Replicates: rep = c[[f'repsd__{m}']].to_numpy(); nrep likewise; (nrep > 1).sum() = 216; np.nanmedian(rep) = 0.3023; propagated adjacent sd = sqrt(rep[:,ia]**2 + rep[:,ib]**2) where both finite (163 pairs). Fingerprint: cols = sorted(c.columns minus 'safe_exp_ids'); blake2b(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(c[cols], index=False).to_numpy().tobytes(), digest_size=8).hexdigest() = '4c3c6628ea0be949'. Bundle: df = pd.read_parquet(dataset.parquet); np.nanmax(np.abs(df.log_D - np.log10(df.D))) = 0.0; df.metal.value_counts(); (df.log_D <= -6).sum() = 3. Provenance: p = pd.read_parquet(provenance_table.parquet); p.publication_id.isna().sum() = 0, nunique = 105; merge with bundle on safe_exp_id validate='one_to_one'. Chemistry map: ch.chem__supercluster.nunique() = 98, value_counts().head(). gen19 pairs: p = pd.read_csv(V5PAIR__primary__cell_pairs.csv); p[p.yardstick_or_arm=='B0'].groupby(['half','category_class']).size() and .n_pairs.sum(); adjacent subset via atomic numbers parsed from state_a/state_b.
