risks.risk: Sign convention clash: gen13 pairs are lighter-first (y = log D(lighter) - log D(heavier)); gen19 pairs are heavier-first. Any k-shot study that mixes gen13 cells/metrics with gen19 pair code, or that quotes a signed mean, will silently flip signs.
risks.mitigation: Declare one orientation in the study's pre-registration and assert it in code (as previous_gen.py:958-961 does); record which convention each imported number uses; use orientation-invariant metrics (MAE, direction accuracy) for cross-generation comparison.

risks.risk: The adjacent-pair contract is ambiguous: PRE_REGISTRATION.md:57 says dZ <= 2 (Nd-Sm included) while metrics.py:34-36 implements dZ == 1 plus Nd-Sm; all published adjacent counts (2,348) and MAEs follow the code.
risks.mitigation: Fix the definition explicitly (dZ == 1 plus Nd-Sm is what every stored number uses) and cite metrics.py:34-36 rather than the pre-registration table.

risks.risk: Adjacent log SF signal sd (0.26 pooled; 0.12-0.39 per type) is below the replicate noise floor of a single pair (median per-(cell,metal) sd 0.302; propagated adjacent sd median 0.556 on the 163 pairs where both metals are replicated); in-sample (extractant x pair-type) means leave >= 32% unexplained. A k-shot gain on adjacent pairs can be smaller than the floor and still look significant if pairs are treated as independent.
risks.mitigation: Report the floor beside every adjacent metric (DATA_AUDIT.md:83-86 rule); resample chemotypes and publications, not pairs; evaluate far pairs and all pairs as primary; treat adjacent and Pr/Nd as secondary with an explicit noise-floor comparison.

risks.risk: Diglycolamide dominance: sc009 holds 72% of cells, 53.6% of adjacent pairs and 52 of the 116 cells with >= 11 metals; TODGA alone is 171 cells / 25.8% of adjacent pairs; Kish n_eff = 11.7 chemotypes; 81 of 90 extractants come from one publication. Pooled metrics and k-shot supports drawn per cell will be TODGA/DGA statements.
risks.mitigation: Use extractant-macro and chemotype-macro aggregation; cap or stratify sc009; report the sc009-held-out fold separately (it trains on 103 cells under BP).

risks.risk: k = 10 support with a held-out adjacent query needs >= 11 measured metals: only 116 cells (50 extractants, 25 chemotypes, 25 publications) qualify, 113 of them with >= 11 adjacent pairs, 78 with all 14; 30 are TODGA cells. The k-ladder at high k is therefore a 25-chemotype study and the arithmetic-closure rule (recovery plan section 8.1) further restricts admissible supports.
risks.mitigation: Pre-compute the admissible-support count per cell for each k before fixing the ladder; publish the number of cells/extractants/chemotypes lost at each k (the plan at lines 234-236 requires this); consider k <= 3 as the headline and k = 10 as a sensitivity.

risks.risk: The 64-column condition key is a laboratory fingerprint (94% 1-NN publication identification, splits.py:31-34); design B numbers overstate new-laboratory performance (DECISION_REPORT.md:530-534). Any new split that does not mask the held-out publications inherits this leak, and the gen13 'series' sensitivity shows identical recorded conditions can hide different experiment series (597 vs 521 cells).
risks.mitigation: Use design BP (or gen19's publication-group pairing) as the selecting design; never report design B as the headline; keep key_mode=series as a sensitivity.

risks.risk: Provenance of the ECFP bit columns (radius, bit size) is not documented in bundle_manifest.json or the README; the chemotype map depends on these exact 2,048 columns. Re-generating fingerprints with a different radius would change the 98/45 chemotype partition.

open_questions: Which orientation should the new study adopt: gen13 lighter-first (y < 0 = heavier preferred) or gen19 heavier-first? Every imported signed number must carry the answer.

Is the adjacent-pair contract dZ == 1 plus Nd-Sm (metrics.py:34-36, all stored numbers) or dZ <= 2 (PRE_REGISTRATION.md:57)? Should Nd/Sm remain 'adjacent' given its sd (0.386) is the largest of all 13 types?
What radius / bit size generated the bundle's ecfp_0..ecfp_2047 columns? Not recorded in bundle_manifest.json or README; only gen11's own recomputation says radius 2 / 2048.

How was publication_id reconstructed (all rows carry status 'reconstructed')? The method lives outside this repository (memory: sibling dataset-builder repo); the 7-of-521 publication-mixed cells were split, but 'Only 8 exact cells in the whole bundle cross a publication' (DATA_AUDIT.md:52-53) cannot be re-derived here without the untracked scripts/audit/ scripts.
Why does DATA_AUDIT.md:65 report 2,115 dZ = 1 adjacent pairs when the frozen cohort gives 2,114? Likely the pre-quarantine prototype, but the audit scripts are untracked.

Should the k-shot study run on the gen13 bundle cohort (521 cells) or on gen19's SAFE archive (515 additional Ln MODEL rows, different condition key, different publication partition)? Sections (6)-(7) would need re-deriving for the archive.

How should pair noise be modelled for supports? Only 163 adjacent pairs have both metals replicated (propagated sd median 0.556), so a per-pair R from repsd__ columns is available for < 7% of adjacent pairs.

For k = 10 supports only 116 cells / 25 chemotypes qualify and the arithmetic-closure rule removes more: what is the admissible-support count per cell per k under the recovery plan's rule (section 8.1), and is the resulting ladder still a multi-chemotype statement?

Is there any out-of-sample R2 of adjacent log SF anywhere outside the repository (e.g. the HANDOFF report or ChatGPT exchanges)? None exists in committed gen13-19 metric files; the recovery plan's R2_adjacent has never been computed.

audits.summary: Every generation from gen12 on lives in its own directory under generations/ with a uniquely named package (gen12eu, gen122, gen13sep, gen14, gen15, gen16, gen18proc, gen19ct), scripts/, tests/, manifests/ and committed small result tables, while bulk artefacts are gitignored and digested (generations/README.md:124-150). The recovery plan that motivates the new k-shot study prescribes the directory name generations/gen20_separation/ with a fixed file contract (README.md, protocol.json, DATA_AUDIT.md, PLAN_FROZEN.md, gen20sep/, scripts/, tests/, manifests/, results/<run_id>/{pair_predictions.parquet, support_pairs.parquet, metrics.csv, comparisons.csv, per_pair.csv, per_group.csv, missing_or_failed.csv, runtime.json, REPORT.md}) (LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md:333-357); the task's 'gen20_kshot' name is not in any document. The sys.path convention is uniform: a script or test inserts its own generation root at sys.path[0] via Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], and a package's paths/bootstrap module inserts the earlier generations it imports (gen13sep/paths.py:13-17, gen14/dirbench.py:36-38, gen15/valuebench.py:31-34, gen16/bootstrap.py:20-25, gen19ct/paths.py:75-79), so no PYTHONPATH is needed for tests although gen19 and gen12 scripts document PYTHONPATH=generations/<gen>. The richest provenance machinery to reuse is gen19ct/manifest.py's Run context manager (deterministic manifests/<script>.json with git HEAD, seed, arguments, archive SHA-256 and binary+LF-normalised digests of every input/output, plus volatile run_info/<script>.json with versions, hardware and runtime) together with gen19ct/paths.py digests()/matches(), the seal script g19_seal_prereg.py and the digest registry gen19ct/evaluation/registry.py. Pre-registration sealing is a SHA-256 footer over everything above it (gen16: g16_prereg_hash.py; gen19: g19_seal_prereg.py with CRLF/BOM normalisation, readiness gates and dated POST-HOC addenda below the footer), and both generations commit a confirmation-seed digest before any discovery run: gen16 with a public hash rule (seeds recomputable; commitment 5a30455b...), gen19 with secrets-drawn seeds in a store outside the repository (commitment 65e8ae8c...), a once-only lock and seed scrubbing to opaque indices i1..i5. The gen14 bench cache generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl exists locally (10.9 MB, built 2026-10-14 16:59, gitignored) so the fast gen16 anchor tests should take about 30 s (fold hash 5 s plus one BP value board 15 s); the slow G13_ET_TOPO39 anchor adds about 16 s. Known failures on this macOS machine are the two gen16 L6 cohort-fingerprint tests (exact rebuild 854171b03411d901 vs frozen 4c3c6628ea0be949) and, in checkouts without runs/gen9_shape/curves/curve_membership.parquet, two gen9 root tests (README.md:176-181); that parquet is present on this machine today. All seven generation suites collect cleanly (13/23/23/12/42/247/886 tests), markers are 'slow' (pyproject.toml:34-37, gen19 conftest) plus gen18's 'validation' and gen19's 'real_registry', and gen19 adds -p no:cacheprovider because its tests must leave the tree byte-identical. There is no Makefile and no script literally named run_all inside the repository's generations; the single-command precedents are gen12's scripts/gen12_finalise.sh (re-derive every table, manifest and test from stored predictions), gen19's scripts/g19_run_phaseAB.py (ordered subprocess steps, --determinism double run, manifest verification) and the sibling builder's dataset_all_metals/scripts/run_all.py. Environment pinning is loose in pyproject.toml, exact only in requirements-gen3.txt (a Linux cluster reference), and the local Mac stack (Python 3.13.0, numpy 2.5.1, scipy 1.18.0, torch 2.13.0, rdkit 2026.03.5) differs from the Windows clone that computed gen13-gen19 (Python 3.14.5, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, torch 2.14.0+cpu, rdkit 2026.03.6); gen12/gen12.2 were computed on this Mac with today's versions. The recovery plan's compute cap is 12 h total compute on one host, at most 2 worker processes and 4 compute threads with no nested parallelism, with a staged 1+2+3+4+2 h table and a cut order (plan:313-325); precedents are gen16's LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT=2 and gen19's torch.set_num_threads(2), MAX_WORKERS=2 and a 60 h wall-clock ledger. Cluster jobs are the user's (slurm/ wrappers from gen2-gen6, START_HERE.md:580, memory note); nothing after gen6 used the cluster. A new gen20 directory currently has no gitignore cover at all, so every parquet it writes would be committable unless it ships its own nested .gitignore plus a MANIFEST.sha256 as gen16/gen18/gen19 do.

findings.topic: (1a) Directory layout a new generation must follow
findings.detail: The shared layout for pre-registered generations is: README.md (orientation, reading order, how to run), DATA_AUDIT.md (written before any model is fitted), PRE_REGISTRATION.md (frozen; later addenda dated), DECISION_REPORT.md, <package>/ (uniquely named library), scripts/ (one runner per phase), tests/ (pre-registered invariants, executable), config/ manifests/ splits/ features/ predictions/ metrics/ bootstrap/ headline_tables/ figures/ analysis/. Brief-driven generations (gen16_leads, gen19) replace DECISION_REPORT with START_HERE/STATUS/REFUTATION_LOG/CONFIRMATION or GEN19_REPORT.md + SUMMARY.md + decisions/Dnn_<topic>.md, and keep a sealed pre-registration. gen19's explicit conventions: unique package name so several generations can share sys.path; capitalised human documents, lower-case sealed `preregistration.md` + `manifests/prereg_sha256.txt`; one loader with derived columns prefixed by the generation tag; every script wrapped in a manifest Run; excluded artefacts digested never promised; writers write_csv/write_json/write_text with LF. A new generation must also get a row in the generations/README.md table (Directory | Dates | Question | Verdict | Status | Entry document | Tests command) and an edge in the dependency graph. The recovery plan names the directory generations/gen20_separation/ and fixes its contents (README.md, protocol.json with data versions/splits/weights/models/thresholds/budget, DATA_AUDIT.md, PLAN_FROZEN.md with date + protocol hash, gen20sep/ with pairs/splits/metrics/baselines/models/calibration, scripts/ audit/pilot/evaluate/report/predict, tests/, manifests/ with provenance+seeds+costs, results/<run_id>/ with pair_predictions.parquet, support_pairs.parquet, metrics.csv, comparisons.csv, per_pair.csv, per_group.csv, missing_or_failed.csv, runtime.json, REPORT.md) and requires that report tables be recomputable from the prediction table without training. The task text's name 'gen20_kshot' appears nowhere in the repository.
evidence: generations/README.md:124-150 (Layout inside a generation + deviations table)
LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md:359 (prediction table required columns; report recomputed from predictions)

findings.topic: (1b) sys.path and interpreter convention
findings.detail: Scripts run from the repository root as `.venv/bin/python generations/<gen>/scripts/<script>.py`; docstrings written on the Windows clone show `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`. Each script inserts its own generation directory: `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))` (gen19 scripts, gen13 scripts/tests). The package's paths/bootstrap module inserts earlier generations: gen13sep/paths.py computes GEN13_ROOT = parents[1], REPO_ROOT = GEN13_ROOT.parent.parent and inserts REPO_ROOT/src; gen14/dirbench.py ROOT = parents[3] and inserts generations/gen13_separation; gen15/valuebench.py inserts gen13 and gen14; gen16/bootstrap.py inserts gen15, gen14, gen13 (and sets LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT=2); gen19ct/paths.py.add_gen18_to_path() inserts gen18_process, gen13_separation and src. Tests: gen19 and gen18 use tests/conftest.py to insert the generation root and register markers; gen12/gen12.2/gen13/gen16 do it at the top of each test module. The relocation test proves each paths module in a subprocess with the generation dir first on sys.path and PYTHONPATH removed. Package names must be unique: gen16_leads and gen16_protocol both use `gen16` and therefore cannot share one sys.path. gen12 and gen19 docstrings additionally set PYTHONPATH=generations/<gen> and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 for scripts, but the README states no PYTHONPATH is needed for any test command. Root tests need PYTHONPATH=src.
evidence: generations/README.md:49-52 (no PYTHONPATH; paths modules add src/)

findings.topic: (2c) What gen19 recorded and the helpers to reuse
findings.detail: gen19ct/manifest.py: `with Run(name, args=..., seed=..., extra=...) as run: run.inputs(...); run.outputs(...)` writes manifests/<name>.json {schema 'gen19.manifest.v1', script, git_head (git rev-parse HEAD, None if git missing), seed, arguments (Paths as posix), archive_master_sha256 (pinned constant 7b329793...), inputs/outputs [{path repo-relative POSIX, sha256, sha256_lf, bytes}] sorted, plus extra} and manifests/run_info/<name>.json {date_utc, runtime_s, python, platform, processor, cpu_count, packages{numpy,pandas,scipy,sklearn,rdkit,catboost,xgboost,torch,networkx}} kept separate so wall-clock never breaks byte identity; write_json is atomic (tmp + os.replace), strict JSON (NaN→null), sorted keys, indent 2, LF; write_csv LF index=False %.6g. gen19ct/paths.py: digests() returns binary sha256 + LF-normalised sha256 for TEXT_SUFFIXES, matches() accepts either (brief §24 CRLF rule), rel() enforces repo-relative POSIX. Fold assignments: folds/<design>__<scheme>.parquet + .json + INDEX.json (committed, 9.9 MB); withheld-seed designs under evaluation/confirmation/folds/ (committed, seed index not value). Hyperparameters and model version: every fold record JSON (gitignored) carries fold digest, resume digest, below-footer prereg digest, addenda digest, code digest and registry stage; the discovery manifest records code_sha256 {combined, parts (42 files)}, plan_state, prereg_gate, discovery_seeds, budget_wall_clock and ledger; manifests/digest_registry.json pins per stage {below_footer_sha256, code_digest, git_head, addenda_count, registered_utc, source} with a code_changes log (56 entries) and superseded entries; records are verified against the registry, never live code. Prediction files: per-fold parquet records gitignored and digested line by line in evaluation/{discovery,confirmation}/MANIFEST.sha256 (3,901 and 7,930 lines) by scripts/g19_manifest_discovery.py (--check also fails if a listed file is not actually gitignored). Report numbers: tables/report_numbers.csv (printed, raw_value, source_path, source_key, kind, rule; 804 rows) re-resolved after writing by g19_build_report.py (exit 3 on mismatch); tables/claims.json is the machine-readable verdict table. Determinism proof: scripts/g19_run_phaseAB.py --determinism, record manifests/phaseAB_determinism.json (66/66 identical, PYTHONHASHSEED unset). Brief §23 lists the required tracking fields: git commit, dataset hash, fold hash, feature version, model version, random seed, hyperparameters, training date, metrics, hardware, runtime.

findings.topic: (3a) gen16 sealing and confirmation mechanics
findings.detail: PRE_REGISTRATION.md ends with two lines `---` and `SHA-256 of every byte above the preceding '---' line: <hex>`; g16_prereg_hash.py computes sha256(body.encode('utf-8')) where body is the text with the footer stripped, `--seal` appends the footer (refuses if already sealed), `--reseal` re-seals after an addendum placed ABOVE the footer (the addendum must quote the previous digest), and running with no flag verifies and exits 1 on mismatch. Recorded digest d004c303...; the file states it was frozen 2026-09-10 after Phase 0 and that the brief is commit df63929. Seed commitment: a public rule seed_i = int(sha256('gen16-confirmation-seed-{i}').hexdigest()[:8],16) % 900000 + 100000, skipping collisions with the five discovery seeds, first five sorted; commitment sha256(json.dumps(sorted(seeds))) = 5a30455b... quoted in §0; seeds kept in a JSON file outside the repository. g16_confirm.py --seeds-file verifies the commitment AND recomputes the rule, loads gen16/claims.py (≤5 claims), writes results/confirmation/ and a marker CONFIRMATION_RUN_ONCE.json that refuses a second run unless --force (then a `_rerun_<timestamp>` suffix, never overwriting). g16_audit_seeds.py walks the AST of every file and fails if any file outside {scripts/g16_confirm.py, scripts/g16_audit_seeds.py, gen16/claims.py} passes `seeds=` or contains a confirmation-seed literal; tests/test_protocol.py checks the seal, the audit and that the rule hashes to the commitment. The withholding is 'procedural, not cryptographic'. The run executed once on 2026-09-10 in 69.5 s with seeds [137171, 506411, 721632, 937310, 939478]; CONFIRMATION.md reveals them after the run. The pre-registration forbids cluster submission by the fleet, dependency changes and a sixth claim.

findings.topic: (3b) gen19 sealing, seed commitment, registry and once-only confirmation
findings.detail:
scripts/g19_seal_prereg.py modes: `--commit-seeds --seed-store PATH` draws N_CONFIRMATION=5 seeds with `secrets` in [100000, 999999] excluding DISCOVERY_SEEDS, writes {n, salt token_hex(32), schema 'gen19.confirmation_seeds.v1', seeds} to PATH (must be OUTSIDE the repository), writes only sha256(canonical JSON) to manifests/confirmation_seeds_sha256.txt (65e8ae8c...), prints the digest never the seeds, and refuses if a commitment or store already exists ('seed shopping'); the seeds are NOT recomputable, unlike gen16. `--seal` copies preregistration_draft.md to preregistration.md appending SEAL_SEPARATOR '

---' and the footer `Sealed SHA-256 of everything above this line: `<hex>``; digest = sha256((normalise(above) + '
').encode('utf-8')) with a UTF-8 BOM dropped and CRLF→LF; refuses (exit 2) unless DATA_AUDIT.md and FEASIBILITY.md exist, no 'TO BE FINALISED' placeholder, no 'DRAFT / UNSEALED' banner, no unticked `- [ ]`, no footer in the draft, every REQUIRED_SECTIONS heading present (primary hypothesis, metrics, hold-outs, success, baselines, model families, tuning, uncertainty, process, failure, seeds, deviations) and the seed commitment quoted in the draft; writes manifests/prereg_sha256.txt (135842499a...). `--check` is read-only, exits 0 only if sealed and intact, and requires everything below the footer to be `## POST-HOC addendum <n> (<YYYY-MM-DD>, <author>; results seen: <yes|no>)` headings numbered from 1 with non-decreasing dates. Both modes write their own Run manifest (g19_seal_prereg.json, g19_commit_seeds.json at git_head 40f6a750...). Sealed 2026-09-15 with 9 addenda appended (lines 1634-2047). Every post-discovery runner is a registry stage; appending an addendum changes the below-footer digest, so stages without records are re-registered (`register --stage ... --force`) and stages with records keep their entries. The confirmation runner gates (a) seal check + registered below-footer digest, (b) registered code digest equals live code, (c) CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md with ≤5 claims, (d) --seed-store verifying against the commitment, (e) idempotence lock evaluation/confirmation/decisions/confirmation.json absent or --resume; seeds enter only via a redacted SeedStore, every write is scrubbed to opaque indices i1..i5, scan_for_seed_leak fails the run if a seed's decimal form appears, and decisions/CONFIRMATION.md (written last) is the only artefact naming the values together with the --verify-seeds verdict. The run is SPENT: the runner refuses any re-invocation. Commit convention: seal and each addendum are separate commits; the run's start, progress and completion were committed (7b64809 IN PROGRESS, b9a03f0 COMPLETE).

findings.topic: (4) gitignore coverage and the size budget for committed tables
findings.detail: Root .gitignore ignores runs/**/*.parquet, *.log, *.png (except !runs/gen7_architecture/cache/*.parquet), dataset_all_metals/ and /dataset_all_metals, the 4.8 MB pretrained embeddings parquet, /figures/, gen13 models/*.joblib (102 MB, over GitHub's per-file limit), gen14 models/*.joblib, gen13 predictions/**/*.parquet (296 files, 134 MB) and metrics/**/fewshot_stage2_pairs.parquet (105 MB), gen14 cache/ and gen13 verify_direction/bench_cache.pkl (10 MB each), gen15 cache/, models, results/*.parquet, exp/**/*.pkl and long tables, gen16_anchor/pairs_BP.pkl, plus a legacy pre-move block. Nested files: gen16_leads/.gitignore (results/**/_*.pkl, _*.parquet, _pe_keep/, two named files, *.log except run.log, reference_species/out/), gen18_process/.gitignore (results/case_prnd/sys_*/draw_*.csv), gen19/.gitignore (one >5 MB parquet, evaluation/discovery/*/*/s*/, evaluation/discovery/logs/, evaluation/confirmation/records/). Confirmed with git check-ignore: gen14 bench.pkl, gen13 prediction parquet, gen13 joblib, runs parquet and gen19 record paths are ignored, but generations/gen20_kshot/results/x.parquet and generations/gen20_kshot/predictions/x.parquet are NOT ignored by any rule, so a new generation must ship its own nested .gitignore. dataset_all_metals/ is listed in the root ignore but 105 of its files are tracked (raw/, clean/, audit/, reports/, scripts/, tests/ 'tracked on purpose' per its nested .gitignore; intermediate/ ignored); a NEW file under it would be ignored. Size conventions: gen16 digests and excludes anything ≥ LIMIT = 1,000,000 bytes, any .pkl or `_`-prefixed scratch, and logs ≥ 200 KB; gen19 excludes 'files over 5 MB written by scripts' with their digests in the writing script's manifest (files_over_5MB) and whole raw-record trees (240.3 MB discovery, 366.1 MB confirmation); gen18 excludes 24 MB of per-draw sweeps; the rule everywhere is 'everything a report cites by number lives in a small committed CSV, JSON or Markdown'. Committed footprints today: gen13 predictions 5.8 MB (no parquet), gen19 tables 8.8 MB and folds 9.9 MB, gen12 predictions 5.4 MB, gen16 results 20 MB on disk; repository-wide 735 tracked parquet files totalling 150 MB, largest tracked file 83.6 MB (a gen5 oof_predictions.csv), .git 518 MB. Present locally: gen14 cache/bench.pkl, dataset_all_metals (archive sha verifies), bundle (fefbefc6 verifies), runs/gen9_shape/curves/curve_membership.parquet.

findings.topic: (5) Test conventions and known failures on this macOS machine
findings.detail: pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] registers only the `slow` marker ('needs the built cohort or a completed run artefact on disk'); there is no root pytest.ini, conftest.py, setup.cfg, tox.ini or Makefile. gen19 tests/conftest.py registers `slow` and `real_registry`; gen18 conftest registers `slow` and `validation` ('a failure is a reported result, not a suite blocker'); gen16 marks two tests slow without a conftest. Commands (repo root): `PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q` (gen2-gen11), `.venv/bin/python -m pytest generations/<gen>/tests -q`, gen19 with `-p no:cacheprovider` (its tests are checked to change no file in the tree, so no .pytest_cache may be written), `-m "not slow"` for fast sets, gen18 `-m "not slow and not validation"`. Collect-only on 2026-10-14 (no errors): generations/tests 13, gen12 23, gen12.2 23, gen13 12, gen16_leads 42, gen18 247, gen19 886 (gen19 README cites 458 tests / 350 s full / 40 s fast on 2026-09-15; the suite has since grown). Hash-sensitive checks run in subprocesses because Python hash() is salted per process (relocation tests, fold-plan hash). Tests never write into the tree: gen19 seal/registry tests use tmp_path copies and never create the real registry. Known failures on this macOS machine: the two `test_reproduces_frozen_key_mode` cases (exact, relaxed) in generations/gen16_leads/tests/test_l6_cohort_audit.py — the exact rebuild fingerprints 854171b03411d901, not the frozen 4c3c6628ea0be949 (40 of 42 gen16 tests pass; STATUS.md reports passes on the Windows clone); two gen9 tests in tests/test_gen9_curve_objective.py fail in checkouts lacking runs/gen9_shape/curves/curve_membership.parquet — that file IS present on this machine today, so they may now pass (not run). Memory note: 18 root tests skip or fail without ignored runs/ gen8/gen9 artefacts. All gen13-gen19 computation ran on the Windows clone; bit-identity on macOS is unchecked.
evidence: ls pytest.ini conftest.py setup.cfg tox.ini Makefile (all absent)

findings.topic: (6) gen16 anchor test duration and the gen14 bench cache
findings.detail: generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl EXISTS: 10,901,386 bytes, modified 2026-10-14 16:59 (today), gitignored by .gitignore:91. gen14.dirbench.load() returns the pickle if present, otherwise calls gen13sep.amplitude_bench.load_bench() and pickles it (protocol 5); the docstring says building 'costs about a minute', the root .gitignore says 'rebuilt in ~5 s'. The build needs the bundle, runs/gen7_architecture/cache/chemistry_map.parquet, runs/gen6_provenance/provenance_table.parquet and gen12_2_eu_pred/features/coordination_descriptors.parquet, all present. test_anchors.py docstring: fast set (`-m "not slow"`) ~30 s; ANCHORS.md timings: fold_hash_subprocesses 5.1 s, bench_load 0.0 s (cached), value_BP 15.0 s (the bp_board fixture used by the two G14/FLAT tests), G13_ET_TOPO39_BP 15.8 s (the slow anchor). So with the cache present the three fast anchor tests take roughly 20-30 s and the slow one adds ~16 s; add ~1 min if the cache must be rebuilt. The pickle is version-fragile (sklearn/pandas objects); it was built locally under sklearn 1.9.0 / pandas 3.0.5 / numpy 2.5.1. Caveat: the anchors were recorded on the Windows clone (numpy 2.5.3) and the macOS exact-cohort rebuild in the L6 audit differs in fingerprint, so whether test_anchors passes bit-for-bit on this Mac is asserted by README.md:176-181 (only the two L6 tests fail) and the memory note, not verified in this audit.

findings.topic: (7) Single reproduce command precedents
findings.detail: No generation has a script literally named run_all and there is no Makefile; `grep -rl run_all` outside .venv hits only the sibling builder dataset_all_metals/scripts/run_all.py (STAGES tuple of stage scripts run as subprocesses, --verify-determinism hashes every artefact, runs twice and compares) and two quality reports. Precedents to imitate: (a) generations/gen12_eu_pred/scripts/gen12_finalise.sh — bash, cd to repo root, PYTHONPATH=generations/gen12_eu_pred, runs analysis → hypotheses → frontier → diagnostics → figures → headline tables → manifest → self-audit → verify_report → pytest; 're-derive every table, figure, manifest and verification from the predictions on disk; recomputes analysis, never models' (note: running gen12_manifest.py without --verify re-stamps the frozen manifest and breaks verify_relocation.py). (b) generations/gen19_chem_transfer/scripts/g19_run_phaseAB.py — STEPS tuple, each step its own process, --list / --steps subset in pipeline order / --determinism (two full runs, byte comparison of data_audit/, descriptors/, figures/ and manifests/<step>.json with PYTHONHASHSEED unset, manifest verification, unclaimed-output listing, code and git HEAD unchanged), exit codes 0/1/2, record manifests/phaseAB_determinism.json. (c) Ordered command blocks in READMEs: gen13 'Reproducing' (tests → g13_run_ladder.py → g13_analysis.py → g13_fewshot.py → g13_headline_tables.py), gen18 'Running' numbered 1-… per DESIGN.md §11, gen19 'How to run'. Long runs follow gen19's pattern: resumable per-fold records with atomic writes, --resume that refits nothing and refuses records under another code digest, a wall-clock ledger (evaluation/<stage>/decisions/wall_clock.json with budget, invocations, stages_done), --max-hours operator pause, and a report builder that refuses unless the run is COMPLETE. The recovery plan requires exactly this (separate process, atomic saves per part, --resume, refusal of incompatible cache, runtime journal, completion check) and that the final answer ends with a reproduction command.
evidence: grep -rl run_all (only dataset_all_metals/scripts/run_all.py, runs/sae_dataset_audit/quality_report.md, gen19 data_audit/dataset_hashes.csv)

findings.topic: (8) Compute constraints and cluster policy
findings.detail: LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md §11: hard cap for the first cycle = 12 hours total execution time of the computational stages on one host, including repeats and checks (coding hours counted separately); at most 2 worker processes, at most 4 compute threads in total, no nested parallelism; stage table 0 inventory/audit 1 h, 1 metrics/quick reference 2 h, 2 pilot A/B + support mode 3 h, 3 check of the frozen procedure 4 h, 4 intervals/report 2 h; before the first expensive run time one typical fit and estimate ALL fits (nested validation × competitors × two modes × repeats) — the timing counts against the budget and uses training data only; if it does not fit, cut candidate B first, then the second support policy, then the second new-experiment check, fixed before results are seen; do not weaken publication exclusion, do not pick easy pairs, do not raise the budget automatically; run long jobs as a separate process independent of the chat with atomic saves, --resume, refusal of incompatible cache, an actual-time journal and a completion check; one settings version before launch and one deviation log. Repository precedents: gen16 PRE_REGISTRATION machine limits (8 GB RAM, ≤6 concurrent bench processes, n_jobs ≤ 2, OMP_NUM_THREADS=2) and gen16/bootstrap.py os.environ.setdefault('LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT', '2'); gen19 torch.set_num_threads(2) in both runners, MAX_WORKERS = 2, BUDGET_HOURS = 60 (discovery) and LADDER_BUDGET_HOURS = 40, a --max-hours operator pause, and the ledger that recorded 76.6 h used against 60 h (budget exhausted, M3-M7 demoted) on a 12-thread Windows machine. Cluster: slurm/ holds gen2-gen6 wrappers only (e.g. gen6_diversity.slurm: --cpus-per-task=8, --mem=16G, --time=04:00:00, OMP_NUM_THREADS from SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK; submit_*.sh default DRY_RUN=1, PARTITION campus, ACCOUNT acf-utk0011, PYTHON_BIN .venv/bin/python); the user submits cluster jobs themselves (memory user-runs-cluster-jobs.md; START_HERE.md §10 'Cluster and SLURM submissions belong to the user'; gen16 pre-registration 'No cluster submission by the fleet'); requirements-gen3.txt is the Linux-cluster exact environment (Python 3.11.11, numpy 2.4.6, torch 2.13.0). Nothing from gen12 onward used the cluster.

findings.topic: Recovery plan k-shot section 8 requirements that gen20 tests must encode
findings.detail: §8.1: before values are revealed, fix target pairs Q and allowed support pairs S per validation series with Q ∩ S = ∅; first-cycle rule: sort unordered pairs by SHA-256 of 'gen20|cell_id|metal_A|metal_B' (canonical orientation, stable IDs) and take the first max(1, ceil(0.2 * n_pairs)) as Q, add Pr/Nd if measured, the rest are S candidates; evaluate k = 0,1,2,3 on the SAME Q for every model and policy; a separate Q_PrNd by the same rule; series with too few supports excluded in advance by availability; arithmetic-closure guard: build the support graph and keep the endpoints of every target pair in different components, enforced at every support choice; policies may read only availability, features and a training-estimated covariance; k counts separation coefficients, not experiments. §8.2: compare a regularised simple line over known measurements, the previous Gen15 adapter on the same set and budget, and a covariance-consistent curve correction f_post = f_prior + C Bᵀ (B C Bᵀ + R)⁻¹ (y_support − B f_prior) with a PSD C (never the old indefinite matrix), solved as a linear system; two fixed policies (widest allowed pair; max expected variance reduction of the target Q); lexicographically first canonical pair on ties. §12 minimal tests (8 items): orientation reversal flips sign and Gen13/Gen19 adapters agree; invalid pairs across conditions/publications/unknown valence; no shared publications/copies/forbidden structures between train and test, all pairs of a series in one part; R² behaviour (perfect 1, test mean 0, bad negative, constant target NA; weights match the evaluator; squared correlation vs scale shift distinguished); series duplication does not change weight; same Q at k=0..3 and no target or algebraically recoverable analogue among supports; covariance PSD and untouched by test data; resume does not refit and incomplete runs never get COMPLETE status. §9 success thresholds are pre-declared and may not be lowered after seeing scores. The final answer must start with four sentences (what can now be predicted, on which data, how much better than the strongest competitor, what still fails) then a table link and a reproduction command, with no bare codes like 'S1 UNDECIDED'.

reusable_components.what: Run context manager writing a deterministic manifests/<script>.json (schema, script, git_head, seed, arguments, archive_master_sha256, inputs/outputs with path/sha256/sha256_lf/bytes, extra) and a volatile manifests/run_info/<script>.json (date_utc, runtime_s, python, platform, processor, cpu_count, package versions); atomic write_json (tmp + os.replace, strict JSON, sorted keys, LF), write_csv (LF, %.6g), write_text, git_head(), _versions().
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Copy into gen20's package as gen20sep/manifest.py and replace `from gen19ct import paths` with gen20's paths module (needs REPO_ROOT, MANIFESTS_DIR, ensure_dir, rel, digests, ARCHIVE_MASTER_SHA256 or an equivalent dataset digest constant). Wrap every script's main in `with Run(NAME, args=vars(ns), seed=SEED) as run:` and call run.inputs()/run.outputs().
reusable_components.caveats: It imports gen19ct.paths directly (manifest.py:29), so it cannot be imported from gen19 without putting gen19 on sys.path and inheriting gen19's REPO_ROOT and manifests directory; copy rather than import. git_head changes the deterministic manifest after every commit (README.md:504-505). packages show null for modules the script never imported.

reusable_components.what: sha256_bytes, digests(path) returning binary and CRLF→LF-normalised SHA-256 plus size for TEXT_SUFFIXES, matches(path, expected) accepting either digest, rel(path) enforcing repo-relative POSIX paths, ensure_dir, pinned dataset digests (ARCHIVE_MASTER_SHA256, BUNDLE_DATASET_SHA256_PREFIX), add_gen18_to_path().
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Pattern for gen20sep/paths.py: G20_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]; REPO_ROOT = G20_ROOT.parents[1]; pin the input digests as constants; no side effects on import (gen13sep/paths.py creates output directories on import, which gen19 deliberately avoided).
reusable_components.caveats: TEXT_SUFFIXES decides which files get the LF digest; parquet is binary-only. The bundle must be read with columns=[...] (README.md:522-524).

reusable_components.what: Seal / check / commit-seeds / verify-seeds CLI: footer 'Sealed SHA-256 of everything above this line: `<hex>`', normalise() (BOM, CRLF), digest_of_above, split_footer, build_sealed_text, readiness gates (placeholder marker, draft banner, unticked boxes, required section headings, seed commitment quoted), below_footer_problems (dated numbered POST-HOC addenda), commit_seeds with secrets + salt and store outside the repo, load_committed_seeds/verify_seed_store; PreregPaths dataclass takes a --root for tests.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Copy as generations/gen20_*/scripts/g20_seal_prereg.py, change the import to the gen20 package, set DISCOVERY_SEEDS to whatever gen20 uses for discovery and REQUIRED_SECTIONS to the plan's section names (the recovery plan calls the frozen document PLAN_FROZEN.md and demands a protocol.json hash in it). Tests: copy tests/test_seal_prereg.py's tmp_path approach so the real draft is never sealed by a test.
reusable_components.caveats: Sealing is an orchestrator decision; the real `--seal` and `--commit-seeds` write Run manifests and must be run once. The seed store must lie outside the repository; the gen19 seeds are not recomputable (unlike gen16's public rule), so losing the store loses the confirmation design.

reusable_components.what: Per-stage digest registry (manifests/digest_registry.json): register_stage, verify_record (record fields prereg_addenda_sha256/code_digest vs the stage entry, superseded entries still verify), log_code_change, reregister_all_stages after an addendum, refuse_unless_sealed / refuse_unless_writable gates for runners, below_footer_digest.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Adopt the idea (records carry the code digest they were written under; verify against a registered entry, never live code) if gen20 has multiple runner stages; for a 12 h single-cycle study a single code digest per run manifest (D.code_digest over the prediction-affecting files) is probably sufficient.
reusable_components.caveats: Tightly coupled to gen19ct.evaluation.discovery (imports D, uses discovery.enumerate_plan, FITTED_ARMS); would need heavy trimming.

reusable_components.what: Ordered multi-step pipeline runner: STEPS tuple, one subprocess per step, --list, --steps, --determinism (two full runs, byte comparison of outputs and step manifests, verify_manifests against disk, unclaimed-output listing, code/git-HEAD unchanged), exit codes 0/1/2, record manifests/phaseAB_determinism.json.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Template for gen20's single reproduce command (scripts/g20_run_all.py or similar): list the stage scripts in dependency order, run each as its own process, verify manifests after the run, and offer --determinism for the cheap (non-fitting) stages.
reusable_components.caveats: Suited to deterministic, non-fitting stages (~4.5 min); for fits use the resumable-record pattern of g19_run_confirmation.py (fold_resume_status, atomic writes, StaleRecordError) instead.

reusable_components.what: Writes evaluation/<run>/MANIFEST.sha256 ('sha256  path  bytes', sorted, LF) for every gitignored raw record; --check recomputes digests, fails on mismatch/missing, and fails if a listed file is not actually gitignored.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Copy for gen20's results/<run_id>/ bulk outputs; pair with a nested generations/gen20_*/.gitignore that excludes the bulk paths. gen16's simpler g16_manifest.py (size threshold LIMIT=1 MB) is the alternative.

reusable_components.what: Prints the SHA-256 of the five-design fold plan (sorted test indices per fold; stricter train+test digest) as one JSON line, designed to be run in two separate subprocesses because hash() is salted per process.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Same pattern for gen20's split: compute the fold/Q/S assignment digest in a subprocess inside tests and compare with a recorded value (anchors.json style).
reusable_components.caveats: Imports gen16.bootstrap and gen14.dirbench.load (needs the bench cache); only the hashing idea transfers.

reusable_components.what: Minimal 61-line seal/verify script for a two-line footer ('---' + 'SHA-256 of every byte above the preceding '---' line: <hex>'); --seal, --reseal, verify-by-default.

reusable_components.caveats: No CRLF/BOM normalisation (gen19 fixed that); addenda go above the footer and require --reseal, which re-stamps the digest.

reusable_components.what: Once-only confirmation runner (verifies seeds against commitment and public rule, loads ≤5 frozen claims, CONFIRMATION_RUN_ONCE.json marker refusing reruns unless --force with a _rerun_ suffix) and an AST audit forbidding `seeds=` keywords / seed literals outside allowed files.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Pattern for gen20's confirmation stage and for a test that no discovery script touches the withheld seeds.
reusable_components.caveats: Hard-codes gen16 paths, COMMITMENT and DISCOVERY seeds.

reusable_components.what: Thread cap (LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT=2 via os.environ.setdefault) and sys.path insertion of gen15, gen14, gen13 before any frozen import.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: gen20sep/bootstrap.py: set LOKY_MAX_CPU_COUNT / OMP_NUM_THREADS to honour the plan's ≤4 threads total and insert gen13_separation, gen14_direction, gen15_curve (and gen19_chem_transfer if its adapter is reused).

reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Import read-only through gen16-style bootstrap; call gen14.dirbench.load() (cache hit ~0 s) to obtain BenchData with frame, folds and metrics without rebuilding gen13.

reusable_components.what: Bash 'finalise' script: re-derive analysis, tables, figures, manifest, self-audit and report verification from stored predictions and run pytest; never refits.

risks.risk: Directory-name conflict: the recovery plan (the only written contract) names generations/gen20_separation/ with a package gen20sep/, while the task names generations/gen20_kshot/. Choosing the wrong name breaks the plan's file contract and the generations/README.md table row.
risks.mitigation: Decide the name before any file is created; if gen20_kshot is chosen, record the deviation from plan §12 in the generation's README and PLAN_FROZEN.md and keep the rest of the §12 contract (protocol.json, results/<run_id>/ files).

risks.risk: No gitignore cover for a new generation: git check-ignore shows generations/gen20_kshot/results/x.parquet and predictions/x.parquet are not ignored, so prediction dumps, caches and logs would be committable; the repository already carries 735 parquet (150 MB) and a 518 MB .git.
risks.mitigation: Ship generations/gen20_*/.gitignore on the first commit excluding results/<run_id>/*.parquet bulk dumps, caches, *.log and anything ≥1 MB (gen16 threshold) or ≥5 MB (gen19 threshold), and write results/MANIFEST.sha256 with a --check script; commit only small CSV/JSON/MD that reports cite.

audits.summary: G14 is a two-degrees-of-freedom curve model. An L2 LogisticRegression (C=1.0, lbfgs, max_iter=5000) behind SimpleImputer(median, keep_empty_features=True) + StandardScaler, fitted on the 39 TOPO39 columns (every LEAN column starting coord__dist__ or coord__arm__), returns p = P(heavy-selective); the deployed "hard" rule maps p>=0.5 to s=-1 else +1; the amplitude is a = s * m where m is the training fold's chemotype-balanced mean |radius coefficient| over well-determined cells only (n_metals>=5); the curvature b is the training fold's balanced mean second coefficient; the predicted centred 14-metal curve is [a, b] @ basis, and each pairwise prediction is curve[ia]-curve[ib] with ia the lighter lanthanide. The basis is two fixed rows from gen13sep.metals.physics_basis — the standardised Shannon CN8 radius and the standardised square of that z-score, each mean-centred then rescaled to row norm sqrt(14). "Centred curve" means log D(Ln) minus the nanmean over the metals that cell actually measured; per-cell labels are ridge-0.5 least squares of that centred row on the two basis rows over observed metals only (basis.fit_coefficients), and the direction label is coefficient<0. FLAT predicts exactly zero (gen15.arms.flat); MEAN_CURVE in the gen14/gen15 benches is the balanced-mean (amplitude, curvature) pair and scores 0.6217 under BP, which is NOT gen13's B1_MEAN_CURVE 14-vector weighted nanmean (0.639 BP) — two different "mean curve" arms exist. The O_* arms are gen15 oracles that read the held-out cell's own sign, amplitude, curvature, level or publication mean; under BP O_SIGN 0.4864, O_AMP 0.3222, O_BOTH 0.1811, O_CURV 0.4272, O_PUBMAG 0.4476, O_EXTMAG 0.4876. Feature blocks measured live: COND 64, MASSACT 8, PHYSCHEM 10, DONORS 13, ECFP 2048, LIG2D 206, COORD 114; LEAN (COND+MASSACT+PHYSCHEM+DONORS+COORD) = 209, CHEM = 137, ALL = 2463. ECFP and LIG2D are the known-harmful blocks and are excluded from every deployed configuration; the 209-column G13_FULL_MODEL scores 0.552 under BP against G14's 0.500. For a brand-new SMILES only COORD/TOPO39 (gen122.coordination.descriptors_for) and PHYSCHEM (RDKit) are exactly recomputable; DONORS is the bundle's Architector census and scripts/g13_predict.py approximates it from coordination counts with core_cn hard-coded to 9.0 — a documented fidelity gap for any new-ligand k-shot query. The anchors reproduce through the frozen benches: G14 BP = 0.5000794414203691, FLAT BP = 0.5885062528901843, G13_ET_TOPO39 macro direction accuracy = 0.7683085207475452, guarded by four tests in generations/gen16_leads/tests/test_anchors.py. Budget is cheap: a 5-seed x 5-fold G14 sweep over one design costs about 15 s total, the whole FLAT+G14 five-design anchor run about 75 s, while gen13's deployed V2_BAG4@lean bag costs 3.7-9.3 s per fold (25 folds per design) and C_DIRECT_ROW 15-37 s per fold. Torch exists in the repo (gen3 latent-difference MLP, gen7 hierarchical_nn, gen8 CNP, gen10 setcontext, gen12 D-MPNN, simplicial) and in gen19 (M1-M7, shared_only), but no module under gen13-gen18 imports torch: the entire gen13-gen18 zero-shot lineage is sklearn ExtraTrees/Logistic/Ridge only.

findings.topic: (1) What G14 is exactly — estimator, features, composition
findings.detail: Direction: generations/gen14_direction/gen14/models.py:123-147 dir_logistic() builds make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy='median', keep_empty_features=True), StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=5000, solver='lbfgs')) and fits with logisticregression__sample_weight=w; it returns predict_proba(Xte)[:,1] = P(amp<0) = P(heavy-selective). Defaults are weights='balanced' (so plain chemotype weights, not confidence weights), units='cell', label='cell', penalty='l2', transform='std'. With only one class present it returns the constant y.mean() (models.py:140-141). Feature set: gen14/dirbench.py:83 topo = [c for c in lean if c.startswith('coord__dist__') or c.startswith('coord__arm__')] — I verified live that this is exactly 39 columns (17 coord__arm__ + 22 coord__dist__). Amplitude prior: models.py:254-256 amp_constant returns np.full(len(Xte), np.average(np.abs(amp), weights=w)) — one scalar per fold. Composition: models.py:293-299 candidate(direction, amplitude) returns the tuple (p, mag); dirbench.py:238-255 decision(p, mag, rule) turns it into the radius coefficient: 'hard' = np.where(p>=0.5, -1.0, 1.0)*mag (the deployed rule), 'expected' = (1-2p)*mag, 'sqrt' = -sign(2p-1)*sqrt(|2p-1|)*mag. The curve is assembled in scripts/g14_value.py:88 as np.c_[a, np.full(len(te), bmean)] @ bench.basis with bmean = np.average(bench.coef[tr,1], weights=w) at g14_value.py:78 (balanced mean curvature over ALL training cells, whereas mag_const at g14_value.py:80 uses only the rich subset rtr with its own weights wr). GEN14_REPORT.md:8-15 states the model as log D(Ln) - mean_Ln log D = a*radius(Ln) + b*radius(Ln)^2 with a = s*m.

findings.topic: (1b) The basis functions and what 'centred curve' means
findings.detail: The basis is built by gen13sep/basis.py:99-104 physics_basis_matrix(('radius','radius_sq')) from gen13sep/metals.py:56-73 physics_basis(): 'radius' = z = standardise(Shannon CN8 radius over the 14 lanthanides), 'radius_sq' = standardise(z**2), and metals.py:72 subtracts the mean from every basis function so each is mean-zero over the 14 metals. basis.py:35-37 then rescales each row to norm sqrt(14) (ROW_NORM, basis.py:27). Promethium is absent throughout (metals.py:11, LANTHANIDES at metals.py:17-18 has 14 entries, no Pm). 'Centred' is defined twice identically: basis.py:31-32 centre_rows subtracts np.nanmean over axis 1, and amplitude_bench.py:82 computes centred = Y - np.nanmean(Y, axis=1, keepdims=True) — the mean over the metals the cell actually measured, so NaNs are never imputed. Coefficients: basis.py:107-113 fit_coefficients solves (B'B + 0.5 I)^-1 B'y on observed metals only, DEFAULT_RIDGE = 0.5 (basis.py:29); basis.py:14-18 notes a fully observed cell is shrunk 3.4% and a two-metal cell much more. Pair predictions: amplitude_bench.py:138-140 and valuebench.py:117-119 both compute curve = coef @ basis then prediction = curve[rows, ia] - curve[rows, ib]; the pair rows come from metrics.py:39-41 pair_rows_for_cell which enumerates a<b over observed metals, so A is always the LIGHTER lanthanide and y = log D(A) - log D(B) (amplitude_bench.py:115 records dZ = Z[b]-Z[a] >= 0). This is the orientation the task brief calls gen13 lighter-first; gen19 uses the opposite (see finding on gen19 orientation).

findings.topic: (1c) The training-set convention that is part of G14's definition
findings.detail: G14 trains the classifier ONLY on well-determined cells. gen14/dirbench.py:47 MIN_METALS = 5; dirbench.py:140 rich = n_metals >= 5; dirbench.py:144 tr = f.train_index[rich[f.train_index]] when rich_only_train=True (the default); dirbench.py:48 MIN_TRAIN = 40 skips a fold with fewer than 40 training cells, and dirbench.py:146 also skips a fold whose training amplitudes are single-signed. Predictions are still made for EVERY held-out cell (dirbench.py:136-137 docstring), so the pairwise metric uses all cells. Measured live: 289 of 521 cells are rich, covering 82 of 90 extractants and 40 of 45 chemotypes; 68.1% of all cells and 70.2% of rich cells are heavy-selective. GEN14_REPORT.md:95-97 attributes 0.038 of the 0.561->0.500 improvement over gen13 stage 3 to exactly these two conventions (train on rich cells, take the magnitude from rich cells) and only 0.023 to the estimator — so a k-shot study that drops the rich filter is not reproducing G14. GEN14_REPORT.md:172-174 records that training on all 521 cells is +0.006 under B/BR/BQ but -0.046 under BP.

findings.topic: (1d) Weights: two different weight calls inside one arm
findings.detail: cell_weights (gen13sep/amplitude_bench.py:90-102) in mode 'balanced' is gen13sep/models.py:30-33 chemotype_balanced_weights: w_i = 1/count(chemotype_i), rescaled so sum(w) = len(w). Mode 'reliability' additionally multiplies by n_obs/(n_obs+2) and renormalises within each chemotype (amplitude_bench.py:100-102). G14 uses 'balanced' everywhere. Note the asymmetry a k-shot reimplementation must copy exactly: the classifier and the magnitude use weights built on the RICH training subset (dirbench.py:148 w = cell_weights(bench.groups[tr], ...) where tr is already rich-filtered; g14_value.py:76-80 builds wr on rtr), while the curvature uses weights built on the FULL training fold (g14_value.py:75,78). gen15/valuebench.py:78-90 encodes the same split: rich_weights() recomputes cell_weights on rich_train(), train_mean_curvature() uses self.w (full fold), train_mean_magnitude() uses rich weights. Also gen14/models.py:38-52 confidence_weights (tau=0.10) and models.py:55-70 extractant_units exist but are NOT in the deployed G14 (GEN14_REPORT.md:170-174 reports both as nulls).

findings.topic: (2) FLAT, MEAN_CURVE and the O_* oracles
findings.detail: FLAT: gen15/arms.py:92-94 returns np.zeros((len(ctx.test), 2)) — predict no separation at all; docstring calls it 'the floor every gain in this programme should be quoted over'. Its gen13 equivalent is ZeroArm/B0_ZERO (gen13sep/models.py:82-89). MEAN_CURVE: gen15/arms.py:97-99 is _curve(train_mean_amplitude(), train_mean_curvature()) = the balanced mean SIGNED amplitude and mean curvature; the same arm is built inline at g14_value.py:89. Distinct from gen13sep/models.py:92-105 MeanCurveArm (B1_MEAN_CURVE), which is a weighted nanmean of the 14-vector centred curves. The two score differently under BP: 0.6217 (gen14/gen15 MEAN_CURVE, results/g14_value_BP.csv and g15_locate_board.csv) vs 0.639 (B1_MEAN_CURVE, DECISION_REPORT.md:415). Oracles (gen15/arms.py:119-171, every one named O_* and 'can never be a deployed arm' per arms.py:3-5): o_sign = true sign x training mean magnitude; o_amp = the cell's own amplitude; o_both = the cell's own two coefficients (ctx.bench.coef[test]); o_curvature = G14 amplitude + the cell's own curvature; o_extractant_magnitude / o_publication_magnitude = mean |amp| of the cell's own extractant / publication peers excluding itself (_group_oracle_magnitude, arms.py:137-147); o_level(stat, how) = magnitude as an isotonic or log-linear function of the cell's own log D level (arms.py:160-171). QUERY_SPAN and N_METALS are explicitly NOT oracles (arms.py:15-16, 177-199): the radius span of the queried metals and the metal count are known before any experiment.

findings.topic: (3) Feature blocks: names, verified column counts, and which are lean / harmful
findings.detail: Blocks are declared in gen13sep/features.py:45 BLOCK_ORDER = (COND, MASSACT, PHYSCHEM, DONORS, ECFP, LIG2D, COORD) and built in features.py:95-149. Counts verified live by building the bench: COND 64 (0.9% NaN), MASSACT 8 (7.3%), PHYSCHEM 10 (0%), DONORS 13 (0%), ECFP 2048 (0%), LIG2D 206 (0.7%), COORD 114 (3.5%); LEAN total 209, CHEM total 137, ALL total 2463 (matches run_spec.json n_features 2463 for every all-blocks run). LEAN_BLOCKS = ('COND','MASSACT','PHYSCHEM','DONORS','COORD') at amplitude_bench.py:45; CHEM_BLOCKS = ('PHYSCHEM','DONORS','COORD') at :46; ALL_BLOCKS at :47. Named subsets over LEAN in dirbench.py:95-114: BITE6 (6 hand-picked bite descriptors), TOPO39 39, DONORS13 13 (chem__*), PHYSCHEM10 10, MASSACT8 8, COND64 64, COORD114 114, CHEM137, LEAN209, plus TOPO_* unions. COORD family split verified live: donor 27, motif 23, dist 22, arm 17, arch 25 = 114. KNOWN HARMFUL: ECFP and LIG2D. gen13sep/scripts/g13_predict.py:13-16 states 'Blocks that do not transfer across laboratories (ECFP, the 206 RDKit descriptors) and a conditions-only member are deliberately out'; DECISION_REPORT.md:551 concludes the compact binding-site blocks are the only representation that transfers. Two opt-in blocks exist and are never in the default ladder: RESP3D (features.py:46-47, features3d.py — xTB geometry response slopes, 15 descriptors x slope/intercept/resid_sd + resp3d__n_metals) and LOGK (features.py:49-50).

findings.topic: (3b) How a new extractant's features are computed from SMILES — and where the pipeline is only approximate
findings.detail: Exact from SMILES: COORD (all 114 columns) via generations/gen12_2_eu_pred/gen122/coordination.py:209-384 descriptors_for(smiles), which takes one canonical SMILES and nothing else (coordination.py:3-6: 'No experimental condition, no target, no fold and no metal enters'); TOPO39 is the coord__dist__ + coord__arm__ subset of that. PHYSCHEM via RDKit Descriptors (g13_predict.py:118-122). ECFP via AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(mol, 2, 2048) (g13_predict.py:112-116). The two deployed entry points: gen14_direction/scripts/g14_predict.py:87-94 _descriptors() calls coordination.descriptors_for and selects the stored topo columns, then predict() at :97-122 applies the pickled pipeline, the hard rule, the stored magnitude and curvature and the stored basis, and flags a topology vector unseen in training (:105-106 against payload['training_topology']). gen13_separation/scripts/g13_predict.py:107-146 _ligand_features() does the fuller block build. APPROXIMATIONS a k-shot study must know about: (a) DONORS is NOT computed from SMILES in training — features.py:103,126 reads it from the frozen gen6 chemistry map (paths.py:24 runs/gen7_architecture/cache/chemistry_map.parquet), whose donor census comes from the bundle's Architector DONOR_TYPES JSON list (src/lanthanide_separation/gen6/chemistry.py:233-247); g13_predict.py:128-146 approximates the 13 DONORS columns from coordination counts and hard-codes chem__core_cn = 9.0, derives chem__dentate from coord__arm__estimated_denticity_per_pocket clipped to [2,8], and comments 'donor census approximated from the coordination donor counts (Architector census unavailable)'. (b) g13_predict.py:188 leaves the LIG2D block as NaN for new rows ('not recomputed'). (c) COORD is read from the frozen parquet (features.py:109-114, 183 extractants x 114 columns verified) and is NaN for the two SF extractants it does not cover (features.py:14-16). gen19 keeps the same rule: features.py REGISTRATION_CHOICES 'topo39_source' says the frozen gen12.2 table only, matched on canonical primary-extractant SMILES, 'not recomputed'.
