findings.topic: (5) C_DIRECT_ROW: the row-wise direct model
findings.detail: gen13sep/models.py:232-269 DirectRowArm, name 'C_DIRECT_ROW'. Learner: tree_pipeline (models.py:36-42) = make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy='median', keep_empty_features=True), ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=400, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=-1)). Target: RAW log D per (cell, metal) row, NOT the centred curve. Design matrix (models.py:244-253 _rows): each cell's feature row repeated 14 times, horizontally stacked with exactly two metal columns — Z_VEC (atomic number) and R_VEC (raw Shannon CN8 radius, models.py:26-27); rows with NaN log D are dropped. Weights (models.py:257-261): the cell's chemotype-balanced weight divided by its number of observed metals then renormalised, 'so chemotype shares are identical to the curve arms'. Prediction (models.py:266-269): predict all 14 metals, reshape, subtract the row mean — the level is learned and then cancelled. random_state is the fold's model_seed = 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 (splits.py:27-29, 58-60), independent of the split seed. It is the pre-registered reference arm for P1 (PRE_REGISTRATION.md:80, :91). BP score 0.583, design-B score 0.495 (DECISION_REPORT.md:412, :107).

findings.topic: (5b) V2_BAG4@lean: members, hyperparameters, and how it was selected
findings.detail: Definition: gen13sep/models.py:758-781 v2_arms(); :764 bag() = BagArm([DirectRowArm(), PhysicsBasisArm(('radius','radius_sq')), LowRankArm(rank=1), LowRankArm(rank=2)], name='V2_BAG4'); :773 BlockSubsetArm(bag(), lean, name='V2_BAG4@lean') with lean = ('COND','MASSACT','PHYSCHEM','DONORS','COORD') at :762. BagArm (models.py:704-717) is an EQUAL-WEIGHT mean of member curves, refit every fold — no learned weights, no inner validation. Every member uses the identical tree_pipeline hyperparameters (400 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2, median imputer, chemotype-balanced weights): DirectRowArm (models.py:240-242), PhysicsBasisArm (models.py:208-213 — fixed radius+radius_sq basis, trees predict the 2 coefficients), LowRankArm rank 1 and 2 (models.py:185-190 — in-fold rank-K data basis from weighted ALS on observed entries, basis.py:57-96, then trees predict the K coefficients). BlockSubsetArm (models.py:671-694) restricts the inner arm to the lean column indices and reindexes ctx.extra['blocks']. SELECTION: it was NOT chosen by any inner-validation rule — DECISION_REPORT.md:355-358 labels the whole V2 ladder exploratory ('the arms were designed after the locked run was read, on the same folds'), and :427 states 'Under the honest design the right configuration is the pure lean bag V2_BAG4@lean, not the mixed bag that contains a conditions-only member', chosen because the mixed bags win under B (0.458) but lose under BP (0.557 vs 0.536). :429-436 names it the deployed configuration. Contrast with M_SELECTED (models.py:318-379 SelectedArm), which IS inner-validated: it fits six candidates on the inner-training chemotypes, scores macro MAE with one vote per inner-validation chemotype, keeps the best and refits on the whole fold; PRE_REGISTRATION.md:73-77 makes M_SELECTED the primary endpoint and forbids promoting a candidate on a test score. Deployed record: generations/gen13_separation/models/deploy.json lists arms direct@lean, physics@lean, lowrank1@lean, lowrank2@lean, cohort_fingerprint 4c3c6628ea0be949, n_cells 521, suggested_pairs La-Lu, Ce-Tm, Eu-Yb.

findings.topic: (6) gen19 M0: inputs, learner, target, orientation
findings.detail: M0 IS B5, not a separate model: generations/gen19_chem_transfer/gen19ct/models/boosted.py:9 'M0 is B5 (section 6 ladder)', :81 ARM_NAMES = ('B5','M0','FLAT_CAT'), :83 FEATURE_PRESET maps both B5 and M0 to the B5 preset. Learner: CatBoost, loss RMSE, eval_metric MAE, depth in {4,6,8}, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg in {3,10}, <=3000 iterations with early stopping after 200 rounds on the inner validation fold, one_hot_max_size 10, thread_count 2, allow_writing_files=False (boosted.py:98-99 DEPTH_GRID/L2_GRID, :182-220 CatBoostConfig, :227 REGISTERED_GRID = 6 configurations). Tuning is nested per outer fold with the 0.005 tie rule resolved toward lower depth then larger l2 (boosted.py:93 TIE_TOLERANCE, :201-203 complexity_key, :235-245 select_config); the outer refit uses iterations = median trees kept by early stopping across the three inner folds and cannot early-stop (boosted.py:47-49, 114-117). Target: log_D — interface.py:69 TARGET_COL = 'log_D'; it is a per-row absolute log D model, not a curve or coefficient model. Features (features.py ARM_PRESETS): blocks ('metal','extractant','condition'), categorical='string' (native CatBoost categoricals), missing='nan'. The metal block comes from descriptors/metals.csv (Z, formal charge, CN6/CN8/CN9 radii, f- and d-electron counts, Pauling EN; categorical category/series/hsab_class; polarizability excluded as all-NA); the extractant block from descriptors/extractant_systems.csv + extractant_components.csv (n_components, 19 donor_* counts, n_donor_sites, denticity_proxy, concentration-share-weighted mw/mol_logp/tpsa/rotatable_bonds, and pca_00..pca_15 = a 16-component PCA of the Morgan COUNT fingerprint of the primary extractant fitted on outer-training SYSTEMS); the condition block from gen19ct.data.normalize.condition_vector (log10 acid/extractant/metal M, O/A phase ratio, temperature, contact time, modifier and complexant presence and log concentrations, acid-grid flag, categorical acid_anion and diluent_family). Table sizes verified: 79 metal-state rows (29 Ln, 24 An, 26 none), 263 systems, 295 components. Model seed 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 (boosted.py:96, 160-164) — same formula as gen13. ORIENTATION: gen19ct/evaluation/pairs.py:12-14 'state_a is the heavier state: larger atomic number, then higher oxidation state ... logSF = log D_a - log D_b', the opposite of gen13/gen14's lighter-first convention; pairs.py:13-14 notes MAE and direction accuracy do not depend on orientation, but a signed per-pair comparison across generations does. USABLE as a 'predict two log D then subtract' baseline: yes, structurally — pairs.py:158-165 derived_logsf(pairs, predictions) already does exactly yhat_a - yhat_b for ANY fitted arm, including lookups; FLAT is flat_logsf (pairs.py:168-170, predicted logSF = 0).

findings.topic: (6b) What retraining gen19 M0 under gen13's BP folds would cost
findings.detail: Cannot be done by configuration — it requires new code, and the two stacks are disjoint in four ways. (a) Different corpora: gen19 reads dataset_all_metals/clean/master_clean.parquet, 16,770 archive records of which 12,411 are MODEL rows, 6,495 lanthanide + 5,420 actinide (data/load.py:3-4, DATA_AUDIT.md:33,39); gen13's cohort is 521 multi-metal CELLS from the frozen bundle 'dataset with 3D structures/dataset.parquet' (paths.py:20-22, sha256 pinned at paths.py:22). (b) Different units: gen13 folds index cells (splits.py:63-113 returns cell index arrays), gen19 arms consume row frames in the prepare_frame layout (interface.py:11-13) with their own fold files (gen19ct/folds/registered.py, io.py). (c) Different hold-out semantics: gen13 BP = chemotype hold-out plus removal of every training cell sharing a publication with a held-out cell (splits.py:31-35, 72-77); gen19's registered designs are V1 (publication-group), V2 (leave-one-metal-out), V5 (hidden cell), V5-P/V5-PAIR/V6. (d) Different extractant identity: gen13 keys on canonical_smiles; gen19 on extractant_system_key with a 263-row system table. Work items for a bridge: map gen13's 521 cells x 14 metals to gen19 row frames with g19_metal_state/extractant_system_key/condition_key, supply a FitContext with hidden_index and an isolation_check (interface.py:31-35, 38-47), and bypass or re-wire the gen19 inner designs (boosted.py:36-39, 118-124) since gen13 folds carry a single 4-way inner chemotype split (splits.py:105-107), not three simultaneous inner cell folds. Compute, measured from gen19's own benchmark (evaluation/discovery/benchmark/measurements_B5.json): per outer fold with ~11,000-12,000 training rows, B5 costs inner_fit 5.8 s (V1, 3 splits, 74 trees) to 68.9 s (V2) and outer_refit 2.3-69.0 s, peak RSS ~0.8 GB; the V1 fold is the closest analogue to a 25-fold gen13 plan, so a 5-seed x 5-fold B5 run on gen19-sized data is roughly 25 x (6+2) s plus calibration, but on gen13's 521 cells (~4,700 rows) it would be considerably cheaper. The sealed cost model put a full V5-P batched B5 run at 450 h (cost_estimate.json), so scope matters enormously.

findings.topic: (7) Training time per fold — G14, the bag, and the full five-design runs
findings.detail: G14 (logistic on 39 columns) is essentially free. results/g14_baseline_board.csv, design BP: LOGIT_TOPO39 0.8 s and BITE6_LOGIT 0.7 s for ALL 25 folds (5 seeds x 5 folds), i.e. ~0.03 s/fold; the ExtraTrees arms on the same folds cost 14.2-14.5 s per 25 folds (~0.58 s/fold): G13_ET_TOPO39 14.4 s, CHEM137_ET 14.2 s, LEAN209_ET 14.5 s, DONORS13_ET 14.3 s. anchors.json timing_seconds: value_B 14.71, value_BR 14.61, value_BQ 15.38, value_A 15.03, value_BP 15.05 for FLAT+G14 together per design (so the full five-design anchor run is ~75 s), G13_ET_TOPO39_BP 15.80, bench_load 0.006 (cached). The bench itself builds in ~1.1 s warm / about a minute cold per amplitude_bench.py:76, and dirbench.py:44,56-67 caches it to generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl, which is gitignored (.gitignore:91) and currently absent — a first run on this machine rebuilds it. gen13 ladder timings (predictions/*/timings.csv, median seconds per fold, 25 folds per design, n_train_cells ~379 under BP and ~417 under B): V2_BAG4@lean 3.94 (BP) / 5.75 (B, mean 9.26, max 21.15); C_DIRECT_ROW 16.88 (BP_v2) / 29.00 (B_v2, max 68.87); M_SELECTED 15.27 (BP_lean) / 11.66 (B_primary); M_PHYSICS 1.24-2.78; M_LOWRANK_K2 2.08-3.47; B1_MEAN_CURVE 0.01; the full un-subsetted V2_BAG4 38.29. Budget implication for a 5-seed x 5-fold x multiple-k study: G14 at ~0.03 s/fold means the model fitting is negligible and the cost will be dominated by the 10,000-replicate chemotype-blocked bootstrap (inference.py:27 REPLICATES = 10_000) and by any bag/row-model arm you include; a 5-fold x 5-seed x 5-k G14 grid is seconds, the same grid with V2_BAG4@lean is ~10-25 min, and with C_DIRECT_ROW ~1-2 h.

findings.topic: (8) Every neural network in the repo and its input representation
findings.detail: Exhaustive list of modules importing torch (grep over generations/ and src/): (a) src/lanthanide_separation/gen3_models.py:272-345 — the gen3 'latent difference' shared-g MLP: nn.Sequential of Linear+SiLU(+Dropout) blocks ending in Linear(.,1), input = two parallel 'shoulder' column contracts (a_columns/b_columns from gen3_data.py:40-49 h3_a2_a_columns / h3_elec_a_columns, i.e. per-metal pair-shoulder features, the H3_A2 and H3_A2_ELEC arms at gen3_evaluation.py:1210-1213), prediction = score_a - score_b, pseudo-Huber loss, AdamW, torch.manual_seed(model_seed) + use_deterministic_algorithms. (b) src/lanthanide_separation/gen7/hierarchical_nn.py — offset/shape network: z_L = LigandEncoder(x_L) with ligand_blocks ('DONORS','PHYSCHEM') (config at :122), z_M from Z/lanthanide index/ionic radius+RBF, z_C from condition_blocks ('COND','MASSACTION'); y = OffsetHead(z_L) + ResponseHead(z_L,z_M,z_C); ligand_dim 64, metal_dim 32, condition_dim 64, hidden 128, depth 2, dropout 0.15, interaction 'film'. (c) src/lanthanide_separation/gen8/cnp.py — Conditional Neural Process; context encoder sees (conditions, metal, measured value), mean-pooled over context points so k=0..5 use one trained state; ligand representation is LIGAND_COLUMNS (cnp.py:100-108), 23 numbers = 8 donor counts + n_total + DENTATE + coreCN + n_ligs + n_fill + the 10 physchem scalars; cnp.py:33-35 explicitly refuses raw 2048-bit ECFP 'since this repo's own finding on lig2d_ext is that a wide 2D descriptor block is actively harmful here'; CNPRES_* variants predict the frozen model's residual and are anchored so they equal OFFSET_K1 at initialisation. (d) src/lanthanide_separation/gen10/setcontext.py — permutation-equivariant set encoder over the whole query design: e_i = MLP(absolute condition_i), g = mean/attention pool, s_i = MLP([e_i,g,cond_i]) minus its own mean. (e) src/lanthanide_separation/simplicial.py + deep_evaluation.py — antisymmetric simplicial message passing on Vietoris-Rips complexes over 3D metal-centred subcomplexes. (f) generations/gen12_eu_pred/gen12eu/dmpnn.py — a hand-reproduced Yang-2019 D-MPNN over the extractant molecular graph (directed bond messages, conditions concatenated AFTER message passing); the docstring records that chemprop could not be imported without mutating the shared environment. (g) generations/gen19_chem_transfer M1-M7: models/neural.py:93-131 (M1 e_m = A z_m + e_series + e_ox + e_element, e_l = W_l z_l + delta_l[system], h = SiLU/Linear condition encoder (32,32), head (64,64) with dropout 0.1; M2 adds the bilinear e_m^T P Q^T e_l; one-hot categoricals, median imputation with __missing indicators, standardisation; AdamW lr 3e-3, warmup 10, batch 512, Huber delta 1, grad clip 5, patience 30, max 300 epochs, <=200k parameters, emb dim <=16) and models/ladder.py:13-48 (M3 mechanism experts, M4 publication-group hierarchy, M5 pairwise loss, M6 physics hinge + embedding smoothness, M7 5-member heteroscedastic ensemble), plus models/shared_only.py (an H3-side subclass with e_series/e_ox frozen at zero). TORCH IN gen13-gen19: no module under gen13_separation, gen14_direction, gen16_anchor, gen16_leads, gen16_protocol, gen17_pairdiff or gen18_process imports torch — the only matches are gen15_curve/exp/ side experiments (exp/embed/encode.py, encode_molformer.py, exp/tabpfn/tp_precompute.py) and gen16_leads/scripts/g16_env_check.py, which merely pins expected versions. In gen19 torch appears only in models/{neural,ladder,shared_only}.py, three scripts and four tests. So the entire gen13-gen18 zero-shot lineage, including G14 and the bag, is sklearn-only (ExtraTrees / LogisticRegression / Ridge / IsotonicRegression). Verified installed: torch 2.13.0.

findings.topic: Fold plan, designs and the scoring/inference stack a k-shot study must not reimplement
findings.detail: splits.py:24 SPLIT_SEEDS = (104729, 130363, 155921, 196613, 262147), :25 N_SPLITS = 5, :26 N_INNER_SPLITS = 4, giving 25 folds per design (anchors.json confirms 25 for each of B, BR, BQ, A, BP). splits.py:27-29 MODEL_SEED_BASE 42, FOLD_SEED_STRIDE 1009, FOLD_SEED_OFFSET 9999991 and :58-60 model_seed = 42 + fold*1009 + 9999991 — a function of the FOLD index only, not the split seed (the gen7 harness contract). Designs (splits.py:30-44): group column is chemotype for B/BP/BR/BQ and extractant for A; BP drops every training cell whose publication appears among the held-out cells; BR drops the same NUMBER of training cells at random; BQ drops whole training publications until at least as many cells AND as many distinct condition series are gone. splits.py:124-149 assert_fold_integrity raises on any extractant/ecfp_cluster/chemotype crossing a boundary and on publication overlap under BP; every run_spec.json I read records overlaps 0 and publication_overlap 0. Metrics (metrics.py:51-118): per_extractant gives mae_all / mae_adjacent (dZ==1 plus Nd-Sm across the Pm gap, :34-36) / mae_far (dZ>=5, :29) / sign_acc_strong (|y|>=0.3, :30) / pair_spearman (cells with >=4 metals, :31); summarise macro-averages over extractants within a seed then over seeds, and metrics.py:17-18 warns pooled numbers are descriptive only because one chemotype holds 375 of 521 cells. Inference (inference.py:41-104 paired_contrasts): reference minus candidate per extractant, chemotype-blocked bootstrap, 10,000 replicates, seed 8675309, percentile + BCa intervals from the SAME draws, mde_80 = 2.80*bootstrap sd, and passes_P1 requires point >= 0.02 AND both intervals exclude 0 AND p<0.05 AND >=4/5 seeds positive AND LOCO sign stability (:92-102). gen16_leads/START_HERE.md:187-190 instructs: 'Import the frozen machinery, never reimplement it ... If you find yourself writing your own metric, splitter or bootstrap, stop.'

findings.topic: Cohort reproducibility check I ran (read-only) — 8 columns are not bit-identical
findings.detail: I rebuilt the cohort in memory (gen13sep.cohort.build_cohort('exact')) and compared it to the committed manifests/cohort_exact.parquet. Shape, column list, dtypes and every cell_id match exactly; pandas assert_frame_equal passes at default tolerance. BUT the fingerprint differs: fresh build 854171b03411d901 vs the recorded 4c3c6628ea0be949 (manifests/cohort_exact.json, and the value every run_spec.json and models/deploy.json pins). Recomputing the fingerprint from the STORED parquet under this pandas gives 4c3c6628ea0be949, so the hash function and pandas are not the cause. Column-by-column: exactly 8 columns differ, all of them replicate standard deviations — replicate_sd_median (1 cell, max abs diff 1.4e-17), repsd__La (1, 5.6e-17), repsd__Pr (1, 5.6e-17), repsd__Sm (1, 1.1e-16), repsd__Tb (3, 1.1e-16), repsd__Dy (1, 2.2e-16), repsd__Yb (1, 2.2e-16), repsd__Lu (2, 2.2e-16). These are last-bit floating-point differences in the groupby std at cohort.py:159-168, consistent with the numpy/scipy minor-version drift between the recording environment (numpy 2.5.3) and this venv (numpy 2.5.1). None of these columns is a feature or a target (repsd__* and replicate_sd_median are in FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_TOKENS at cohort.py:64-65 and are never read by a model), so no score should move — but the cohort fingerprint, which is the programme's identity check, does NOT reproduce in this environment, and the committed parquet is therefore the authoritative artefact to load. I did not run the anchor tests themselves (they were collected only), so whether G14 BP still equals 0.5000794414203691 here is unverified.

findings.topic: TOPO39 has only 22-28 distinct values — the capacity limit behind G14
findings.detail: Measured live over the 521-cell cohort: the 39 TOPO39 columns take only 28 distinct vectors across all cells and 22 distinct vectors across the 289 rich cells. GEN14_REPORT.md:58-60 gives this as the mechanism for the logistic beating the trees: 'A linear model on 39 columns extrapolates to a topology vector it has not seen; a forest can only interpolate between the 22 distinct vectors the corpus contains.' Consequences for a k-shot study: (a) the effective ligand-side design has ~22 points, not 90 extractants or 289 cells, which is consistent with the Kish n_eff ~12 quoted at models.py:8-11; (b) g14_predict.py:105-106 flags a query whose topology vector matches no training row, and GEN14_REPORT.md:191-203 documents the one identified failure mode — an alpha-alkylated diglycolamide whose 39 columns are bit-identical to an ordinary strongly heavy-selective DGA but whose selectivity is reversed; a seven-column steric block tried against it made things worse (0.920 -> 0.720 macro accuracy on strongly directed extractants under BP). Any k-shot design that treats TOPO39 as a continuous 39-dimensional ligand space will overstate its own coverage.

findings.topic: The existing few-shot machinery a k-shot study should build on, not re-derive
findings.detail: Three layers already exist. (a) gen13sep/fewshot.py:1-22 — one-pair adapters on a predicted centred curve: no_model_linear (ignore the model, set the slope in standardised radius from the measured pair), rescale (gain ratio shrunk toward 1), basis_shift (move along the basis direction that changes the measured contrast, lam=0.7); support pairs drawn deterministically per (cell, repeat) via blake2b, NOT python hash (fewshot.py:35-36 stable_hash) — this is the fix for the salted-hash trap; query pairs exclude the support pair. (b) gen13sep/fewshot_stage2.py:1-31 — the BLUP: u_hat = Sigma d (d' Sigma d + sigma^2)^-1 r with Sigma the between-metal residual covariance estimated LEAVE-CHEMOTYPE-OUT from the held-out residuals of other chemotypes of the same split seed, so no cell and no member of its chemotype contributes to its own correction; basis_shift is the special case where Sigma is the basis Gram matrix. (c) gen15/fewshot.py:1-21 — the same comparison inside the gen15 bench with three additions: a FIXED scoring set (support pairs removed from scoring at every k so k=0,1,2,3 are byte-identical questions), a direction-conditional curvature after the measurement, and the choice of WHICH pair to measure (widest dZ vs greedy D-optimal under the residual covariance); NOISE_VAR = 0.09 at gen15/fewshot.py:45-47 is the locked stage-2 value, two independent log D readings at the cohort median within-replicate sd 0.212. The deployed gen13 predictor already ships the covariance and the greedy design (g13_predict.py:80-100, models/deploy.json suggested_pairs La-Lu, Ce-Tm, Eu-Yb). Also relevant: src/lanthanide_separation/kshot_calibration.py:1-31 documents the within-cell transitivity trap — log_SF(A,C) = log_SF(A,B) + log_SF(B,C) holds exactly inside a cell, so a query pair spanned by support pairs is an arithmetic consequence of the support and must be stratified out ('all' vs 'free' rows via union-find), and the model-free null is the two-parameter trend fit on the same k measurements.

findings.topic: Secondary zero-shot arms that exist and were measured null — do not re-run them as novel
findings.detail: gen13sep/arms_stage2.py enumerates the parametrisation and weighting branch and DECISION_REPORT.md:390-396 closes it at <=0.006: CentredRowArm (:99-155, trees on the centred row target with rich metal descriptors, aggregate mean/median, balanced/reliability weights) scores 0.489 vs C_DIRECT_ROW 0.495 on design B, p=0.71, not LOCO-stable, and its BP swap S4_BAG_MIX3C is -0.013 against V2_BAG_MIX3 with 0/5 seeds; MedianCoefficientArm (:158-184, forest median instead of mean — the L1 readout), ReliabilityWeightedArm (:187-222), StackArm (:225-290, convex weights on a simplex grid chosen on inner-validation chemotypes), HierarchicalCurveArm (:333-415, extractant-level ligand model plus a condition deviation head) which DECISION_REPORT.md:394 calls 'the worst arm' that 'loses to its own condition-free ablation', ExtractantBalancedArm (:445-470). gen13sep/models.py also holds KernelCoefficientArm (:418-473, kernel ridge on Tanimoto(ECFP) x RBF(conditions)), HybridPhysicsResidualArm (:476-497), ProjectedDirectArm (:382-399), HelperBlockArm (:505-614, the add/gated/residual/shuffled protocol for an opt-in block with a width-matched permutation null). gen15/shape.py adds the curvature ladder: curv_constant (:54-67, weighted median instead of mean), curv_direction_conditional (:70-91), curv_sign_model (:97-121), shape_alphabet (:150-179, weighted k-medians on (a,b) with a multiclass logistic assignment). gen15/shape.py:5-8 records that giving each cell its own true b takes BP MAE from 0.500 to 0.427 (O_CURV 0.4272 in g15_locate_board.csv), so curvature is a measured 0.073 of headroom that no deployed arm claims.

reusable_components.what: The general arm bench: a candidate is arm(ctx) -> coef of shape (n_test, 2), scored on byte-identical pairs with gen13's frozen metrics and chemotype-blocked bootstrap. Ctx (:49-90) carries bench, design, seed, fold, train/test indices, balanced weights w, model_seed, the named feature-index sets fs, the LEAN matrix X, the rich mask, and the convenience accessors amp, cur, feat(name), rich_train(), rich_weights(), train_mean_curvature/amplitude/magnitude. score() (:139-161) returns the five-design board, contrasts and tables in one call; wide() (:164-167) pivots to an arm x design matrix.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen15 import valuebench as V; then V.score(bench, {'FLAT': arms.flat, 'G14': arms.g14, 'MY_KSHOT': my_arm}, designs=('B','BR','BQ','A','BP'), comps={'MY_vs_G14': ('G14','MY_KSHOT')}). Put generations/gen15_curve, gen14_direction and gen13_separation on sys.path first — import gen16.bootstrap (gen16_leads/gen16/bootstrap.py:23-25) to do it the way the frozen scripts do. The bench object comes from gen14.dirbench.load().
reusable_components.caveats: An arm must return exactly (n_test, 2) coefficients, so a genuine k-shot arm that corrects a whole 14-vector curve does not fit this signature — gen15/fewshot.py exists precisely because of that and uses its own loop over all_folds. valuebench writes nothing, but RESULTS at :45 points into gen15_curve/results, which holds committed CSVs. A k-shot arm must also not read ctx.bench.Y at a test index unless the support pairs are then removed from scoring.

reusable_components.what: The frozen direction bench: load() with an on-disk pickle cache (:56-67), feature_sets() giving the 17 named column-index sets over the LEAN matrix including TOPO39 (:73-114), run() for out-of-fold (p, magnitude) per cell (:129-161), unit_hits / Blocked / direction_board / paired_gain for chemotype-blocked macro accuracy (:167-232), and decision() for the hard/expected/sqrt rules (:238-255).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen14 import dirbench as db; bench = db.load(); FS = db.feature_sets(bench); oof = db.run(bench, 'NAME', M.candidate(M.dir_logistic(), M.amp_constant), features=FS['TOPO39'], design='BP'). To reproduce G14's deployed curve use db.decision(p, mag, 'hard') and assemble np.c_[a, bmean] @ bench.basis exactly as scripts/g14_value.py:88 does.
reusable_components.caveats: CACHE at :44 is generations/gen14_direction/cache/bench.pkl, which is gitignored (.gitignore:91) and currently does not exist on this machine, so the first load() rebuilds the bench (about a minute) and WRITES that file — the only write in the path, and it is an ignored directory, not a tracked artefact. MIN_METALS=5 and MIN_TRAIN=40 are baked in; run() silently SKIPS a fold that fails either guard or that has single-signed training amplitudes (:146), so a fold count below 25 is possible and should be asserted, not assumed.

reusable_components.what: The direction models and amplitude priors as plain closures with the uniform signature fit_predict(Xtr, amp, w, groups, Xte, seed, ext) -> ndarray: dir_logistic (the deployed G14 estimator, :123-147), dir_extratrees (gen13's locked 400 trees, :96-108), dir_always_heavy (:80-87), dir_train_majority (:90-93), dir_svm, dir_logistic_cv, dir_from_regression, dir_blend, dir_threshold; amp_constant (:254-256), amp_regression, amp_trees, amp_shrunk; candidate() to compose (:293-299); confidence_weights and extractant_units as optional label treatments.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: import gen14.models as M; M.candidate(M.dir_logistic(), M.amp_constant) is exactly the deployed G14 arm, and gen15/arms.py:32-38 _logistic_sign shows how to call dir_logistic() directly to get the sign vector for a k-shot arm.
reusable_components.caveats: Defaults matter: dir_logistic() with no arguments is the deployed configuration (C=1.0, weights='balanced', units='cell', label='cell', penalty='l2', transform='std'). GEN14_REPORT.md:165-174 records every non-default as a measured loss (inner-CV C -0.086 BP, C=0.3 -0.042, L1 -0.021, rank transform -0.105, PCA -0.008, confidence weights +-0.003, extractant units -0.007), so changing one silently changes the baseline. dir_from_regression is a measured failure (-0.045 to -0.062 in all five designs) and amp_regression is unstable (1.09-1.15 macro MAE in results/g14_value_BP.csv).

reusable_components.what: FLAT, MEAN_CURVE, G14 and G13_FULL as ready reference arms, plus every O_* oracle and the two non-oracle query-side candidates (query_span_magnitude, n_metals_magnitude). _logistic_sign (:32-38) is the reusable G14 direction call; _fit_magnitude_1d (:41-62) is a reusable isotonic-or-log-linear one-covariate magnitude fit.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen15 import arms as A; VALUE_ARMS = {'FLAT': A.flat, 'G14': A.g14} is literally what gen16/anchors.py:31 uses to produce the published anchors, so starting a k-shot study from that dict guarantees the baseline matches the anchor digits.
reusable_components.caveats: A.mean_curve is the two-coefficient mean, NOT gen13's B1_MEAN_CURVE 14-vector mean — they score 0.6217 and 0.639 under BP respectively, so quoting one as the other misstates the baseline by 0.017. Every O_* arm reads held-out truth and can never appear in a deployed comparison; gen15 GEN15_REPORT and the gen15 honest-floor memory note that an in-sample oracle is not a ceiling.

reusable_components.what: The frozen fold plan for all five designs: build_folds / all_folds returning Fold objects with train_index, test_index, inner_train_index, inner_validation_index, held_out_groups and the model_seed property; assert_fold_integrity as the leakage guard; fold_plan and max_train_tanimoto (with the far/mid/near banding at 0.40/0.60) for similarity reporting.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen13sep.splits import all_folds; for f in all_folds(bench.frame, design='BP'): ... — this is how dirbench.run (:143), amplitude_bench.run_candidate (:124) and valuebench.run_arms (:102) all iterate, so reusing it keeps pairs byte-identical across generations.
reusable_components.caveats: It imports lanthanide_separation.gen6.cohorts.seeded_group_kfold via gen13sep.paths, which inserts src/ into sys.path as an import side effect (paths.py:15-17) and also mkdirs eight output directories under gen13_separation (paths.py:41-43) — importing the package touches the filesystem. model_seed depends only on the fold index, not the split seed, so two seeds share model seeds by design; reproducibility of the plan must be tested in a SUBPROCESS (test_anchors.py:40-49) because of salted hash().

reusable_components.what: paired_contrasts: reference-minus-candidate per extractant with the chemotype as the resampling block, one shared set of 10,000 draws (seed 8675309) feeding the percentile interval, the BCa interval and the two-sided p, plus seeds_positive, leave-one-chemotype-out sign stability, mde_80 = 2.80 x bootstrap sd, passes_intervals and the full pre-registered passes_P1 rule. HIGHER_IS_BETTER negates sign accuracy and Spearman so positive always favours the candidate.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen13sep.inference import paired_contrasts; paired_contrasts(per_extractant_table, {'LABEL': ('reference_arm','candidate_arm')}, value='mae_all', replicates=10000). gen15/valuebench.py:134-136 wraps it as contrasts().
reusable_components.caveats: It needs a per-extractant table in gen13sep.metrics.per_extractant layout and silently SKIPS a comparison whose reference or candidate column is absent (:57-58) or that has fewer than 3 finite deltas (:61-62) — an empty result frame means 'not computed', not 'no effect'. MARGIN is fixed at 0.02 (:29) and MIN_SEEDS_POSITIVE at 4 (:30). With 45 chemotypes and ~12 effective units the intervals are wide: gen11's lesson recorded in memory is that an inconclusive-by-power result is not a null.

reusable_components.what: The curve algebra: centre_rows, physics_basis_matrix (named fixed bases, rows normalised to sqrt(14)), fit_coefficients / fit_all_coefficients (per-cell ridge 0.5 on observed metals only), curves (coef -> 14-vector), fit_data_basis (rank-K weighted ALS on observed entries with a fixed sign rule), explained_variance.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen13sep.basis import physics_basis_matrix, fit_all_coefficients, curves — the three calls needed to turn any (amplitude, curvature) pair into a 14-metal curve and any observed centred matrix into labels.
reusable_components.caveats: DEFAULT_RIDGE = 0.5 is load-bearing: a two-metal cell's coefficient is shrunk 30-40% (arms_stage2.py:20-21), so the LABEL a k-shot study fits is itself a shrunk quantity and a two-metal cell is not a weak version of a fourteen-metal cell. fit_data_basis is fold-dependent (fitted on the training centred matrix), so any arm using it is not comparable to a fixed-basis arm column-for-column.

reusable_components.what: descriptors_for(smiles) -> the full 114-column coordination-topology row from one SMILES and nothing else; build_table for many; family_of / columns_by_family for the five families (donor, motif, arm, dist, arch); use_spec / active_spec_path / spec_digest for the frozen-vs-posthoc specification switch.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen122 import coordination; d = coordination.descriptors_for(smiles) — this is exactly how both deployed predictors featurise a new ligand (g14_predict.py:88-93, g13_predict.py:109). Prefix every key with coord__ if it is not already prefixed, as both callers do.
reusable_components.caveats: TWO specifications exist and they differ: the frozen v1.1.0 (config/coordination_smarts.json) is what every locked result was computed against, and a post-hoc file corrects four rule-level defects found after the locked evaluation (coordination.py:96-101, and the ring/lactam branches at :139-141 and :165-169 switch on it). Using the post-hoc spec silently changes TOPO39 and therefore G14. use_spec clears the lru_caches, but the module-level cache means a process that has already computed descriptors under one spec must be restarted or explicitly switched. The training-side COORD block is READ from the frozen parquet (183 extractants x 114), not recomputed, so a new ligand's descriptors come from a different code path than the training rows'.

reusable_components.what: per_extractant (one row per seed x extractant x arm with mae_all, mae_adjacent, mae_far, sign_acc_strong, pair_spearman) and summarise (extractant-macro within seed then over seeds, chemotype-macro, pooled), plus pair_rows_for_cell, is_adjacent, heavier_always_sign_accuracy, effective_sample_size.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen13sep.metrics import per_extractant, summarise — gen15/valuebench.py:128-131 board() is a two-line wrapper, and reusing it is what keeps a new number comparable with every locked table.
reusable_components.caveats: macro_mae_extractant is THE metric; pooled columns are descriptive only because one chemotype holds 375 of 521 cells (metrics.py:17-18) and the repo's own memory records pooled and macro ranking arms in opposite orders. mae_adjacent includes the Nd-Sm pair across the promethium gap (:34-36), which is not a true dZ=1 neighbour. pair_spearman is computed only for cells with >=4 metals and returns NaN for a constant prediction, so FLAT has no Spearman.

reusable_components.what: The four-test drift guard: fold-plan sha256 recomputed in a subprocess, G14 and FLAT under BP to four decimals, both plus the G14_vs_FLAT contrast to full float precision against results/anchors/anchors.json, and (slow) the gen13 stage-3 direction headline exactly.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Run python -m pytest generations/gen16_leads/tests -q -m 'not slow' before trusting any new number, and again after adding any dependency; generations/gen16_leads/scripts/g16_anchors.py regenerates the recorded JSON and ANCHORS.md.
reusable_components.caveats: The recorded environment (anchors.json) is python 3.14.5 / numpy 2.5.3 / scipy 1.18.1 / rdkit 2026.03.6; this venv is python 3.13.0 / numpy 2.5.1 / scipy 1.18.0 / rdkit 2026.03.5, and I measured a last-bit drift in the cohort's replicate-sd columns that already breaks the cohort fingerprint. I collected these tests but did not execute them, so whether the full-precision assertions still hold here is unverified — run them first. Do not install TabPFN (START_HERE.md:205-207: it pins sklearn<1.7 and pandas<3 and shifts every result by ~0.0014).

reusable_components.what: The deployable G14: fit() trains the logistic on all 289 well-determined cells and pickles the pipeline, the topo column list, the magnitude, the curvature, the basis and the set of training topology vectors; predict(smiles) returns direction, probability, confidence, amplitude, the 14-metal curve, logSF_La_Lu, the suggested first pair and a topology_unseen_in_training flag.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Read it as the exact specification of the deployed zero-shot model for a new SMILES; the fit() body at :51-84 is the shortest correct statement of G14 (imputer + scaler + LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=5000), rich cells, rich weights for the magnitude, full-cohort weights for the curvature).
reusable_components.caveats: MODEL at :48 is generations/gen14_direction/models/deploy.joblib and that directory does NOT exist in this checkout (nor is it tracked), so predict() cannot run until fit() is invoked — and fit() writes. Note the curvature at :73-74 is averaged over ALL cells with full-cohort weights while the magnitude at :72 uses rich cells and rich weights; a reimplementation that uses one convention for both will not reproduce 0.5000794414203691.

reusable_components.what: The BLUP one-pair correction with a leave-chemotype-out residual covariance, plus centred_residual, residual_covariance (pairwise-complete, shrunk toward its own diagonal), adapt_conditional and greedy_support_design — the estimator-aware choice of which pair to measure.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: from gen13sep.fewshot_stage2 import adapt_conditional, centred_residual, residual_covariance, greedy_support_design — exactly the imports g13_predict.py:52-53 uses; gen15/fewshot.py re-runs the same comparison inside the gen15 bench under all five designs.
reusable_components.caveats: Sigma must be estimated leave-chemotype-out from held-out residuals of OTHER chemotypes of the same split seed, or the correction leaks; the module enforces the convention but a caller that passes an in-sample covariance will silently get an optimistic number. gen16 found the measured-mode residual covariance indefinite and 90% intervals covering 98.8%, so the covariance is a usable point estimator but not a usable uncertainty model. NOISE_VAR 0.09 (gen15/fewshot.py:45-47) is an assumed value derived from the median within-replicate sd, not a fitted one.

risks.risk: The cohort fingerprint does not reproduce in this environment: a fresh build gives 854171b03411d901 against the recorded 4c3c6628ea0be949, caused by last-bit float differences in 8 replicate-sd columns (max abs diff 2.2e-16). Every run_spec.json and models/deploy.json pins the recorded value, so a k-shot study that rebuilds the cohort will either fail a fingerprint assertion or, worse, record a different fingerprint beside new numbers and make them look like a different cohort.
risks.mitigation: Load the committed generations/gen13_separation/manifests/cohort_exact.parquet rather than calling build_cohort(), or pin the environment to the recorded one (numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, rdkit 2026.03.6, python 3.14.5). Before anything else, run python -m pytest generations/gen16_leads/tests -q -m 'not slow' and report the digits: if G14 BP still equals 0.5000794414203691 the drift is confined to non-feature columns and is harmless to scores; if it does not, stop and fix the environment first. The differing columns (replicate_sd_median, repsd__*) are in FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_TOKENS and are read by no model, so a score change would indicate a second, unrelated cause.

risks.risk: Two different arms are called 'the mean curve' and they differ by 0.017 under BP: gen15/arms.mean_curve (two balanced-mean coefficients) scores 0.6217 while gen13's B1_MEAN_CURVE (weighted nanmean of the 14-vectors) scores 0.639. A k-shot study that quotes a gain over 'MEAN_CURVE' without saying which one is not comparable to either generation.
risks.mitigation: Quote gains over FLAT (0.5885062528901843, identical in all five designs because it has no training dependence) as the primary floor, exactly as gen15/arms.py:92-94 and the gen15 honest-floor finding prescribe, and name the mean-curve variant explicitly whenever it is used. FLAT is also the only baseline that cannot drift with the environment.

risks.risk: G14 is defined by its conventions as much as by its estimator: the n_metals>=5 training filter plus taking the magnitude from rich cells is worth 0.038 of the 0.561 -> 0.500 improvement, against 0.023 for the estimator (GEN14_REPORT.md:95-97). The magnitude and the curvature are also averaged over DIFFERENT populations with DIFFERENT weights (rich cells / rich weights vs all cells / full weights). A reimplementation that applies one convention uniformly will silently produce a different 'existing baseline' and every k-shot delta will be measured against the wrong zero.
risks.mitigation: Do not reimplement G14. Call gen15.arms.g14 or compose gen14.models.candidate(gen14.models.dir_logistic(), gen14.models.amp_constant) and assemble the curve exactly as scripts/g14_value.py:76-88 does, then assert the BP score equals 0.5000794414203691 before adding any k-shot layer.

risks.risk: The ligand feature pipeline for a NEW extractant is not the pipeline used in training. DONORS (13 columns) is read in training from the frozen gen6 Architector census, but g13_predict.py:128-146 approximates it from coordination counts with chem__core_cn hard-coded to 9.0 and chem__dentate derived from a rounded, clipped topology descriptor; LIG2D is left entirely NaN for new rows (g13_predict.py:188). A k-shot study whose queries are genuinely new SMILES is therefore evaluating a different feature map from the one the cross-validated numbers were produced with.
risks.mitigation: For a k-shot study scored on the frozen 90-extractant cohort this does not bite — all features come from the frozen tables. It bites only for truly novel queries. Prefer G14, whose entire input is TOPO39 and therefore exactly recomputable from SMILES by the same code path in both directions (g14_predict.py:87-94 calls the same coordination.descriptors_for the frozen table was built from), and state explicitly that any arm using DONORS or LIG2D has a new-ligand fidelity gap. If DONORS is needed, obtain the real Architector census rather than the approximation.

risks.risk: TOPO39 takes only 22 distinct values over the 289 rich cells (28 over all 521). A k-shot design that samples 'new ligands' by perturbing a 39-dimensional vector, or that assumes 82 independent ligand observations, will dramatically overstate its own power; the effective number of units for a chemotype-level scalar is about 12 (Kish n_eff, models.py:8-11).
risks.mitigation: Treat the ligand side as ~22 design points and power the study on extractants-as-units with the chemotype as the resampling block, which is what inference.paired_contrasts already does. Report mde_80 alongside every point estimate and, following the gen11 lesson, label an underpowered result inconclusive rather than null. Carry the topology_unseen_in_training flag (g14_predict.py:105-106) on every query.

risks.risk: Within-cell transitivity makes some k-shot query pairs arithmetic consequences of the support: log_SF(A,C) = log_SF(A,B) + log_SF(B,C) holds exactly inside a cell, and gen13's cells are complete graphs. Without stratification the measured k-shot gain is partly free arithmetic, not model performance — the trap kshot_calibration.py:1-31 was restructured to prevent.
risks.mitigation: Stratify every query row into 'all' and 'free' (not spanned by the support) with a union-find per cell over the fixed k_max support pool, so the stratum does not change with k, exactly as src/lanthanide_separation/kshot_calibration.py specifies. Also adopt gen15/fewshot.py's fixed scoring set — remove the support pairs from scoring at EVERY k so k=0,1,2,3 are byte-identical questions — and always report the model-free null (NAIVE_LINE / the two-parameter trend fit on the same k measurements), which at D-optimal k=3 scores 0.2347 against the model's 0.1700.

risks.risk: Python's hash() is salted per process and silently broke cross-run pairing in gen8. Two live uses remain in gen13: arms_stage2.py:330 extractant_key hashes fingerprint bytes to identify extractants, and that key feeds HierarchicalCurveArm and ExtractantBalancedArm. Any k-shot support draw or cell pairing built on hash() will not reproduce across processes.
risks.mitigation: Use gen13sep.fewshot.stable_hash (blake2b, fewshot.py:35-36), which is what the locked few-shot protocol already uses for support-pair draws, and test any split or draw reproducibility in a SUBPROCESS as test_anchors.py:40-49 does rather than only in-session. Avoid the two arms_stage2 arms that depend on extractant_key, both of which are measured nulls anyway.

risks.risk: ECFP (2048) and LIG2D (206) are known-harmful and excluded from every deployed configuration, yet they are present in the default BLOCK_ORDER and in ALL_BLOCKS, so a run that passes the default blocks silently includes them (the all-blocks runs record n_features 2463). G13_FULL_MODEL on the 209 lean columns already scores 0.552 under BP against G14's 0.500, and the memory record is that deleting LIG2D is the only block removal that is a significant gain.
risks.mitigation: Pass LEAN_BLOCKS explicitly (amplitude_bench.py:45) or a named subset from dirbench.feature_sets, and assert the resulting column count (209 for LEAN, 39 for TOPO39) before fitting. Never accept the default block list for a transfer claim.

risks.risk: Design choice drives the conclusion. G14 spans only 0.4906-0.5001 across the five designs (range 0.010) but the 209-column regression spans 0.437-0.552 (range 0.115), looking best under the leaky exact-extractant design A and worst under BP. gen13 DECISION_REPORT.md:584 states outright that design B must not select the deployed model. A k-shot study that reports one design, or that selects on B, will reach the opposite ranking from the deployment-relevant one.
risks.mitigation: Report all five designs for every arm, as gen13 Addendum 3 requires and as valuebench.score() does in one call, and let BP select. State the regime with every number (the repo's own standing rule), and quote each increment against the cheapest sensible alternative as well as against FLAT.

risks.risk: Pair orientation differs between generations: gen13/gen14 enumerate a<b so A is the LIGHTER lanthanide (metrics.py:39-41), while gen19 defines state_a as the HEAVIER state (pairs.py:12-14). Any signed quantity — a direction label, a sign accuracy by class, a per-pair residual carried between the stacks — flips.
risks.mitigation: Fix one orientation for the k-shot study, state it in the report, and assert it in code from the dZ sign (gen13's dZ = Z[b]-Z[a] >= 0). MAE and direction accuracy are orientation-invariant (pairs.py:13-14), so prefer those for cross-generation comparison and never carry signed per-pair values across the boundary.

risks.risk: gen19 M0 is not a drop-in 'predict two log D then subtract' baseline for the gen13 BP cohort: different corpus (12,411 MODEL rows from dataset_all_metals vs 521 cells from the frozen bundle), different unit (rows vs cells), different hold-out semantics (V1/V2/V5 vs chemotype+publication BP), different extractant identity (extractant_system_key vs canonical_smiles), and an inner-tuning design that assumes three simultaneous inner cell folds rather than gen13's single 4-way inner chemotype split. Treating its published 0.3499 V5 macro MAE as comparable to G14's 0.500 BP would be a category error — different metric, different target, different corpus, different regime.
risks.mitigation: If a log-D-then-subtract baseline is wanted, build it inside the gen13 stack (C_DIRECT_ROW already is exactly that: trees on raw log D with Z and radius, differenced in-cell) rather than porting M0. If M0 itself is required, scope the bridge explicitly — map cells to gen19 row frames, supply a FitContext with hidden_index and isolation_check, and replace the inner design — and budget from measurements_B5.json (5.8-69 s inner fit and 2.3-69 s outer refit per fold at ~11k training rows, ~0.8 GB peak RSS). Never compare the two numbers directly without restating both in one metric.

risks.risk: Several results in this repo are known to be fragile in ways that would silently contaminate a k-shot study: seed-pooled centring contaminated gen11's published level/shape numbers (centre within fold and seed, never across); the min_rows cohort filter was the real ceiling in gen5 (it discarded 37 of 47 chemically novel extractants); and installing TabPFN pins sklearn<1.7 and pandas<3 and moves every result by ~0.0014 against effects of 0.004-0.02.
risks.mitigation: Read generations/gen16_leads/START_HERE.md:195-215 (the known-traps list) before designing the study; centre within fold and seed; audit any cohort filter before accepting it; add no dependency without re-running the anchor tests and reverting if an anchor moves.

risks.risk: The gen14 bench cache is gitignored and absent, and the two deploy artefacts are inconsistent: generations/gen13_separation/models/ holds only deploy.json (the .joblib is untracked and absent) and generations/gen14_direction/models/ does not exist. Any k-shot study that expects to load a frozen fitted model will instead silently refit, or crash.
risks.mitigation: Plan to rebuild: dirbench.load() regenerates cache/bench.pkl (about a minute, into a gitignored directory) and g14_predict.py fit / g13_predict.py fit regenerate the deploy payloads. Record the cohort fingerprint and the environment beside anything refitted, and do not assume the refit reproduces the recorded fingerprint (see the first risk).

numbers.name: G14 extractant-macro MAE of log SF, design BP (the anchor)
FLAT (predict 0) extractant-macro MAE, BP (identical in all five designs)

open_questions: Do the four anchor tests still PASS in this venv? I collected them (4 tests) but did not execute them, and I measured a last-bit cohort drift that already changes the cohort fingerprint (854171b03411d901 vs the recorded 4c3c6628ea0be949). Running python -m pytest generations/gen16_leads/tests -q is the single highest-value next action; it is cheap (~30 s for the non-slow set, plus ~16 s for the slow gen13 anchor).

Which 'Model 1' is actually intended — G14 (0.5001 BP, two degrees of freedom, TOPO39 only, exactly recomputable from SMILES) or gen13's deployed V2_BAG4@lean (0.536 BP, four ExtraTrees members on 209 lean columns)? They are different models with different costs (0.03 s vs ~4 s per fold) and different new-ligand fidelity (G14 needs only TOPO39; the bag needs the approximated DONORS block). The task brief quotes 0.500 for 'the deployed gen14 model', which points at G14, but the repo also calls the bag 'the configuration to deploy' (DECISION_REPORT.md:429-436).

Is the k-shot study scored on the frozen 90-extractant cohort (where all features come from frozen tables and the DONORS approximation is irrelevant) or on genuinely novel SMILES (where it is a real fidelity gap)? This changes which arms are admissible.

Should the curvature coefficient b be part of the k-shot study? gen15/shape.py:5-8 measures that giving each cell its own true b takes BP from 0.500 to 0.427 — 0.073 of headroom that no deployed arm claims, and that one measurement might partly recover. The curvature ladder (curv_constant, curv_direction_conditional, curv_sign_model, shape_alphabet) already exists but I did not read its result board, so whether any feasible curvature arm beat the constant is unresolved here.

The recovery plan LANTHANIDE_SEPARATION_RECOVERY_PLAN.md (repo root, Russian, never executed) defines six R2 variants, hierarchical weights and a section-8 k-shot protocol with hash-defined fixed query sets and an arithmetic-closure rule. I did not read it in this audit. Its arithmetic-closure rule is almost certainly the same transitivity trap kshot_calibration.py documents, and its hash-defined query sets must use blake2b rather than python hash(); both should be checked against that file before the design is fixed.

Does the gen14 bench cache need rebuilding, and does the rebuild reproduce? cache/bench.pkl is gitignored and absent, so the first dirbench.load() rebuilds it from the freshly built cohort — which is the artefact whose fingerprint does not reproduce here. Whether a bench built from the fresh cohort still yields G14 BP = 0.5000794414203691 is exactly what the anchor test would settle.

What inner-validation budget does a k-shot arm get? gen13 folds carry a single 4-way inner chemotype split (splits.py:105-107, N_INNER_SPLITS 4), and gen14 measured that choosing the logistic penalty on that inner split costs -0.086 under BP (GEN14_REPORT.md:165-166) — the inner split does not predict the outer one. Any k-shot hyperparameter (shrinkage, covariance shrink, which pair to measure) therefore needs its selection cost paid honestly or fixed a priori.

Is the gen16 finding that the measured-mode residual covariance is indefinite and 90% intervals cover 98.8% already fixed anywhere in the code? gen13sep/fewshot_stage2.residual_covariance shrinks toward its own diagonal with shrink=0.25 and ridge=1e-3, which may or may not be the response to that finding; I did not trace the fix, and it matters because the BLUP is the natural k-shot point estimator.

gen19 M0's reported 0.3499 is a V5 unit-macro MAE on log D over 4101 rows — not comparable to G14's 0.500 extractant-macro MAE of log SF on the 521-cell cohort. If the study wants a 'predict two log D then subtract' comparator, is C_DIRECT_ROW inside the gen13 stack (which is exactly that model) acceptable, or is porting M0 genuinely required? The porting cost is new code plus a fold/unit/corpus bridge, not a configuration change.

audits.summary: A gen13 'cell' is one extractant x one publication_id x the exact 64-column cond__ key with NaN treated as a value, averaged per (cell, metal), >= 2 lanthanides (gen13sep/cohort.py:1-18, 133-161); the 'series' key mode is a sensitivity that drops contact_time/metal_concentration from the key and appends the gen6 experiment_series_id (cohort.py:55-57, 140, 149-152; cohort_series.json: 597 cells / 89 extractants), while gen8's 'series' and 'curve' are gen5 objects on a different cohort (5,248 log D rows / 152 extractants / 303 series / 1,176 one-axis curves, runs/gen8_architecture/series_audit.md:3-7). Setting B requires several cells of one extractant in one publication: 25 of 90 extractants have >= 2 cells in one publication, 17 have >= 3, 15 have >= 5, 11 have >= 10; 65 extractants have at most one cell per publication and 64 have exactly one cell in total (the untracked gen20 AUDIT.md A.3 agrees: 26 of 90 with >= 2 cells, 9 with >= 2 publications). Only 41 (extractant, publication, identical metal set) groups hold >= 3 cells, over 15 extractants and 8 chemotypes. Within the 38 multi-cell (extractant, publication) groups, acid concentration varies in 22 groups (363 cells), metal concentration in 13, extractant concentration in 12, contact time in 7, temperature in 6, diluent one-hots in up to 5 each, acid identity in 4; only 16 of the 38 groups vary a single axis family and 22 vary two or more, so most groups are grids, not titrations. For Setting A, 84 of 90 extractants have a largest cell with >= 4 metals (>= 6 pairs) and 44 have a full 14-metal cell, so k measured pairs can be drawn from one cell for almost every extractant without mixing conditions (gen20 AUDIT.md A.3 counts 275 cells / 81 extractants / 39 chemotypes eligible at k = 3 under its no-closure rule). Under the untracked gen20 plan's own Setting B definition (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:208-212: unit = (extractant, publication) with >= 2 cells sharing >= 1 adjacent pair; gate >= 10 extractants from >= 5 chemotypes) the strict-adjacent count is 27 units / 19 extractants / 11 chemotypes with 1,041 query adjacent pairs over 190 query cells, so the gate passes numerically; but three of the 27 units are literal duplicates (THDGA, TODGA, T2EHDGA in pub_b9dfc468cd: identical log D on all 8 metals, differing only by contact_time 15 vs NaN), leaving 23 units / 17 extractants / 11 chemotypes, and 63.7 % of the query pairs come from chemotype sc009 and 51.7 % from TODGA plus DMDODGA alone. The decisive fact is headroom: copying the adjacent log SF from one other cell of the same publication gives pooled MAE 0.105 (extractant-macro 0.116) against FLAT 0.160, and leave-one-cell-out copying gives 0.098 / 0.108; the median cross-condition change of an adjacent pair is 0.043 and 91 % of such changes are below 0.3, i.e. below the replicate floor (per-(cell, metal) sd 0.302, cohort_exact.json; adjacent y sd 0.231, gen13 DATA_AUDIT.md:65). A model can therefore gain at most ~0.05-0.1 over a no-model copy, which is under gen13's 0.02 margin by any realistic bootstrap on 11 chemotypes dominated by one, and the earlier cross_condition study already found the model indistinguishable from a pair-mean lookup from k ~ 2 on 12 DGA extractants (docs/results/kshot_calibration_study_20260817.md:23-27, 93-104, 148-154). Gen8's cross-series matrix says one measurement transfers within a curve type (acid->acid +0.190, extractant->extractant +0.243, lanthanide-series->lanthanide-series +0.332) and largely not across types (acid->metal_series -0.161, extractant->metal_series -0.180), 'a ligand has a level per series', 'measure in the system you intend to predict' (runs/gen8_architecture/cross_series/calibration_geography.md:66-116; docs/results/gen8_architecture_results_20260820.md:362-382; decision_report.md:42-45, 108-109); that was measured on log D level, and in log SF the level cancels, so Setting B inherits only the shape-transfer part, which is exactly what the copy baseline already captures. Gen19's 'V5 cell' is a (metal state x extractant system) unit, not a condition cell (folds/V5__cell_only__exact.json 'unit_type': 'cell', 'cells': [[metal, SMILES]]), gen19 uses a 17-field 6 s.f. condition key and heavier-first orientation and is not joined to gen13, so it offers no Setting B fold design. Recommendation: do not register Setting B as a claim-bearing experiment; either report it as infeasible-for-inference with the counts above, or run it only as the exploratory arm the plan already classes it as, on the 23 non-duplicate units, with the nearest-cell copy as the mandatory null and the Setting A k = 3 ladder on the query cell itself as the comparator.

findings.topic: What a 'cell' and a 'series' are, in each generation
findings.detail: gen13: a cell is one extractant x one gen6 publication_id x the exact 64-column cond__ key (NaN == NaN; floats rounded to 9 s.f.), with replicates averaged per (cell, metal) and >= 2 lanthanides; the publication was added to the key because 7 of 521 exact cells mixed two publications. The 'series' key mode is a sensitivity only: it drops cond__contact_time_min and cond__metal_concentration_mM from the key (RELAXABLE_CONDITION_COLUMNS) and appends the gen6 experiment_series_id so that rows with identical recorded conditions but different reconstructed series stay apart; it yields 597 cells / 89 extractants (vs 521 / 90 exact; 'relaxed' = 509 / 90). The cohort parquet carries 'experiment_series_ids' and 'safe_exp_ids' per cell, which is the only hook to gen8's curve tables. gen8 reuses gen5's series (one extractant x one setting of the categorical conditions) and defines a 'curve' as a maximal subset where exactly one axis varies; 303 series, 1,176 curves, 56 grids holding 3,183 of 5,248 rows; this is a log D cohort of 152 extractants, not the gen13 SF cohort.

findings.topic: Setting B gate as the gen20 plan defines it, counted with strict adjacent pairs
findings.detail: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (untracked) section 3.3 defines Setting B as: unit = (extractant, publication) with >= 2 cells sharing >= 1 adjacent pair; support = all pairs of 1 (then 2) support cells; query = adjacent pairs of the remaining cells; run only if >= 10 extractants from >= 5 chemotypes qualify under BP. findings.topic: Setting B headroom: the no-model copy already sits at the replicate floor
findings.detail: On strict adjacent pairs within one (extractant, publication): leave-one-cell-out copy (predict a pair by its mean over the other cells of the group) gives pooled MAE 0.098 and extractant-macro MAE 0.108 against FLAT 0.160 / 0.150 (1,412 rows, 19 extractants, 11 chemotypes). A deployable single-support-cell copy (nearest log acid concentration, ties first) gives pooled 0.105 / macro 0.116 against FLAT 0.160 / 0.156 (976 rows, 17 extractants); the median cross-condition change of an adjacent pair is 0.043, the 90th percentile 0.263, and 91.4 % of changes are below 0.3. Per extractant the copy MAE is 0.046-0.137 for 14 of 19, with only the sc060 tetraaza-pentacycle (0.256) and the sc029 phenanthroline diamide (0.396, worse than FLAT 0.234) and TBDGA (0.177) above 0.15. On all pairs the copy gives pooled 0.272 / macro 0.233 vs FLAT 0.663 / 0.473, and on far pairs (dZ >= 5) 0.415 vs 1.090. The replicate floor is median per-(cell, metal) sd 0.302 on this cohort (0.237 on the raw bundle), i.e. up to ~0.43 per pair if independent, and adjacent y has sd 0.231 overall, so the condition-to-condition change of an adjacent separation factor (median 0.043) is far inside measurement noise. For comparison the Setting A ladder on the same cohort reaches adjacent macro MAE 0.139 at D-optimal k = 3 (G14) and 0.154 at widest k = 1: one other-condition cell of the same paper is a better 'measurement' than three pairs of the query cell itself. Any model in Setting B therefore competes for at most ~0.05-0.10 of MAE on 11 chemotypes dominated by one, below gen13's 0.02 margin by any honest chemotype-blocked interval.

findings.topic: Q5: what gen8's cross-series finding implies for Setting B
findings.detail: gen8 measured one-shot offset calibration of the frozen log D model on 143 held-out ligands, with the measured row's curve type as rows and the predicted rows' curve type as columns. Gains over zero-shot: acid->acid +0.190 (69 ligands), extractant->extractant +0.243 (25), metal_series->metal_series +0.332 (85), temperature->temperature +0.025; off-diagonal mostly negative: acid->metal_series -0.161, extractant->metal_series -0.180, metal_series->acid -0.036, acid->extractant -0.028, extractant->acid -0.066, none->metal_series -0.590. The report's reading: 'A ligand does not have one level; it has a level per series' because the categorical conditions that define a series (diluent, modifier, acid identity) move the level as much as the ligand does; deployment consequence 'measure in the system you intend to predict'; the decision report records the pre-registered condition 'calibration helped only rows near the measured condition' as FAILED, partially, and headlines 'calibration is series-local'. Where in the sweep matters too: a measurement at a single-point acid series gives one-shot MAE 0.455, mid-acid 0.832, high 0.873, low 1.046; low-acid measurement costs +0.244 vs mid-range. Separately, the frozen model draws every unseen titration too flat (extractant slope 0.116 vs true 2.574, acid 0.355 vs 1.656), and its slope prediction is worse than the corpus-median null, so a model's predicted change across acid/extractant concentration is unreliable; the K3 adapter (level + lanthanide + acid slope + extractant-concentration slope, ridge-shrunk) beats K1 by +0.044 at k = 2 and +0.115 at k = 5 only because the slopes are measured on the ligand itself. Implications: (i) gen8 is a log D (level) result on a different cohort; in log SF the level cancels exactly, so Setting B inherits only the shape-transfer component, which the strongest diagonal (lanthanide series -> lanthanide series, +0.332) says transfers within one categorical series and the copy baseline above already captures; (ii) 8 of the 27 strict-adjacent units change the diluent and 4 change the acid identity between cells, which by gen5/gen8's definition makes them different series, so Setting B would mix within-series and cross-series transfer and must stratify by whether only a continuous axis (acid/extractant/metal concentration, temperature) or a categorical axis (diluent, acid, additive) differs; only 16 of 38 multi-cell groups vary one axis family and only 2 of the 21 stricter groups vary a single family; (iii) the k-shot calibration study's cross_condition regime (support from other conditions of the extractant, query = a held-out condition; 12 eligible extractants, 26 of 32 DGA analogues) found the model no better than a pair-mean lookup or a two-parameter dZ fit from k ~ 2 (model - PAIRMEAN -0.003 at k=1, -0.009 at k=10), which is the Setting B question already answered once in the negative for the model and in the positive for the measurement.

findings.topic: Q4: can a >= 10 extractant / >= 5 chemotype condition-adaptation experiment be built, and how would query/support be defined
findings.detail: Numerically yes on the plan's own definition (19 extractants / 11 chemotypes strict-adjacent; 17 / 11 after removing the three duplicate-only units; 13 / 7 if two support cells are required), and no for the cross-publication form (9 extractants / 4 chemotypes). A defensible definition, if run: unit = (extractant, publication) group from the 23 non-duplicate units; support cell = ONE cell chosen target-free by a declared rule (gen8's rule: mid-range acid, central lanthanides, i.e. the cell nearest the group's median log acid and median log extractant concentration; ties lexicographic by cell_id), and the support = all measured pairs of that cell (support labels are its true y); query = all strict-adjacent pairs of every other cell of the group whose pair type the support cell contains (1,041 pairs over 190 cells under the max-adjacent-pairs rule; a mid-acid rule would give a similar count but should be counted before sealing); fixed across every k, model and policy; a second budget adds a second support cell by the same rule on the remaining cells (20 units / 13 extractants / 7 chemotypes). Nulls: COPY (support cell's own y for the same pair), FLAT, and the Setting A ladder on the query cell itself (its own k = 1..3 pairs under no-closure) as the comparator that answers 'is another condition worth more than another pair'. Stratify every table by (a) single continuous axis differing (acid conc / extractant conc / metal conc / temperature), (b) categorical axis differing (diluent / acid identity / additive), (c) contact-time-only (noise); and by the log distance in acid concentration between support and query cells. Under BP the support cell's publication is masked from training and both cells sit in the same held-out fold, so no additional masking is needed; the 94 % publication fingerprint of the condition columns is not a leak here (support and query are the same laboratory by construction) but it means any condition-feature model will reproduce the support cell's curve regardless of chemistry, so the model-minus-COPY contrast is the only informative one. Effective sample size: 11 chemotypes with sc009 holding 9 of 19 extractants and 63.7 % of query pairs; TODGA+DMDODGA 51.7 %; chemotype-blocked bootstrap will be driven by two or three blocks.

findings.topic: Q6 recommendation
findings.detail: Setting B should not be registered as a claim-bearing experiment on this cohort. The gate passes on counts (19 extractants / 11 chemotypes; 17 / 11 after duplicate removal) but the quantity it asks a model to predict, the change of an adjacent separation factor between two conditions of the same paper, has median magnitude 0.043 and is below 0.3 in 91 % of cases, against a replicate floor of 0.30 per (cell, metal); a no-model copy of the support cell already scores 0.105-0.116 (FLAT 0.160) and beats the entire Setting A k = 3 ladder (0.139). The maximum model headroom is therefore ~0.05-0.10 on 11 chemotypes dominated by one (sc009, 63.7 % of queries) and two extractants (51.7 %), which cannot clear gen13's P1 margin of 0.02 with a chemotype-blocked BCa interval and a per-seed sign requirement, and the earlier cross_condition study (12 DGA extractants) already returned model = lookup from k ~ 2. gen8 adds that calibration is series-local on the level and that the frozen models mispredict condition slopes by 5-20x, so a model's claimed transfer across a diluent or acid change is not credible from this data. Two acceptable reports: (1) 'infeasible for inference' with the counts above and the copy-baseline numbers as the reason; or (2) the exploratory arm the plan already classes it as, on the 23 non-duplicate units, with COPY as the registered null, stratified by continuous-vs-categorical axis change, BH-corrected, and explicitly not a registered claim. If (2) is run, the only result worth reporting is whether any model beats COPY on the categorical-change stratum (8 units differ in diluent, 4 in acid identity), because the continuous-axis stratum is a replicate-floor measurement. Setting A, by contrast, is well-posed on 84 extractants without mixing conditions and is where the registered claims belong.

risks.mitigation: Treat contact_time-only and metal_concentration-only groups as a separate 'nuisance' stratum or run the relaxed/series key mode as a sensitivity (cohort_relaxed: 509 cells; cohort_series: 597 cells).

risks.risk: Inherited machinery defects: gen15 covariance indefinite in 100 % of estimates and over-covering intervals; no closure rule in gen15; gen13 metrics are lighter-first while gen19 is heavier-first.
risks.mitigation: Use the plan's BLUP20 (inner-OOF PSD covariance) and gen20k's stable SHA-256 seeding; keep gen13 orientation and never join gen19 tables.

risks.risk: The 94 % publication fingerprint in the condition columns means a condition-feature model in Setting B will reproduce the support cell's curve irrespective of ligand chemistry; a positive 'model' result could be a lookup on the condition columns.
risks.mitigation: Report model minus COPY only; add a conditions-only arm (no ligand features) as a second null.

risks.risk: Cross-publication Setting B is impossible at the stated gate (9 extractants / 4 chemotypes), so any 'between-laboratory' claim is out of reach on this cohort.
risks.mitigation: State it as out of scope; gen16's between-laboratory finding (+0.005 within a lab) already covers the point.

audits.summary: The reference repo is the upstream "lanthanide_dataset_builder + automl" project that produced ml_separator's frozen bundle: its AGENTS.md is addressed to lanthanide_dataset_builder, its scripts/build_dataset_no3d.py is the stage-1 builder, and collaborator_update/dataset.parquet is byte-identical (sha256 fefbefc6…f5dd) to ml_separator's "dataset with 3D structures/dataset.parquet". I verified same 5992x2261 shape, identical safe_exp_id set, identical log_D and all 64 cond__ columns; the only difference against the repo's own data/processed/final_ml_dataset_3d.parquet is the geometry side (geometry_ok 4746 there vs 5479 in the bundle). So it is the same upstream and the same SAFE csv schema, and the shipped tables carry no DOI: build_dataset_no3d.py strips DOI/entry_author/exp_id as provenance and leakage keywords, although raw_data/*_SAFE.csv do carry DOI, entry_author and addition_date. The scientific target is per-row log D, with pairwise adjacent log SF built post hoc from out-of-fold predictions; evaluation is 5-fold grouped CV on extractant SMILES x 2-3 repeats, and the headline is adjacent-pair log SF R2 on 905 "legacy" pairs (+0.326 best system), not macro MAE. The repo does have real neural networks — four torch 3D encoders (MPSN simplicial, SchNet-style distance, distance-biased attention, persistence-image CNN), an FT-Transformer, two set transformers over blocks/cells, and a zero-width tabular control — plus CatBoost/LightGBM/XGBoost/HistGB, Optuna sweeps, greedy block selection, NNLS/inverse-variance stacking and paired cluster bootstraps. The single most transferable modelling idea is the anchored level/shape decomposition (train a second model on block-centred targets, keep the flat model's block mean as anchor), worth about +0.05 adjacent R2 over flat, plus the finding that MAE/quantile-0.6 loss beats RMSE by ~+0.11. There is no k-shot, few-shot or fine-tuning machinery anywhere; "transfer" means Am/Cm joint training (family-level only) and self-supervised masked-charge pretraining of the simplicial encoder. Calibration exists only as post-hoc nested rescaling of predicted differences and LOEO split-conformal intervals. The leakage discipline is strong on extractant identity, frozen confirmation populations and SHA-pinned artefacts, but it groups only by extractant: there is no chemotype, scaffold or publication/DOI hold-out, so its numbers are systematically more optimistic than gen13's BP design, and its own DUALKEY report shows the topology result halves and loses significance under a stricter condition key. Three components are directly adaptable to pairwise log SF on gen13's cohort under BP: automl/collab_repro.py (already a from-scratch implementation of the antisymmetric-ExtraTrees pair model, equal-extractant macro MAE and extractant bootstrap), automl/topo/pair_model.py (all-pairs within-block delta training) and the anchored recipe in automl/topo/anchored_champion.py. Nothing runs as checked out: every entry point loads automl/artifacts/matrix/matrix.parquet, which is gitignored and absent, and the SLURM scripts hardcode cluster paths. On data overlap, the raw SAFE csvs are the same snapshot the bundle was built from — 48,138 raw rows exactly matches the builder's recorded raw_row_count, and 26,654 valid lanthanide rows reduce to 7,891 after exact de-duplication against the builder's 7,665-after-canonicalisation and 5,992 final — so they add no new lanthanide rows and cannot add adjacent-pair coverage. What they do add is provenance (DOI, entry_author, addition_date) and other metals: 2,030 de-duplicated Am rows on 131 extractant SMILES, 120 of which are shared with the lanthanide set, plus Cm, Y, U, Th, Pu, Np. Adding any of that is a data decision for the user, not something to do silently.

findings.topic: What the repository is: purpose and target
findings.detail: Purpose: predict the distribution coefficient log D of lanthanide(III) solvent-extraction complexes and, specifically, adjacent-lanthanide separation (neighbouring Shannon radii differ ~0.013 A). Target variable is log_D = log10(D) per experimental row (TARGET='log_D', scripts/build_dataset_no3d.py:119, computed at :849-852 from finite positive D). Pairwise log SF = log D(A) - log D(B) is NOT a training target anywhere; it is constructed post hoc from out-of-fold row predictions inside one (extractant, binned-conditions) block, after averaging replicates within a (block, metal) cell. Metals: 14 lanthanides La-Lu, Pm absent (LANTHANIDE_DESCRIPTORS lists 14 symbols with lanthanide_index 1..15 leaving index 5 unused, src/chemistry/coordination.py:50-66; evaluation.py:222 notes Pm absence means the Nd/Sm pair is correctly not counted as adjacent). Dataset: 5,992 deduplicated rows / 190 unique canonical ligand SMILES overall; the modelled 'legacy' subset is 4,746 rows / 162 extractants / 956 Architector+GFN2-xTB complexes (README.md:8-11, automl/README.md:136-152).
