findings.topic: DOIs and publication identifiers
findings.detail: The shipped tables carry NO DOI or publication id. build_dataset_no3d.py:236-249 lists DOI/doi/doi_link/publication/paper/entry_author/exp_id/addition_date in PROVENANCE_COLS and in LEAKAGE_KEYWORDS, so they are excluded both from the content-dedup key and from the final table; final_ml_dataset_no3d_info.json records content_dedup_excluded_provenance including DOI. I confirmed on the parquets that the only DOI/source-like column present is 'geometry_source'. The DOIs do exist upstream in raw_data/*_SAFE.csv (column 'DOI', plus entry_author and addition_date), which matches ml_separator's existing memory note that the DOIs are not in the bundle but join from the sibling builder repo. One consequence for this audit: nothing in the reference repo's modelling ever holds out a publication or a laboratory; the only exception is automl/topo/ceiling_v2.py:70-140, which re-reads the raw csvs to tag cells as within-one-DOI vs across-DOIs for a (withdrawn) ceiling estimate.

findings.topic: Neural network architectures present (torch only, no keras/tensorflow)
findings.detail: Six distinct torch architectures plus one control. (1) SimplicialNet, message-passing simplicial network over Vietoris-Rips complexes: 3 simplex levels (nodes/edges/triangles), boundary and co-boundary messages, LayerNorm residual updates, metal-centred readout, soft radial shell histogram, optional angular readout and attention pooling, optional FiLM on conditions, optional pair head; embedding width 9*dim (default dim 96, 3 layers, dropout 0.15). (2) DistanceNet, SchNet-style continuous-filter convolution over the same edges with a Gaussian RBF on the edge distance, deliberately identical readout/head/width so it is a 'no-simplex' control. (3) AttentionNet, transformer over the atoms of one complex with a learned per-head bias from a radial basis on the pairwise distance (Graphormer-style), dense or cutoff-restricted. (4) PersistenceCNN, three conv blocks (16/32/64) + BatchNorm + SiLU over the shipped 20x20 persistence images, ~35k params. (5) FTTransformer over tabular columns: one token per numeric column, ECFP bits folded into 8 tokens, CLS token, pre-norm encoder, pinball loss at q=0.6. (6) BlockTransformer / CellTransformer: set transformers whose tokens are the rows, or the (block, metal) cells, of one composition block, output centred within the block by construction, L1 loss on the block-centred target. (7) TabularNet: the matched control with a width-zero embedding so the head sees only the tabular block. Also sklearn MLPRegressor in the model zoo. Losses: Huber (default, delta 1.0) / MAE / MSE / pinball on the level term; squared or Huber error on within-block pair differences with adjacent pairs weighted 3x; optional decomposed objective weighting block means separately; optional auxiliary head on CShM / interaction energy / charge transfer with NaN masking; self-supervised pretraining head reconstructing masked xTB charges and edge filtration radii. Regularisation/optimisation: AdamW + CosineAnnealingLR, weight decay 1e-4, grad-norm clip 5.0, dropout, LayerNorm; checkpointing keeps the best state dict by inner-validation loss or by adjacent-pair R2, with patience; pretrained encoder cached to disk and loaded encoder-only with strict=False.

findings.topic: Gradient boosting, AutoML sweeps and ensembles
findings.detail: Model zoo make_model() covers lightgbm (plus dart), xgboost, catboost, HistGradientBoosting, RF, ExtraTrees, ridge/elasticnet/huber/SVR/kNN/MLP, with NATIVE_NAN_MODELS marking the tree learners that consume NaN directly. Champion CatBoost parameters: 1500 iterations, lr 0.04, depth 9, l2_leaf_reg 3.0, rsm 0.3, loss Quantile:alpha=0.6 (and an MAE-deep variant for the shape model). Sample weighting schemes: group_inv, group_inv_full, metal_inv, target_lds, combo. Sweeps: run_sweep.py drives ablation (feature-block presets), models (learner x weighting) and Optuna modes, writing JSONL with full provenance; Optuna spaces per learner in models.suggest_params; select_features.py does forward stepwise search over whole descriptor blocks plus grouped-CV permutation importance; champion.py re-runs a 29-row shortlist at 5 repeats with a cluster bootstrap over extractants; ensemble.py stacks saved out-of-fold predictions with NNLS and with inverse-variance/disagreement weighting under an outer grouped CV, and calibrates the per-row uncertainty; compare.py does the decisive paired bootstrap; automl/topo/best_stack.py and stack_test.py do nested per-extractant blend weights exploiting the linearity of the pair construction. collab_repro.py additionally reimplements an antisymmetric ExtraTrees pair model (impute-median + indicator -> 200 trees, reversed-copy augmentation with negated target, prediction (f(A,B)-f(B,A))/2, group-balanced weights, StratifiedGroupKFold(5) stratified by pair label and grouped by extractant, inner 3-fold grid over (max_features, min_samples_leaf)).

findings.topic: Input representations and how a (molecule, metal, conditions) row is encoded
findings.detail: A row is keyed by safe_exp_id ('<source_stem>:<exp_id>') and carries a geometry_key 'Z|ligand_SMILES|inner-sphere anion' (1,256 unique planned complexes, 956 with clean geometry). Tabular blocks assembled in dataset.py: rdkit (10 named RDKit descriptors), ecfp (2,048 Morgan bits, radius 2, precomputed), metal (Atomic Number, lanthanide_index, Shannon CN-8 ionic radius, metal_ox), cond (64 numeric/one-hot condition columns), plan (DENTATE, coreCN, n_ligs, n_fill), qc (geometry QC class one-hot + geometry_ok). 3D blocks from geom3d_features.py, 293 descriptors per geometry: G1 first shell (realised M-L distances within 3.10 A, observed CN, donor element counts, donor electronegativity/hardness), G2 contraction (shell minus Shannon radius), G3 polyhedron (continuous shape measures vs ideal CN-6..10 polyhedra, angular statistics, convex hull), G4 steric (%V_bur at 3.5/5.0/7.0 A, solid-angle shadowing, SASA), G5 electronic (xTB metal charge, ligand->metal charge transfer, donor charge statistics, dipole, residual force norms), G6 element-resolved metal-centred RDFs, G7 global shape, G8 chelate ring/bite angles, G9 persistent-homology summaries. Derived in dataset.py: g10 within-ligand-family relative (delta/z/rank across the series), g12 series-smoothed fitted value, g13 family slope (ligand-level selectivity descriptor), g14 family mean, g15 coordination-number-free residuals plus intensive forms and a bond-valence sum, g11 flattened persistence images. metal_physics.py adds a per-lanthanide lookup block (4f count, aqua CN, hydration enthalpy and free energy, third ionisation energy, Ln-OH2 distance, tetrad coordinates |n_f - 3.5/7/10.5|, half-shell and CN-break flags, 3/r charge density, Born residual) — deliberately conformer-noise-free constants. Blocking keys: composition_key = extractant_group || ten binned geom_cond fields; strict_composition_key additionally pins every numeric cond column. Encoder input per complex: node features are xTB partial charge, a charge-missing flag, is_metal, is_donor and distance-to-metal, plus a 27-element Z embedding vocabulary; edges and triangles carry their Vietoris-Rips filtration radii; conditions reach the encoder only through the concatenated tabular block or through FiLM modulation of the pooled embedding. Metal identity therefore enters three ways at once: the metal block, the geometry (one complex per metal), and the mphys lookups.

findings.topic: Training procedure, splits, CV, search, early stopping, seeds
findings.detail: Split: grouped K-fold on extractant_group (the canonical extractant SMILES), 5 folds, 2-3 repeats for sweeps and 5 for the champion stage, using sklearn GroupKFold with shuffle=True/random_state (with an explicit note that unshuffled GroupKFold leaves ~81% of each fold unchanged between seeds, so earlier 'protocol A' repeats were near-duplicates and are screening-only). An extractant never appears in train and test together; every reported number comes from pooled out-of-fold predictions. Row filters: all / has3d / ok_only / cn9_light / cn8_heavy / cn9_matched:<seed> (the last subsamples the light half to the heavy half's extractant-coverage profile). Optional winsorisation of the training target only. Hyperparameter search: distributed Optuna over a shared SQLite study, plus a hand shortlist; neural runs use fixed configurations with per-seed tags. Early stopping for every neural arm uses an inner validation split that is itself grouped by extractant (15% of training groups), with criterion either MSE or adjacent-pair R2, patience 6-30 depending on the module; the best state dict is restored before prediction. Seeds: default split seed 42, repeats add rep to the seed, fold seeds are seed + rep*100 + fold; the pretrained encoder seed is fixed at 42 and deliberately independent of the run seed; ensembles use seeds 42/51/67/83/91/103/107/109; a --deterministic mode swaps scatter reductions for sort-based ones, pins cuDNN and sets CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG, and inertness of any train.py change is proven by requiring max|delta oof| = 0 against a published parquet. Three-way extractant split for the C6 campaign (screen/select/report, snake draft balanced on adjacent-pair count, deterministic, verifiable) exists in automl/topo/c6_split.py, and automl/topo/fresh_eval.py freezes a 444-pair confirmation population that refuses to be overwritten.

findings.topic: Transfer learning, fine-tuning, few-shot, calibration: what exists and what does not
findings.detail: There is NO k-shot or few-shot machinery, no measured-mode calibration from a small number of measured pairs of a held-out ligand, and no fine-tuning of a trained model on new chemistry. A grep for few-shot/k-shot/fine-tune/warm-start across automl/ returns only the self-supervised pretraining comment and unrelated 'charge transfer' feature names. What does exist: (a) self-supervised pretraining of the simplicial encoder on masked xTB charges and edge radii, computed once outside the CV loop, cached by (dim, layers, epochs, conformers, seed) and loaded encoder-only; (b) actinide transfer in automl/an_ln/: build.py rebuilds the row table admitting Am and Cm by patching the pipeline's metal gate and giving them Z, a Shannon-scale pseudo lanthanide_index (Am 5.27, Cm 5.93) and a radius (1.090/1.080 A), experiments.py runs ln_only (Am scored zero-shot as a pseudo-lanthanide) vs ln_am (joint training with an is_actinide flag) on pre-frozen Am/Eu pairs; (c) post-hoc calibration of the predicted difference in automl/topo/calibration_test.py — nested per-extractant scale / affine / isotonic transforms fitted on the other extractants only, with a cluster-bootstrap interval on the gain and an explicit optimal-shrinkage-vs-miscalibration verdict; (d) split-conformal intervals calibrated leave-one-extractant-out plus an abstention curve on 8-seed ensemble disagreement in automl/topo/decision_quality.py; (e) inverse-variance/disagreement ensemble weighting and an uncertainty-calibration table in automl/ensemble.py.

findings.topic: Evaluation metrics
findings.detail: evaluation.full_metrics reports a decomposition rather than a single R2: r2_overall, r2_between (R2 of size-weighted per-extractant means), r2_within (after removing each extractant's own mean), r2_within_composition (after removing extractant+conditions), per-extractant median R2 and the fraction of extractants beating their own mean (with an explicit warning that the size-weighted per-extractant mean is not robust and reaches about -14), within-group Pearson/Spearman, RMSE/MAE/median AE, Spearman/Pearson, per-metal mean and min R2, and the selectivity family: sel_spearman_mean/median, sel_kendall_mean, sel_logSF_mae, sel_logSF_r2, sel_sign_accuracy over all metal pairs in a block, then the adjacent-only restriction sel_adj_logSF_r2 / mae / sign_accuracy / true_sd / pearson. The adjacent construction averages replicates within a (block, metal) cell before differencing, and is factored into one function precisely so figures and metrics cannot drift apart (a figure that enumerated raw row pairs once inverted the published result). Comparisons use a paired cluster bootstrap resampling whole extractants, with a multiplicity-respecting variant (an earlier version that collapsed duplicate clusters made published intervals 12-29% too narrow) and a Bonferroni-style correction for the number of looks. pair_coverage.py quantifies that Eu's 28% row share does not propagate fully into the pair population because a pair needs both neighbours measured in the same block.

findings.topic: Leakage safeguards and known leakage
findings.detail: Safeguards: extractant-grouped outer CV and extractant-grouped inner validation; derived feature blocks (g10, g12-g15) are documented and designed to use geometry only, never target values, and a family is built from its own extractant's structures; composition blocks nest strictly inside extractants (checked: 0 of 552 blocks span two extractant groups), so block means and block-centred features never straddle a fold; out-of-fold encoder embeddings come from the restored best checkpoint of a model that never saw those extractants; stacking is done on predictions, with nested per-extractant weights; a frozen 444-pair confirmation population and committed pre-registrations for every confirmatory test; control_guard pins 324 artefacts by SHA-256; explicit guards that make an unsupported flag fail loudly rather than become a silent no-op (a prior bug recorded pair_head=True while doing nothing on every modern run). Known leakage and limitations the repo itself records: representations must not be stacked, because fold identity is recoverable from out-of-fold embeddings at 100% accuracy; the anchored and pairwise estimators are batch predictors whose prediction for one row depends on which other rows are scored with it (no label leakage, but valid only for whole-extractant screening, not single-row inference); protocol-A sweeps used a splitter whose repeats were 81% correlated and are screening-only; the headline blocking key bins the conditions, and under the strict key the topology contrast falls from +0.0375 to +0.0177 with an interval touching zero; two shipped columns carry +inf on 13 rows and are sanitised to NaN downstream rather than fixed upstream. Most important for a BP-style design: grouping is by extractant SMILES only — there is no chemotype/scaffold grouping and no publication or DOI hold-out anywhere in automl/, so homologues, stereoisomers and same-laboratory condition fingerprints of a test extractant can all sit in training.

findings.topic: Headline results as the repo states them (for calibration against gen13/gen20 numbers)
findings.detail: Best system: prediction = anchor + 0.65*shape_tabular + 0.35*shape_encoder, reaching +0.326 adjacent-pair log SF R2 on the 905 legacy pairs, with the 3D contrast confirmed at +0.0156 on the frozen 444 pairs. Best single model: anchored CatBoost q60/q60, 8-seed ensemble, +0.318 — above every stack the project ever fitted. Mechanism gains: the anchored level/shape split is worth roughly +0.05 over flat at matched parameters (+0.268 -> +0.318) and about +0.11 at fast parameters; swapping RMSE for MAE on CatBoost is worth +0.1066 adjacent R2 and also improves log D R2; training the within-block contrast rather than the absolute value is worth +0.186 for the simplicial net, +0.042 for the PI-CNN and +0.030 tabular. Learning curve: +0.146 / +0.196 / +0.254 / +0.301 / +0.307 at 7.8 / 15.4 / 30.4 / 45.9 / 60.8 training extractants, so 98% of the full-data score is reached at ~46 extractants and doubling the extractant count is worth only +0.01 to +0.04 — the repo explicitly retracts its own earlier claim that data is the binding constraint. Decision quality: mean Spearman 0.46 across the 12 adjacent positions, top-quartile hit rate 0.50 against 0.25 by chance, conformal coverage 79.3/89.7% at nominal 80/90%. Negative results with teeth: transformers tie or lose (attention encoder ties the distance encoder, FT-Transformer and set transformers lose and take weight 0.00); topology adds nothing beyond the distance encoder (encoders correlate 0.963, triangles no better than edges, persistence features collapse the shape model); up-weighting metal features x5/x10 hurts; condition deltas do not transfer out-of-extractant; the energy channel did not replicate; the +0.53 ceiling was withdrawn and no point ceiling is identifiable. Cross-pipeline check: the repo reproduced ml_separator's A2 macro MAE at 0.3238 +- 0.0057 against the stated 0.3192 +- 0.0078, and found the two pipelines statistically tied under the macro MAE metric.

findings.topic: Operational state: nothing runs as checked out
findings.detail: Every modelling entry point loads automl/artifacts/matrix/matrix.parquet via matrix_cache.load_cache (which rebuilds it from data/processed/final_ml_dataset_3d.parquet plus the geom3d shards if missing); automl/.gitignore excludes artifacts/ entirely, and the clone's automl/artifacts/ contains only an_ln, fresh_eval, gxtb_series and lnxtb — so the matrix cache, the geom3d descriptor shards, all out-of-fold parquets and every pretrained encoder are absent. The analyses that read only saved predictions (anchored_3d.py, calibration_test.py, decision_quality.py, dualkey_test.py, transformer_eval.py, restack.py) therefore cannot run either. The SLURM scripts hardcode /home/gridsan/bmironov/lanthanidestrain and `module load anaconda/Python-ML-2025a`, and the geometry pipeline hardcodes /nfs/home/nshank3/lanthanide_dataset_builder with a specific account/partition. tests/ (9 modules, ~48 tests) covers only the dataset builder and geometry recovery; automl/tests/ (17 modules) covers descriptor mathematics, encoder invariances, determinism and palette contrast — neither suite covers the pair metric or the split designs that matter for gen20.

findings.topic: Data overlap: the raw SAFE csvs are the bundle's own source, not new data
findings.detail: raw_data/ holds 31 *_SAFE.csv files, each with the identical 38-column header (exp_id, extractant name/concentration, acid, solvent, metal name and oxidation state, metal concentration, phase modifier, holdback agent, Extractant_SMILES, Extractant_inchi, ini_comp, organic acid concentration, DOI, entry_author, addition_date, obsDvalues/obsDvaluesValue, temperature, contact and shaking time, radiolytic dosage, comments, volume and third-phase fields). Total 48,138 data rows, which matches the builder's recorded raw_row_count of 48,138 exactly — the csvs are the same snapshot the bundle was built from. Lanthanide rows (Metal_Name in La..Lu) with a finite positive D and a non-empty SMILES: 26,654, against the builder's after_valid_D count of 26,653 (one row differs: a single Pm row, which the bundle cannot carry). After removing exact duplicate rows: 7,891 unique rows, consistent with the builder's 7,665 after canonical-SMILES validation (225 invalid SMILES removed) and 5,992 after content de-duplication. So there are no lanthanide rows here that are not already represented in ml_separator's bundle, and no adjacent-pair coverage to be gained: adding these csvs would re-derive the same cohort. The csvs are also not newer than the bundle — the latest addition_date anywhere is 2026-02-10, the bundle was built 2026-08-07, and zero rows carry a date after that. Note each csv is a metal-named export but contains other metals too (e.g. Ca_SAFE.csv holds 2,371 valid lanthanide rows), so file names are not a metal partition.
evidence: scratchpad/audit_scratch/count_safe.py and count_safe2.py outputs (48,138 rows; 26,654 valid Ln; 7,891 after exact dedup; max addition_date 2026-02-10)

findings.topic: Data overlap: what the raw csvs DO add (report only, not to be added silently)
findings.detail: Two things the bundle lacks. (a) Provenance: a DOI string on every row (116 distinct raw strings among valid lanthanide rows, but unnormalised — 'doi:10…', 'DOI: 10…', 'https://doi.org/…', some rows carrying two DOIs — so the number of distinct publications is lower), plus entry_author (Thomas Summers 3,599 rows, Baosen Zhang 3,110, Aurora Clark 1,182 after dedup) and addition_date (2024-12, 2026-01, 2026-02 cohorts). ml_separator already has a reconstructed publication_id for all 5,992 rows in runs/gen6_provenance/provenance_table.parquet, so this is a cross-check source rather than a necessity. (b) Other metals on overlapping chemistry: 5,316 valid Am rows reducing to 2,030 unique on 131 extractant SMILES, 120 of which also appear among the lanthanide SMILES, from 55 DOIs; Cm 337 -> 144 unique on 13 SMILES (12 shared); Y 112 -> 49 on 1 SMILES; Sc 10; and outside the trivalent problem U 4,027, Pu 3,515, Th 2,409, Np 1,272 valid rows. The reference repo already exploited the Am/Cm route (automl/an_ln/) and reports it closed for the lanthanide target: joint training reaches Am/Eu R2 +0.467 but a no-model ligand-family lookup scores +0.472, within-family skill is +0.02, and the lanthanide metric moves +0.002 +- 0.020. Y is the only untried augmentation it names, and it was deferred.
evidence: scratchpad/audit_scratch/count_safe2.py output (Am 5,316/2,030/131 SMILES/120 shared/55 DOI; Cm 337/144/13/12; Y 112/49/1; author and date counts)

findings.topic: Compatibility verdict for gen13 cohort + BP design, pairwise log SF
findings.detail: The repo has real neural networks, so the honest answer is not 'no NN' — but no component is drop-in. Three are genuinely adaptable, in descending order of readiness. (1) automl/collab_repro.py is already a from-scratch implementation of ml_separator's own pair pipeline: it builds the pair cohort, the antisymmetric ExtraTrees estimator, the transitive projection, the PAIRMEAN baseline, equal-extractant macro MAE and the extractant-resampled paired bootstrap, reading the bundle parquet directly and asserting its hash. It needs no target change at all; what it needs is gen13's cohort (its own cohort filter requires complete conditions and collapses to 34 extractants, against gen13's 90) and gen13's BP folds in place of StratifiedGroupKFold on extractant. (2) automl/topo/pair_model.py trains directly on all within-block cell pairs (6,389 under the binned key) with CatBoost/LightGBM, MAE or quantile loss and adjacent up-weighting, and already scores pairs out-of-fold with extractant grouping; it needs the gen13 cohort and BP folds plugged into its grouped_folds call, and its feature construction trimmed (it mixes in ECFP and RDKit blocks that gen13 deliberately excludes as non-transferable across laboratories). (3) automl/topo/anchored_champion.py is the anchored level/shape recipe and the one mechanism worth importing as a modelling idea rather than as code — but it is a log-D row model whose anchor cancels in every pair, so under a pure pair target it reduces to the shape model alone. Changes required for any of them: the metric must become extractant/chemotype-macro MAE under BP rather than pooled adjacent R2; the split must come from gen13's splits.py (chemotype groups plus the publication mask, with BR/BQ controls) because the repo groups only by extractant SMILES; the matrix cache and geom3d shards must be rebuilt or the 3D paths dropped; anchored and pairwise estimators are batch predictors and must not be used for single-row inference; absolute cluster paths and module loads must be replaced; and the repo's headline numbers must not be quoted alongside gen13's, since they are a different target, a different pair population and a weaker hold-out. The neural encoders are the least transferable part: they need the per-complex Vietoris-Rips asset joined by geometry build id, a GPU, 8-32 seeds per arm for stable ensembles, and the repo's own verdict is that four independent 3D encoder architectures land on effectively the same predictions (effective rank 1.05 of 8) and add about +0.015 over the best tabular model. Finally, the clone is untrusted downloaded content: it must be read, never imported or executed, and its SLURM scripts must never be submitted.

findings.topic: Reusable ideas that cost nothing to adopt
findings.detail: Independent of code reuse, five of the repo's methodological devices map directly onto gen20's problem. (a) adjacent_pair_arrays is factored out of both the metric and the figures so they cannot disagree, after a figure that enumerated raw row pairs once inverted a published result — worth mirroring for any new pair metric. (b) Nested blend/calibration weights fitted on the other extractants only, exploiting the linearity of the pair construction so a 21-point weight search is vector arithmetic rather than a re-groupby. (c) The equal-extractant criterion for choosing any blend weight, because the dominant extractant (21% of pairs there, 43.6% of rows in ml_separator's cohort) otherwise dictates every other extractant's weight; the repo discloses that the pair-weighted variant was run first and reports the cost. (d) Freezing a confirmation population before any model runs, with a module that refuses to overwrite the frozen file, plus a committed decision rule naming the endpoint and the consequence of each outcome. (e) Proving a harness change inert by re-running a published arm under a deterministic flag and requiring max|delta out-of-fold| = 0 — the repo reports 0.000e+00 across 4,746 rows for two separate changes. Also worth noting as a cautionary pattern: four causal mechanisms the author inferred by reading the code were each falsified by their own test, which is why that repo promotes nothing to ESTABLISHED without a test that could have gone the other way.

reusable_components.what: A 385-line from-scratch implementation of ml_separator's own pair pipeline: pair cohort construction (build_cohort:67), antisymmetric feature reversal (reverse_features:175), antisymmetric ExtraTrees with reversed-copy augmentation and (f(A,B)-f(B,A))/2 prediction (make_est:185, fit_predict_antisym:202), group-balanced weights (group_weights:196), StratifiedGroupKFold outer/inner with a 3-point grid, transitive projection (run_seed:271-282), PAIRMEAN baseline, equal-extractant macro MAE (macro_mae:212), full metric set (seed_metrics:289) and an extractant-resampled paired bootstrap with rng 8675309 (paired_bootstrap:305).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Read it as a reference implementation of the macro-MAE metric and the antisymmetric pair estimator; it is the closest thing in the repo to gen20's target and needs no target change. To use it against gen13's cohort, replace build_cohort with the gen13 cohort loader and replace the StratifiedGroupKFold calls with gen13 splits.py folds (design BP, including the publication mask).
reusable_components.caveats: Do not execute this file from the clone — it is untrusted content and it asserts a dataset hash then reads a parquet path inside the clone. Its own cohort filter requires every one of the 64 conditions to be present, which collapses 190 extractants to 34 and is exactly the filter gen13 rejected; its folds are grouped by extractant SMILES only, with no chemotype or publication hold-out, so its numbers are optimistic relative to BP.

reusable_components.what: All-pairs within-block delta model: builds one training example per within-block cell pair with replicate averaging matching the evaluator (build_pairs:77), features = pair identity (indices, delta radius, mean radius, 4f counts, tetrad coordinates, Gd-crossing, CN-break crossing), condition deltas and block-level condition means, plus ligand context; CatBoost or LightGBM with MAE/RMSE/quantile loss and an adjacent up-weight; scored out-of-fold on the adjacent subset with extractant-grouped folds (run_config:183); feature ablations identity / identity_cond / full.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: The pair-feature construction and the identity/condition/ligand ablation axis transfer directly to a pairwise log SF model on gen13's cohort; swap the matrix source for the gen13 cohort frame and the folds for BP.
reusable_components.caveats: Reads automl/artifacts/matrix/matrix.parquet, which is absent from the clone. Its 'full' feature set includes ECFP and the RDKit block, which gen13's DECISION_REPORT excludes as non-transferable across laboratories. The repo's own result is that this model reaches +0.191 standalone but its errors duplicate the row models' and it adds nothing in a stack.

reusable_components.what: The anchored level/shape recipe and its champion parameters: CHAMP = CatBoost 1500 iterations, lr 0.04, depth 9, l2_leaf_reg 3.0, rsm 0.3, Quantile:alpha=0.6 (line 50) and MAE_DEEP (line 52); run_cell:110 fits a base model on log D and a residual model on the key-centred target, then recombines as anchor + shape_weight*centred_shape + (1-shape_weight)*centred_base; 15 named cells including composition-level anchoring, shape weights 0.7/0.8/0.9, 3D blocks given only to the shape model, a block-mean control, and literal metal-feature up-weighting.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Import the idea, not the file: train a second model on the cell-centred target and keep the first model's cell mean as the level. Under a pure pair target the anchor cancels, so the shape model is the whole model — which is what gen15's curve model already does; the transferable detail is the loss asymmetry (quantile 0.6 for the level, MAE for the shape).
reusable_components.caveats: Depends on matrix_cache and the absent artifacts cache. The combination is a batch predictor: a row's prediction depends on which other rows are scored with it. The repo's own learning curve shows this family saturates by ~46 training extractants.

reusable_components.what: Nested post-hoc recalibration of a predicted difference: per held-out extractant, fit scale / affine / isotonic on the other extractants' adjacent pairs only (_fit_apply:73, calibrate:94), then a cluster-bootstrap interval on the gain that holds the transform fixed across draws so the interval measures the gain rather than the transform's own variance (gain_interval:115), and an explicit optimal-shrinkage-versus-miscalibration verdict driven by whether the lower bound clears zero.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Directly applicable to gen20's measured-mode question as the null for 'does rescaling the predicted curve help': it is the no-new-information calibration baseline, and the gain_interval discipline is the right way to price a best-of-three transform.
reusable_components.caveats: Pure post-hoc rescaling, not k-shot calibration — it uses no measurement of the held-out ligand, only the other extractants' residual scale. Depends on saved out-of-fold frames that are absent from the clone.

reusable_components.what: Screening-oriented read-out of a pair model: per-position ranking of held-out extractants (Spearman and top-quartile hit rate against 0.25 chance, ranking:94), pooled and within-extractant Spearman, sign accuracy restricted to pairs with a clear measured direction, split-conformal intervals calibrated leave-one-extractant-out, and an abstention curve on ensemble disagreement (conformal:132).
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: Gen16 found the measured-mode residual covariance indefinite and 90% intervals covering 98.8%; this module's LOEO split-conformal construction is a distribution-free alternative that cannot produce an indefinite covariance, and its abstention curve is the honest way to report that confident pairs are also the small-separation ones.
reusable_components.caveats: Its coverage numbers (79.3/89.7% at nominal 80/90%) are on the repo's own 905-pair population under extractant-only grouping and will not carry over to BP. Reads saved per-seed parquets that are absent.

reusable_components.what: A 137-line per-lanthanide constants block: 4f electron count, aqua coordination number across the 9->8 break, hydration enthalpy and free energy, third ionisation energy, Ln-OH2 distance, tetrad coordinates |n_f - 3.5/7/10.5|, half-shell and CN-break flags, 3/r charge density and a Born residual; plus series_shape() to display which columns are non-monotone across the series.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: A clean, conformer-noise-free alternative metal axis for any curve or pair model: these are lookup constants, so they add no geometry noise, and the tetrad terms give a coordinate that is deliberately not collinear with the ionic radius, which is what lets a model bend where the measured series bends.
reusable_components.caveats: The repo's own verdict (finding D2) is that these aqueous-phase and f-shell descriptors do not generalise. Values are quoted to the precision of the source compilations; Cm/Am are not in this table (they are added separately in an_ln/build.py), and Pm is present but never occurs in data.

reusable_components.what: Split-half reliability of the adjacent-pair target: keep every (block, metal) cell with at least two rows, split each cell's rows at random, build adjacent pairs from each half independently, correlate, and Spearman-Brown to full size — a bound on the metric that assumes nothing transfers from the replicated subset to the rest. Records the attempt and its failure explicitly so the next person does not repeat it.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: The right template for any future ceiling claim on gen13's cohort, and a direct answer to 'how much of the adjacent-pair signal is even measurable'.
reusable_components.caveats: The repo's conclusion is that the noise floor is NOT identifiable from this dataset by three independent routes, and that cells acquire replicates preferentially when sources disagree, so the bound is biased and is reported only for the replicated subset. Any ceiling must come from designed replication, not from this.

reusable_components.what: A deterministic three-way extractant split (screen / select / report) built as a snake draft balanced on adjacent-pair count rather than extractant count, with a --verify mode that rebuilds and byte-compares the files and prints a hash. Its docstring states why a new split was needed: the previous confirm half had been scored on by four prior campaigns.
reusable_components.how_to_reuse: The pattern — separate budgets for screening, ranking and the one pre-declared look, balanced on the unit the metric actually averages — maps onto gen20's arm selection, and the --verify mode is a cheap guard that a frozen split has not drifted.
reusable_components.caveats: Splits only on extractant, not chemotype or publication, so it does not by itself give a BP-grade hold-out; and it calls train.build_row_table, which needs the absent matrix cache and the Vietoris-Rips asset.

risks.risk: The clone is untrusted downloaded content containing ~31k lines of Python, 150 shell scripts and a 2,641-line SLURM entrypoint that submits cluster jobs. Executing or importing any of it, or letting an interpreter run with that directory as cwd, would run third-party code; its SLURM scripts target a specific account and partition and could submit real jobs.
risks.mitigation: Keep it strictly read-only, as this audit did: inspect with grep/sed/cat/Read only, never import its modules, run any analysis Python from a separate directory with -I and pass file paths as arguments. Never submit anything under its slurm/ or automl/slurm/.

risks.risk: Importing its headline numbers into gen20 reasoning would be an apples-to-oranges comparison. Its target is per-row log D with pairs derived afterwards, its metric is pooled adjacent-pair R2 on 905 pairs of a 162-extractant population, and its hold-out groups only extractants. Gen13/gen20 score extractant- or chemotype-macro MAE on a 521-cell, 90-extractant, 45-chemotype cohort under BP, which additionally removes the held-out cell's publication.
risks.mitigation: Never quote a number from this repo next to a gen13+ number without naming the target, the pair population and the design. If a cross-check is wanted, the only like-for-like anchor already exists: its reproduction of A2 macro MAE at 0.3238 +- 0.0057 against the stated 0.3192 +- 0.0078.

risks.risk: Its evaluation has no chemotype, scaffold or publication hold-out, so its reported transfer to 'unseen extractants' includes homologues and same-laboratory condition fingerprints of test ligands. Gen13 measured that the 64 condition columns identify a cell's publication with 94% 1-NN accuracy, which is precisely why design BP exists.
risks.mitigation: Treat every number in this repo as an upper bound on what the same method would score under BP. If any component is adapted, replace its splitter with gen13 splits.py (BP, with the BR and BQ controls) before fitting anything, and re-measure rather than assuming the reported effect size carries over.

risks.risk: Its anchored and pairwise estimators are batch predictors: a row's prediction depends on which other rows are scored alongside it, because the anchor is a mean over the block or extractant. The repo documents this clearly, but a careless port would produce numbers that cannot be reproduced for a single new ligand and that silently depend on the scoring batch composition.
risks.mitigation: If the anchored recipe is adopted, fix the aggregation unit explicitly to the cell and verify that a single-cell prediction is unchanged when other cells are added or removed; otherwise use the shape model alone, which is what the pair target reduces to anyway.

risks.risk: Nothing in automl/ runs as checked out — the matrix cache, geom3d descriptor shards and all out-of-fold parquets are gitignored and absent, and paths are hardcoded to two different clusters. Any plan that assumes a component can be run to reproduce a number will stall.
risks.mitigation: Treat the clone as documentation and as a source of algorithms to re-implement against ml_separator's own cohort, not as a runnable pipeline. If a specific number must be checked, request the artifacts or rebuild only the minimal input (the matrix cache derives from data/processed/final_ml_dataset_3d.parquet, which is present).

risks.risk: The repo's own strongest caveat is that the topology and 3D results are key-dependent: the published contrast falls from +0.0375 [+0.0173, +0.0510] under the binned condition key to +0.0177 [-0.0023, +0.0367] under the strict key, and the matched control's stack weight degenerates to 0.00. Adopting any 3D channel on the strength of the binned-key number would import a half-sized, non-significant effect.
risks.mitigation: If 3D is revisited, score under the exact-condition key from the start (gen13's cohort already uses an exact 64-column key), and budget for the effect being about half the advertised size.

risks.risk: Adding the raw SAFE csvs, the Am/Cm rows or the DOI columns to gen20's inputs would change a frozen cohort. The gen13 cohort fingerprint 4c3c6628ea0be949 and the bundle hash fefbefc6… are what make gen13-gen19 comparable.
risks.mitigation: Report the availability, as this audit does, and change nothing. Any addition is a user decision and would need a new cohort fingerprint, a re-run of the frozen designs and an explicit statement that the new numbers are not comparable to gen13-gen19.

risks.risk: Several of the repo's quoted results are selection-exposed or superseded in ways that are easy to miss if only the README is read: the +0.53 ceiling was formally withdrawn, the fixed-weight +0.3277 number is look-selected and the module says it must not be quoted, the +0.326-vs-+0.313 system margin is explicitly flagged as needing a designed test before being called a gain, and one 'tuning gain' of +0.0178 fell to +0.0003 on replication.
risks.mitigation: Read automl/reports/SCIENTIFIC_FINDINGS.md status labels (ESTABLISHED / SUPPORTED / FALSIFIED) and CEILING_NOTE.md before reusing any figure from README.md, which is dated 20 August 2026 and is not the current register.

risks.risk: The 3D encoder route is expensive and, by the repo's own measurement, nearly exhausted: four independent architectures have effective rank 1.05 of 8, the two best encoders correlate at 0.963 at pair level, and the whole 3D contribution is about +0.015 over the best tabular model. Each arm needs 8-32 GPU seeds for a stable ensemble.
risks.mitigation: If a neural 3D arm is proposed for gen20, treat +0.015-class gains as the realistic prior and require a powered design; the cheaper lever the repo identifies is the objective (contrast training, robust loss), not the representation.

open_questions: Direction of the data exchange is inferred, not proven: the reference repo's collaborator_update/ holds ml_separator's bundle parquet and its report describes receiving a geometry-repaired drop, while its own data/processed table is the 4,746-geometry_ok ancestor. I did not find a document stating which repository first produced the 5,992-row table, so 'the reference repo is upstream of the bundle' rests on AGENTS.md naming lanthanide_dataset_builder, the manifest's absolute paths into that sibling repo, and the row-count chain matching. Worth confirming with the user before any provenance claim is published.

Whether the raw SAFE csvs are bit-identical to the snapshot the bundle was built from cannot be proven without re-running scripts/build_dataset_no3d.py, which is forbidden here (it would overwrite committed outputs). The evidence is strong but indirect: 48,138 raw rows matches raw_row_count exactly, and my 26,654 valid lanthanide rows differ from the recorded 26,653 by a single row, which I believe is the one Pm row the bundle cannot carry. A read-only re-derivation into a scratch directory would settle it if the question matters.

The 116 distinct DOI strings are unnormalised (three different prefix conventions, some rows carrying two DOIs), so the true number of distinct publications behind the lanthanide rows is unknown from this audit. ml_separator's own runs/gen6_provenance/provenance_table.parquet already carries a reconstructed publication_id for all 5,992 rows; whether those reconstructions agree with the raw DOIs is a cross-check I did not run.

Whether the reference repo's 3D assets can be joined to gen13's cohort at all: its encoders key on geometry_feature_build_id, and the bundle ships features/vietoris_rips_inputs.npz, but the bundle has 1,155 accepted geometries against 1,256 planned specs and 101 complexes with no accepted geometry, while the repo's asset covers 956. I did not verify that the bundle's asset and the gen13 cohort's cells intersect sufficiently for an encoder arm, and 179 of the bundle's geometry_ok rows were reported as shipped without structures.

Whether anything in the reference repo can actually be run to reproduce a number, given that the matrix cache, geom3d shards and all out-of-fold parquets are gitignored and absent. If a specific figure must be checked rather than cited, either the artifacts are needed or the minimal cache must be rebuilt from the present parquet — and that rebuild would be running untrusted code, so it should happen only with explicit instruction and in an isolated copy.

Its 'one measurement' story is absent, which is the gap most relevant to gen20: there is no k-shot or few-shot calibration anywhere, so the repo offers no independent check on ml_separator's finding that one measurement of a new extractant beats every zero-shot modelling gain. Its calibration_test.py is the closest relative and is a no-new-information rescaling, i.e. a null rather than a method.

Its learning-curve conclusion (saturation by ~46 extractants, more of the same chemistry is low yield) was measured by subsampling a fixed 76-extractant pool under extractant-only grouping. Whether it holds under BP, where chemotypes rather than extractants are held out and 53 single-lanthanide chemotypes are the named cheap lever in ml_separator's own notes, is untested and would change the priority of data acquisition if it did not.

gaps.question: Which query-set definition does the study adopt - the recovery plan's SHA-256 20 % subset (plan:234) or something else - and is it fixed across k, arms and policies?
gaps.answer_or_check: Already decided in code, but by nobody's report: gen20k/design.py:45-56 makes Q = ALL strict-adjacent pairs of the cell (candidates = the non-adjacent pairs), not the plan's ceil(0.2 n_pairs) hash subset. This is better than gen15 (Q no longer depends on which pairs a policy chose) and it makes Pr/Nd automatically a member of Q, but it is a deviation from the only written contract and it makes every gen15/gen16 measured-mode number non-comparable (their Q is 'all pairs minus supports'). Action: record the deviation in a sealed plan before the first run, and keep the gen13-definition variant (`adjacent_gen13`) as the declared sensitivity. tests/test_leakage.py:70 already asserts the query is fixed and never contains a support; add an explicit test that the Q of a given cell is byte-identical across k, arm and policy.

gaps.question: Is Pr/Nd measurable in this cohort, and with what spread (kshot_existing lists this as unverified)?
gaps.answer_or_check: Answered by data_target and independently by gen20 AUDIT.md A.3: Pr/Nd is measured in 172 cells over 71 extractants, 35 chemotypes and 38 publications, with heavier-minus-lighter mean +0.107 and sd 0.234 (one of the better-covered adjacent types). So a Q_PrNd endpoint is feasible on the gen13 cohort. Caveat for anyone tempted to use gen19 instead: its V5-PAIR selection and confirmation halves contain zero Pr/Nd cell pairs.

gaps.question: What exactly is 'common-query vs remaining-query' evaluation, and how is the k-ladder kept from confounding k with cohort shrinkage?
gaps.answer_or_check: Nobody defined it. The numbers to build it on are in gen20 AUDIT.md A.3: eligibility under the no-closure rule at k = 0/1/2/3/5/8/10 is 378/331/302/275/196/120/114 cells, 82/82/82/81/74/51/50 extractants, 40/40/40/39/34/26/25 chemotypes, 45/44/42/40/36/25/25 publications and 2114/2067/2032/1980/1730/1337/1297 adjacent query pairs. Action: define 'common' as the k=10-eligible intersection (114 cells / 50 extractants / 25 chemotypes) and report every rung twice - on the common set (so the ladder is one population) and on each k's own eligible set (so coverage is not hidden) - with the units lost at each k printed, as plan:234-236 requires.

gaps.question: Is there a leakage-injection test, and what does it cover?
gaps.answer_or_check: Yes, and no report mentions it: generations/gen20_kshot/tests/test_leakage_injection.py has 7 tests - test cell injected into training, publication crossing, support present in the query, redundant (arithmetically closed) support, held-out residual inside the covariance, unmasked inner training, and a target-derived feature. tests/test_leakage.py adds 14 more including test_no_query_pair_is_arithmetically_determined (:80), test_covariance_is_psd_and_noise_from_training_replicates (:134), test_support_draws_and_fold_plan_reproduce_in_a_subprocess (:144), test_orientation_and_antisymmetry (:169), test_r2_undefined_cases_and_direction_tie_rule (:200) and test_cohort_matches_frozen_manifest (:210). Missing against plan:§12: a resume/COMPLETE-status test and a 'same Q at every k' test.

gaps.question: What is the deciding statistic for the new endpoints, given the chemotype percentile bootstrap over-rejects (0.071-0.0815 at nominal 0.05) and nobody adopted the wild cluster bootstrap?
gaps.answer_or_check: Unresolved and must be fixed before the run. gen13sep/wildcluster.py (WCR with CR2/CR3, Bell-McCaffrey dof, test-inversion CIs) and gen16_protocol/gen16/clusterboot.py already exist and hold 0.041-0.053 size; gen16 and gen19 kept the percentile+BCa bootstrap for continuity. Check gen20k/inference.py and gen20k/bootstrap.py for which one is wired and whether mde_80 is emitted, then declare one deciding p plus the other as a printed sensitivity. Note WCR does not apply directly to an R2 difference: for R2 use a cluster bootstrap that recomputes the denominator per resample, vectorised through per-cluster sums of w, w*y, w*y^2 and w*e^2.

gaps.question: Is the study sealed, and is anything run?
gaps.answer_or_check: No and no. generations/gen20_kshot has no PRE_REGISTRATION.md, no protocol.json, no manifests/prereg_sha256.txt, no confirmation-seed commitment and no .gitignore; manifests/, predictions/ and results/ are empty directories. The precedents to copy are gen16 (scripts/g16_prereg_hash.py --seal, public seed rule, CONFIRMATION_RUN_ONCE.json) and gen19 (scripts/g19_seal_prereg.py with readiness gates, secrets-drawn seed store outside the repository, digest registry). Seal before the first fit or none of the k-ladder numbers can be called confirmatory.

gaps.question: What is the minimum detectable effect for the new primary endpoint, on the population the study actually scores?
gaps.answer_or_check: Nobody computed it. The scoring population at k >= 3 is 81 extractants in 39 chemotypes (A.3), with sc009 holding 23 of them; Kish n_eff is 10.07 and Bell-McCaffrey dof 9.57 on the comparable 40-chemotype profile, and gen16's detectability table puts the detectable between-chemotype R2 at 0.196 (1 predictor) even at the reliability-weighted n_eff of 34.26. Action: emit mde_80 (2.80 x bootstrap sd, inference.py:95-105) for every registered contrast before looking at any score, and state plainly which gates cannot open at their own margin - gen16's L2 gate had an MDE of 0.039 against a 0.02 margin.

gaps.question: Does BP need a copy-group-aware variant, and is the 45-cell cross-publication copy exposure real at row level?

Still unanswered from splits_leakage: how many of those 45 cells are literal value copies of a gen13 training cell (run gen19's cross_publication_copies restricted to the 5,992 bundle rows, |delta log D| <= 0.005) - group membership alone overstates the exposure.

gaps.question: Which Setting B arm is the registered null, and is Setting B claim-bearing?
gaps.answer_or_check: setting_b's recommendation has been adopted in code: gen20k/setting_b.py declares Setting B exploratory with COPY as the null, on 23 non-duplicate units / 17 extractants / 11 chemotypes. The outstanding decision is whether the support cell's adjacent pairs are revealed (making COPY the exact trivial predictor) or only its non-adjacent pairs (changing the null to a within-cell line fit); the module as written reveals all pairs of the support cell, so COPY is defined for every query and must be beaten, not merely reported beside.

top_risks.risk: The primary endpoint sits inside the measurement noise floor, so a win can be arithmetic or covariance bookkeeping rather than chemistry.
top_risks.why: Adjacent log SF has sd 0.231 and mean |y| 0.167 (FLAT MAE 0.167 strict-adjacent), while the per-(cell, metal) replicate sd is 0.302 and the propagated sd of an adjacent pair with both metals replicated has median 0.556 (163 pairs). On the gen15 BP board the whole measured-mode adjacent ladder runs 0.199 -> 0.139, and at D-optimal k=3 the entire ligand corpus is worth 0.006 (G14 0.170039 vs FLAT 0.175665 all-pairs; 0.139 vs 0.145 adjacent). Every k=1 'chemistry helps' contrast in gen13/gen15/gen16 is null (G14-NAIVE_LINE +0.008, p=0.354; G14-FLAT +0.002, p=0.723), and gen4 already found model = pair-mean lookup from k ~ 2.
top_risks.mitigation: Register FLAT, NAIVE_LINE (and COPY for Setting B) as nulls at EVERY k on identical supports, not only at k=0; print the replicate floor beside every adjacent number; keep all-pairs and far-pairs as co-primary so the headline is not decided inside the floor; and report the arithmetically-determined fraction separately - gen20k/design.py already keeps the support set a forest and tests/test_leakage.py:80 asserts no query pair is closed, which is the one defence gen15 never had.

top_risks.risk: Outer-fold selection plus an over-rejecting bootstrap on an effectively tiny number of independent units.
top_risks.why: The incumbents the study compares against were themselves chosen on the outer folds of the same five discovery seeds (gen14's LOGIT_TOPO39 from a 30-candidate sweep scored under all five designs including BP; gen15's D-optimal policy and covariance kind from outer sweeps), and only gen16's L3a claim was ever re-estimated on withheld seeds. The deciding chemotype percentile bootstrap rejects at 0.071-0.077 on the 45-chemotype profile and 0.0705-0.0815 on the 40-chemotype one, against 0.041-0.053 for WCR/CR3-t. The scored population at k>=3 is 81 extractants in 39 chemotypes with Kish n_eff ~10 and one chemotype holding 23 extractants.
top_risks.mitigation: Seal the protocol (gen16/gen19 pattern) before the first fit; select every free choice (covariance estimator, policy, adapter, neural hyperparameters) on inner cross-fits or a declared selection half, never on outer scores; commit confirmation seeds and spend them once; register WCR or CR3-t on Bell-McCaffrey dof as the deciding p with the percentile p printed for continuity; emit mde_80 before looking.

top_risks.risk: The k-ladder confounds the budget with the cohort, and the high-k rungs are a diglycolamide statement.
top_risks.why: Eligibility collapses along the ladder: 378 cells / 82 extractants / 40 chemotypes at k=0 down to 120/51/26 at k=8 and 114/50/25 at k=10 (gen20 AUDIT.md A.3). Of the 116 cells with >= 11 metals, 52 are sc009 and 30 are TODGA alone; sc009 holds 375 of 521 cells and 53.6 % of adjacent pairs, and under BP the sc009 fold trains on 76 cells. A ladder read down its own column therefore mixes 'more measurements help' with 'the surviving cells are easier and narrower'.
top_risks.mitigation: Report every rung on the k=10-common subset as well as on its own eligible set, publish the cells/extractants/chemotypes/publications lost at each k, make extractant-macro and chemotype-macro the headline aggregations, cap or stratify sc009, and show the sc009-held-out fold separately. Treat k <= 3 as the headline and k = 5/8/10 as declared sensitivities.

top_risks.risk: Cross-set and cross-generation quoting: four mutually incomparable scoring sets now exist and the two generations disagree on orientation.
top_risks.why: gen15 section 4 (widest-only exclusion), section 5 (union of three strategies, 57,638 pairs under BP), section 7 (training-fold covariance) and gen16 L5 (52,662 pairs) already give different numbers for the same arm - the programme has made this mistake twice, and the k=0 score alone moves 0.4387 / 0.4395 / 0.4597 across strategies in a sweep where k=0 uses no measurement. gen20's Q is a fifth set (strict-adjacent only). On top of that gen13/gen14/gen15 orient pairs lighter-first while gen19 orients heavier-first, so any signed quantity flips, and gen13 scores a zero prediction as wrong while gen20k/metrics.py scores it 0.5.
top_risks.mitigation: Fix one scoring set and one orientation before any value is revealed and assert both in code (gen20k already has tests/test_leakage.py:169 for orientation/antisymmetry); print n_rows, n_cells, n_extractants and n_chemotypes beside every number; re-run the incumbents (G14, FLAT, NAIVE_LINE, gen15 BLUP) on gen20's own Q rather than importing their published values; never join a gen19 table to a gen13 one.

top_risks.risk: The neural arm has far less effective ligand-side design than it appears, and multi-seed ensembles invite a false positive.
top_risks.why: The 39 TOPO39 columns take only 28 distinct values over 521 cells and 22 over the 289 rich cells, so the ligand design is ~22 points, not 90 extractants; Kish n_eff over chemotypes is ~12. Under BP the sc009 fold trains on 76 cells (gen20 AUDIT.md A.3), and gen20 measures the neural head's training cost at 0.4 s per fold, so nothing stops a large arm grid being run - the constraint is statistical, not computational, and the audit says so explicitly. The reference repository's own learning curve saturates by ~46 extractants and its four 3D encoders have effective rank 1.05 of 8.
top_risks.mitigation: Declare the neural arm's seeds, ensemble size and inner-selection criterion before running (gen20k/nnc.py already fixes 8 seeds and an inner adjacent-MAE criterion); pair it with a ligand-feature-free refuter and with the tree arm on identical supports; power the contrast and state the MDE; treat HEAD_FT/FULL_FT as documented over-fitting checks selected on inner folds only, as the module's own docstring says.
